chapters.title: Chapter 2601 Gaia’s Heaven
paragraphs: "Let me get this straight..."
After a moment of silence, Mei Feng spoke with a dumbfounded look on her face.
"The reason you want to go outside the city alone is so that you can clean up the Void Specters? Do you really expect me to believe that? I cannot see its purpose or how it benefits you."
"Well, to put things plainly, I get stronger through defeating these Void Specters," Yuan revealed the truth to her without revealing too many details.

Mei Feng raised an eyebrow at his statement and replied, "This is the first time I've heard such a thing. We've been cleaning Void Specters for generations, but nobody has ever gotten stronger from doing so. There's a reason why they're considered trash, you know?"
"One man's trash is another's treasure," Yuan responded with a smile on his face. "Also, in case you forgot, I am not from this world, so things work differently for me."

Mei Feng rubbed her eyes and sighed, "Regardless, I cannot allow you to leave the city alone, especially when you are still a mere Corporal. I have already given you too many exemptions. As much as I want to support you, I am a General, and I cannot give you too much favoritism. If you want to go outside alone, then keep on doing missions, build up your reputation, and increase your rank."
"How long does it usually take to be promoted to Sergeant?" Yuan asked.

"There's no set amount of time," she replied. "Most soldiers never advance beyond Corporal, since Sergeants are considered elite. To become one, you'll need to accumulate enough achievements and merit by completing missions. But if you want an example, then the quickest anyone has ever been promoted to the rank of Sergeant from Corporal is three years."
"Three years, huh?" Yuan mumbled, relieved that it wasn't too ridiculously long.
"Then how do I go about joining cleanup missions without coming to you? I don't want to bother you too often, after all."
"Just go to the mission hall. You can ask about missions and even request them there."
"Alright. Thanks."
"From now on, unless you really need my assistance, refrain from coming here. I can't have a Corporal coming to me for every little issue," she said a moment later.
"I understand."
Yuan left shortly after.
"Well? What did the General say? Can you go outside by yourself?" Sergeant Bing asked.
"No. She said it's too early—that I should do more missions and increase my rank before she reconsiders it."
"That's to be expected," said Sergeant Quang. "Not only did you just join the military, but you're just a Corporal. Hell, not even Sergeants are allowed to leave the city alone."
"Where is the mission hall?" Yuan then asked.
"We'll take you there."
Some time later, Yuan arrived at the mission hall.
"There are a lot of people here," Yuan remarked after entering the building to see thousands of soldiers present.
"If a soldier isn't resting or training, they will be here to look for missions."
"How does this place work?" Yuan asked.

"You see those capsules over there?" Sergeant Bing pointed at the rows of machines at the end of the room where most of the soldiers in this place were gathered, most of them seemingly waiting for their turn.
"Once you enter the capsule, you can see all of the missions that are available to you, or request to join others' missions."
"What sort of missions are typically available?"
"That depends on your rank, but as a Corporal, you should have a good number of them unlocked."
"Alright."
Yuan went to queue up for the machine shortly after.
While he waited, Yuan looked around and noticed that the majority of soldiers present were ranked between Private First Class and Corporal.
"Hey, isn't that the guy who fought a Captain during the recent recruitment?"
"You're right! And look at his insignia! He's already a Corporal!"
It didn't take long before some of the soldiers there noticed and recognized Yuan.
"That's the guy who broke all of the previous records? He doesn't look that capable."
Eventually, a few of them approached Yuan and asked him, "Which family are you from?"
"I don't have one," Yuan calmly replied.
"What? Surely, you must be joking."
"What makes you think that?" Yuan asked.
"There's no way you could've broken all of those records without the help of your family!"
Yuan shrugged. "Then I don't know what else to tell you."
"He obviously wants to keep it a secret, just like the Ironwoman."
"Right? I bet he comes from the same background as that woman."
"What if he's that woman's brother?"
"Is that true? Are you the Ironwoman's brother?"
Since he had nothing to do in line, Yuan decided to chat with these soldiers, even though most of them were just questioning his background.
Eventually, it was his turn to use the machine.
Once inside, a notification appeared.
<Welcome to the Mission Board, Corporal Yuan>
"Let me see what mission is available to me."
<Checking the user's credentials>
<You are allowed to accept missions up to the rank of Sergeant>
<Listing all available missions in 3...2...1...>
A moment later, a list of missions appeared before Yuan.
"There are a lot fewer missions than I anticipated..." Yuan mumbled after seeing only about thirty or so missions available.
[Mission: Gather Unknown Ore in the Orange Zone]
"Unknown Ore? What is that?"
He checked the mission details.
[Mission Details: Enter the Orange Zone and gather Unknown Ores]
[Rank Requirement: Corporal]
[Squad Requirement: 4]
However, there was no information on the Unknown Ores.
With no other choice, he decided to ask the others later and proceeded to check the other missions.
[Mission: Gather Unknown Crystal in the Red Zone]
[Rank Requirement: Sergeant]
[Squad Requirement: 6]
"Unknown Crystal?"

There were several other missions that required him to venture outside to gather items that he had no information on. Other than that, the rest of the missions were miscellaneous things such as acting as a guard for individuals within the city.
"Huh?"
Yuan's eyes widened with surprise when he noticed a certain mission.
[Mission: Escort individual to Spirit City]
[Rank Requirement: Sergeant]
[Squad Requirement: 4]
"Spirit... City? There are other cities in this world?"
This was the first time Yuan had heard of such a thing. In fact, he'd thought this was the only city in the world.
After taking a moment to digest this new information, Yuan went to look for the cleanup mission.
Although there were other missions that allowed him to venture outside the city, his main purpose was to kill Void Specters.
However, he couldn't see the cleanup mission on the list of available missions.
"Where are the cleanup missions?" he asked.
<Cleanup missions are automatically assigned to soldiers>
"Then how do I join one?"
<You may request to join a squad with that mission>
"Then send a request for me."
<What time frame?>
"The sooner the better."
<Request has been sent>
<Request has been approved>
"That was quick."
Yuan remarked, as the request was basically instantly approved.
[Mission Details: Cleanup Void Specters up to the Orange Zone. Meet at the Southern Gate at 0600 in 12 hours]
"Tomorrow, huh? That's great."
Yuan exited the machine shortly after.
"When's your next mission?" Sergeant Bing asked when Yuan returned to them.
"Tomorrow."
"That fast, huh?"
As they made their way back to the residential area, Yuan asked, "What are Unknown Ores and Unknown Crystals?"
"They are important resources that can only be found in the Orange Zone and beyond. There are multiple uses for them, such as crafting weapons and Gaia Stones."
"Is that so..." Yuan mumbled, wondering if they were anything like Spirit Stones or treasures in his world.
"Even if you aren't on a mission to gather them, you should pick them up if you come across them, as you can exchange them for merits and money," Sergeant Quang said.
"What do they look like?"
"You'll know when you see one. You won't miss them, either." Sergeant Bing replied. "They stick out like a sore thumb against the barren landscape with their glistening appearance."
"Unknown Ore or Unknown Crystal?"
"Both. Unknown Ores are much more common, though."
"I'll keep that in mind." Yuan nodded.
"Also, am I right in assuming there are other cities besides this one? I saw a mission to escort someone to Spirit City. Is that a separate city, or just a place within this one?"
Sergeant Bing and Sergeant Quang looked at him with one eyebrow raised, looking confused by his question.
"You mean... you didn't know there were other cities out there?" Sergeant Bing eventually spoke.
"...No," Yuan answered truthfully.
"Well, do I have news for you."
Sergeant Quang chuckled. "There are eight other cities besides this one, so there are nine cities in total."
Sergeant Bing added, "Our city is called Gaia's Heaven. We are also the largest city out there."
"I'll be damned..." Yuan muttered in a somewhat dazed tone.

chapters.title: Chapter 2602 Third Mission
paragraphs: "How does one get to the other cities?" Yuan asked after taking a moment to digest the new information.

"There is a portal that can teleport between all of the cities. However, there is only one such portal, and it is heavily regulated by the military. Unless you're from an influential or wealthy family, it's nearly impossible to use it due to how much energy it consumes," Sergeant Quang explained.

"In other words, if you want to travel to another city, you'll need to go there on foot... or drive there, which requires you to go through the Black Zone," Sergeant Bing continued. "But honestly, I don't see a point in traveling to another city, especially given how dangerous it can be. We already have everything one can ask for in this city, too."
"Are you trying to travel to another city?" Sergeant Quang asked out of curiosity.
Yuan quickly shook his head.
"No, I was just unaware of their existence until just now. I have no reason or intention of going to another city for now."
"For now, huh?"
"Well, it's not like I can predict the future."
Yuan continued, asking, "What is in the other cities, anyway? How do they differ from this one?"
"I've never been to another city, so I cannot tell you."
"Have you never encountered someone from a different city?"
"Nope. As mentioned earlier, only those incredibly influential and wealthy would travel between cities."
"What about missions? I saw one earlier that involved escorting someone to Spirit City."

Sergeant Bing shook her head. "Just because a mission is available doesn't mean you qualify for it. Those missions offer the most merit, but they also have the strictest rules and highest requirements. Everyone must undergo a rigorous screening process before they're even allowed to partake in it, and tens of thousands of soldiers apply each time."
"The most merits, huh? So I should apply for these missions if I want to improve my rank the quickest," Yuan mumbled.

"In theory, yes. However, whether you'll be accepted or not is an entirely different story. Moreover, they don't just look at your capabilities. Even if you're more than qualified to take the mission, the subject of the mission has the final say, so if they don't like you, they can still disqualify you."
"What a pain in the ass."

"That's why I don't even bother applying for those missions," Sergeant Bing sighed. "Still, if you want to advance beyond Sergeant, taking part in them is almost a necessity. They give you the chance to build connections with influential and powerful people who may be able to help with your promotion."
"I'll keep that in mind."
Once they reached the residential area, Yuan asked them before heading into his living quarters, "You're not coming with me tomorrow, right?
Sergeant Quang replied, "After seeing what you're capable of during the last mission, I no longer have a reason to be concerned."
"It was quite entertaining, and I wouldn't mind accompanying you again, but I am a bit behind my training schedule," Sergeant Bing said.
"Alright. Then I won't wait for you guys tomorrow. See you later."
"Stay safe."
The next day, Yuan showed up to the rendezvous at the Southern Gate in the morning at 0600. Of course, he brought along his minigun.
The other soldiers stared at Yuan with bewildered expressions, almost as if they couldn't believe what they were seeing.
"A Corporal...?"
"With a minigun...?"
"Are you pranking us?"
Yuan replied with a calm smile, "I can assure you that I am not messing around. In fact, I will even do all of the cleaning alone, so you just need to follow me and try to keep up."
"What are you even talking about...?"
"Squad leader, he's clearly fucking with us. Let's just leave him behind and go."
"Unfortunately, his name is on the list, and we cannot leave without him. It's also too late to remove him," sighed the squad leader.
"Whether I am messing with you or not will be clear once we leave the city walls," Yuan said.
"Whatever... Just don't get in our way."
They teleported to the top of the city walls shortly afterward.
The moment they jumped down the city walls and landed on the ground, Yuan started flying forward.
"Try to keep up!" he said to them.
"T-This guy! He's running off on his own!
"Just forget about him. We're already outside the city, anyway."
"Even if you say that... I don't want to make a report because we let him go and die off on his own."
"...Fuck."
With no other choice, the soldiers quickly chased after Yuan.
"Fuck! How fast is this guy moving?!"
Even after chasing for hours, they still couldn't catch up to Yuan, almost as if he'd vanished entirely.
"What if he's already dead?"
"Wait! I see him!"

They caught up to Yuan because he'd come to a stop, arriving just in time to watch him gun down the Void Specters before him with his minigun. However, since there were just a few of them, none of the soldiers were impressed.
If anything, they were annoyed at him for running ahead.
"H-Hey! He's running off again!"
Before any of them could even approach Yuan, he sped off immediately after defeating the Void Specters.
"Don't tell me he actually plans on dealing with all of the Void Specters by himself?!"
"Did you not see that big ass minigun he was carrying? There's no way he'll last longer than a day if he fights alone!"
"Not just that, but he's only at the Fifth Ascension. I doubt he'll last for even half a day."
"Damn it... Where did such a reckless idiot come from? I knew something was weird when someone willingly joined us for our cleanup mission!"
However, an entire day passed, and Yuan continued eliminating the Void Specters on his own without any trouble or slowing down.
"What is going on?! How is he still going?! He should've exhausted himself long ago!"
The soldiers following behind were left baffled by Yuan's abnormal performance.

chapters.title: Chapter 2603 Cleaning Maniac
paragraphs: Two days have passed since Yuan left the city and started cleaning up the Void Specters alone. The soldiers on the same mission and following behind had expected him to exhaust himself by the end of the first day. Yet, he showed no sign of slowing down even after two whole days.
"This doesn't make any sense! How is he still going after two days without rest?!"
"I haven't seen him take even a sip of stamina potion, either."
"Who'd be stupid enough to use potions for this sort of mission, anyway? Those things are incredibly expensive."
"If he continues cleaning at this rate, we'll be done by tomorrow, and these missions usually take at least a week."

Unbeknownst to these soldiers, Yuan had no intention of stopping the mission until they verbally asked him to stop. This meant that he continued cleaning past the Green Zone and into the Orange Zone, something most, if not all, soldiers refrain from doing.
After all, the mission only asked them to clean the Green Zone, and going above and beyond yielded no bonus merit. Unless there was something to gain, most would not even consider it.
"Hey... Aren't we past the Green Zone already?"
Eventually, one of the soldiers realized this and asked aloud.
"You're right! Then why isn't he stopping?"
"Maybe he doesn't know?"
"Damn it!"

"Hey, Corporal! Stop! We've already gone past the Green Zone! There's no need to keep on going because the mission is already complete!" The squad leader shouted at Yuan, who was just preparing to speed off again.
Yuan stopped and turned to face them.
"I am aware, but I want to keep on cleaning," he said calmly.
"What? Why?"
"Just because," he shrugged.
"Are you insane? There's literally no point. We're heading back," said one of the soldiers.
"Alright." Yuan didn't even try to argue.

Since completing missions faster meant earning merit more quickly, Yuan had no objections to returning to the city, as it still moved him closer to his goals. Of course, that didn't mean he wouldn't try to extend the mission again during future assignments.
"Hey, how are you not tired after shooting that thing for days without rest? Even I can't last longer than a few hours, and there's no way you have more Limitless than me."
"You won't be able to replicate it even if I told you," Yuan replied.
"And what makes you so sure?"
"I just am," he said, refusing to elaborate further.
After returning to the military base, Yuan immediately went back to the mission hall to grab another cleanup mission, repeating the process again and again.

In the blink of an eye, an entire month passed. During that time, Yuan participated in every cleanup mission he could, completing seven in total. He even managed to convince one of his squads to let him spend several days clearing Void Specters in the Orange Zone.
His highly unusual behavior quickly drew attention, and it wasn't long before his name spread throughout the military, earning him the nickname "Cleaning Maniac."
"Have you heard? Some Corporal with a minigun has been going around volunteering for every cleanup mission he could."
"Someone is actually willingly doing those missions? Why?"
"Who knows? But from what I've heard, he does all of the cleaning alone while the rest of his squad just quietly follows behind."
"What? That sounds amazing! Where was he during my cleanup mission two months ago?"
"Apparently, he joined the military only a month ago."
"Huh? And he's already a Corporal?"
"Because he's also the prodigy who broke every record during the last recruitment."
"That's the same person? What the hell is someone like him doing wasting his time on such pointless missions? If he wants to earn merit, there are plenty of other missions that offer far more!
"You can never tell what a genius is thinking—especially one of his caliber."
It wasn't just the ordinary soldiers who were baffled by Yuan's actions, as even General Gu and the officers on his side were greatly puzzled by it.
"What the hell is going on? Why is he doing this?"
"What if it's actually General Mei's orders?"
"That makes even less sense! Why would General Mei recruit someone like that just to keep sending him on cleanup missions? What a waste of his potential!"
"Regardless of his reason for doing it, isn't this a good opportunity to get rid of him before he becomes too troublesome?" Someone suddenly said.
"You want to get rid of him while he is outside the city, where there is no surveillance?"
"That's right."
"It's not like there is zero surveillance. Have you forgotten about Gaia's System? It can tell if a soldier has purposefully killed another soldier."
"We can just use a scapegoat."
As the officers openly discussed killing Yuan, General Gu remained silent, listening without interruption.

Eventually, he spoke. "There's no need for a scapegoat. According to those who've gone on missions with him, he always asks to venture farther than necessary—even into the Orange Zone. We can simply take advantage of that and let him go as far as he wants. The further he goes, the higher the chance an accident will occur. There is virtually no risk for our soldiers either since he also willingly does the cleanup alone."

"The only problem is that we have to wait for him to be assigned to one of our squads," one of the officers said. "That could take months—or even years if we're unlucky—and there's no telling how long he'll keep up this charade."
"I can handle that," another replied. "I'll be responsible for assigning cleanup missions next month. Still, to avoid making it too obvious, we'll need to wait at least two months."
"Then we'll leave it in your hands, Captain Huang."

Meanwhile, Yuan continued taking on cleanup missions, completely unaware that he had already become the target of a conspiracy. Of course, even if he knew, he wouldn't care. If anything, he'd probably welcome it.

chapters.title: Chapter 2604 Unknown Ore
paragraphs: "General Mei, are you making Corporal Yuan partake in the cleanup missions nonstop?" one of her officers asked during a meeting.
"What sort of question is that? Why would you think that?" she asked with a puzzled face.
"That's just what the others have been saying."
"I've also been hearing it," another replied. "They claimed that you're trying to assert dominance over the new recruit by forcing him to do these missions over and over again."
"How stupid." Mei Feng sneered in disdain at such outrageous claims. "Why would I even need to assert any dominance? It's not like he's being disobedient."

"So it's true that he's willingly doing these cleanup missions himself? Why? While I am happy to see a soldier finally eager to do something that everyone else finds a chore, it's a little concerning how eager he is..."
"Right? It's literally all he does. Mission after mission. Without rest. It's like he's possessed or something."
"General, shouldn't we assign him something more fitting for someone called the upcoming Ironman?" someone suddenly suggested.
"Why?"
"I mean... we'll become a laughingstock if someone so talented keeps on doing these cleanup missions..."

"Let them laugh. In case you forgot, Corporal Yuan joined just a little over a month ago. Do you remember what you were doing during your first year, let alone the first few months? Give him some time to adapt and familiarize himself with his new surroundings, and if he wants to spend all of his time doing cleanup missions, let him. It's not like he's harming anyone."
"I agree with General Mei. We should give him some time... at least until those who joined at the same time as him finish their training."
"So a year, huh? Fair enough."
Meanwhile, Yuan began his second month of cleanup missions.

As his name and reputation continued to spread, more and more soldiers were willing to let Yuan spend some time in the Orange Zone cleaning up Void Specters, which extended his time outside the city but at the cost of completing missions more slowly.
Time continued to pass swiftly, and in the blink of an eye, it was the start of Yuan's third month in the military.
However, instead of going on a new cleanup mission after completing his last, Yuan went to the training area to see how much closer he got to defeating the enemy on the 46th floor.
"Foolish mortal..."
After several intense rounds later, Yuan sighed in defeat.
"I knew it wasn't much, but I didn't think two months of absorbing the Void Specters' Eternal Essence would only help me last a few seconds longer..."
At this rate, he'd need to keep on doing cleanup missions for decades to have any noticeable results.
"This won't do. I will need to head further into the Red Zone, if not even deeper. However, I doubt they'll agree to let me venture so far away from the city so soon..."

He considered doing the gathering missions that would allow him to enter the Red Zones, but upon asking Sergeant Bing about it, he learned that attacking Void Specters during such missions was highly frowned upon since it was unnecessarily risky for everyone involved.

"Guess I'll give it another month and ask Mei Feng if I can go outside alone again. My reputation has risen quite significantly, and pretty much everyone is aware that I can handle the cleanup missions alone without issue."
With that in mind, Yuan started doing cleanup missions again.
"So, just to be clear, we won't be doing anything but following you, right?" asked the squad leader.
"That is indeed correct," Yuan confirmed.
"I've heard a lot about you, Corporal Yuan. If you don't mind me asking, is there a reason you prefer cleaning alone? I don't want to feel like we're taking advantage of you."
Yuan smiled and said, "Don't worry, I am doing this of my own accord, and the reason I prefer doing it alone is simply that it's much more efficient and faster."

Although the soldiers didn't agree with Yuan's statement, none of them complained because Yuan was going to do all of the work alone. After all, how could a single person clean more efficiently than a whole group of people?
Eventually, they reached the Orange Zone.
"You mind if we spend a few days in the Orange Zone? I want to continue cleaning."
"Only if you tell us why you're so obsessed with cleaning."
"Sure. It's nothing crazy," Yuan said before giving them the same explanation he'd told everyone else. "Cleaning Void Specters is soothing for me. It's kind of like therapy.
"Like therapy?" The soldiers raised their eyebrows, looking puzzled by his unexpected response.
Despite their curiosity, none of them dared to question Yuan further, as they did not want to be disrespectful.
However, inside their minds, they wondered if Yuan's parents were soldiers who died to Void Specters, hence his hatred and obsession to clean them.
"A-Alright... If you want to enter the Orange Zone, go ahead..."
"Thanks."
A few days into cleaning in the Orange Zone, just as they were prepared to return to the city, Yuan noticed something that stopped him in his tracks.
"Hm?"
Not far away, something glinted in the distance.
"Is that what I think it is?" Yuan muttered as he walked toward it.
A few moments later, he bent down and picked up the object—a fist-sized, glistening stone.
"Oh? You found an Unknown Ore? How lucky."
"So this is an Unknown Ore, huh? This is my first time seeing one," he said.
"They're usually much further into the Orange Zone, so it's pretty rare to find them in this area."
Yuan examined the Unknown Ore as they made their way back to the city.
'This thing... it contains Eternal Essence!' Yuan's eyes widened slightly after realizing this.
'And it's not a small amount!'
The Unknown Ore in his hand contained enough Eternal Essence to rival that of a thousand Void Specters—roughly the number he usually wipes out during a single cleanup mission.

chapters.title: Chapter 2605 Unknown Ore(2)
paragraphs: When they returned to the military base, one of the soldiers asked Yuan, "Corporal, how long do you think you'll continue doing these missions? I know you're new to the military, but surely you won't be doing this for the rest of your career, right?"
Yuan chuckled, "Of course not. I will stop doing these missions when I feel like I have done enough, which might be sooner than I originally anticipated."
"Is that so? In any case, good luck, and thanks for doing the mission for us."
"It's been my pleasure."
After going their separate ways, Yuan made his way back to the residential area instead of the mission hall.
When he arrived, he saw Sergeant Quang coming out of his room.
"Oh? I was about to head to the mission hall to find you," Sergeant Quang remarked.

Although Sergeant Quang and Sergeant Bing were still acting as Yuan's bodyguard on base, they were no longer as strict and constantly following him around like watchdogs. Moreover, rather than both of them following Yuan simultaneously, they took turns, which was suggested by Yuan himself, allowing them to have more time to themselves.
"Look what I found." Yuan retrieved the Unknown Ore he had discovered during the mission and showed it to Sergeant Quang.
"How far into the Orange Zone did you go to find that?"
Instead of celebrating Yuan's find, Sergeant Quang looked concerned. The presence of an Unknown Ore suggested Yuan had ventured deep into the Orange Zone.
"Not far at all. In fact, I ventured less than I usually do. According to the soldiers with me, I was just incredibly lucky."
"In that case, they're right. Unknown Ore is rarely found near the outskirts of the Orange Zone because we patrol those areas so frequently."
"How do they even come into existence?" Yuan suddenly asked.
"Honestly, I don't know, but most people just consider it nature's gift."
"I see..."
"Anyway, since you have an Unknown Ore, I guess you'll want to turn it in for merit and money? I'll bring you to the distribution center."
"Actually, before we do that, I have a few questions. Do they do anything special to the Unknown Ore when you turn it in? For example, will they examine it?

Sergeant Quang raised an eyebrow at Yuan's strange question and pondered for a moment before responding, "Not that I know of. What is there to examine, anyway? Do you think people hand in fake Unknown Ores or something? These ores are impossible to fake—not that anyone would be stupid enough to do something like that in the first place since it's a serious crime."
Yuan fell silent for a moment.
Then, without a word, silently absorbed all of the Eternal Essence in the Unknown Ore.
After absorbing all of its Eternal Essence, Yuan examined the Unknown Ore for any changes.
"There's no change!" Yuan's eyes widened.
To his surprise, the Unknown Ore showed no discernible change in its appearance even after losing all of its Eternal Essence.
He looked at Sergeant Quang and showed him the Unknown Ore again.
"Notice anything different?" he asked.
"No...?" Sergeant Quang answered, sounding uncertain, as he wondered if Yuan was asking him some kind of trick question.
"Take a closer look." Yuan insisted, even handing the entire Unknown Ore to him.

After taking a good moment to examine the Unknown Ore, Sergeant Quang looked at Yuan and asked, "Are you messing with me or something? Are you going to tell me that this isn't an Unknown Ore but something else entirely?"
"Yes, I was just messing with you." Yuan chuckled as he retrieved the Unknown Ore. "But it's really an Unknown Ore."
"Anyway, can you take me to the distribution center now?
"Sure..." Sergeant Quang sensed that something was off about Yuan, but he couldn't quite put his finger on it.
Some time later, they arrived at the distribution center, and Yuan went to hand over the Unknown Ore despite having already absorbed all of its Eternal Essence.
'Even if they realize something is wrong with it, I can just say that I found it in that condition, and they have no prove that I'd done anything to it...' Yuan chuckled inwardly.

Despite his questionable actions, Yuan didn't mind all that much. It was only a single Unknown Ore, and while he still wasn't certain whether this was a real world or merely an illusion, he leaned toward it being the latter, so he figured he might as well do a few unethical things.
"One Unknown Ore, correct? Please place your hand on the machine, so I can credit you for your merits."
The worker accepted the Unknown Ore after a mere glance at it and gestured toward the machine before Yuan.
<You have received some merits>
<You have received 1,000 Gaia Credits>
After receiving the reward, Yuan calmly walked away, acting completely innocent with nothing to hide.
'So the money is distributed and used through the system too, huh?' Yuan thought to himself after realizing that this was his first contact with this world's currency.

'And since they seem to have no clue that I'd already absorbed the energy inside the Unknown Ore... I might as well stop doing cleanup missions and start going on the ones that focus on gathering them!'
However, just to be sure they didn't notice the Unknown Ore's drained Eternal Essence and couldn't track him for it, Yuan continued doing cleanup missions for another two weeks.
"Did you hear? The Cleaning Maniac has finally stopped doing cleanup missions!"
"No. Where did you hear that?"
"From my buddies who are scheduled for a gathering mission for Unknown Ores. He said that Corporal Yuan is on his team."
"Oh, really? Did that weirdo finally get bored of Void Specters, or did he just realize there are better missions out there?"
The news spread quickly, eventually reaching the ears of General Gu and General Mei. One was delighted by the news, while the other was furious.

She continued, "I knew he'd eventually start taking other missions, but this is quicker than I anticipated..."

Someone then said, "It may not seem like it, but many people are eager to see what he'll accomplish, and they've been disappointed so far. Compared to the Ironwoman, who took on all kinds of dangerous missions shortly after joining, they find his performance underwhelming. Given his unprecedented talent, they expected him to follow in her footsteps."
"Can you really compare the two, though? I don't know why Corporal Yuan decided to join the military, but I doubt he has the same goal as the Ironwoman."
"Corporal Yuan has a completely different demeanor, too," Mei Feng said. "Unlike that woman, he's carefree... almost a little too carefree."
"Enough about Corporal Yuan. Any news from General Gu's side?" Someone suddenly asked.

Mei Feng replied, "I gave him a pretty stern warning, and he hasn't tried to do anything so far. However, we can never be too cautious. Keep an eye on them to make sure they don't try anything on Corporal Yuan."
"Yes, General!"
Meanwhile, on the other side, General Gu started fuming after learning about Yuan's sudden change of activities, especially when they were so close to their plan.
"That stinking brat barely managed to dodge a bullet!"

"Please calm yourself, General Gu. There's a good chance that little bastard is only trying out something new and will return to doing cleanup missions soon." One of the officers tried to reassure him.
Another then spoke, "Even if he doesn't, there are still plenty of ways to get him to join our squad for their cleanup mission."

"However, we should proceed cautiously and put our plans on hold for now," said Captain Huang, the officer responsible for assigning cleanup missions. "General Mei's people have been watching us like hawks. If we do anything suspicious, they'll seize the opportunity to ruin us."
General Gu nodded and said, "I'll leave everything to you and await good news."
"Yes, General!"
Several days later, Yuan showed up at the mission's meeting spot, and instead of meeting at the gates, they met in front of the mission hall.
"Wow! It's really him! The Cleaning Maniac!"
One of the soldiers exclaimed with excitement, almost as if they were meeting their idol.
"There's... a lot of people..." Yuan muttered, a little taken aback by how many soldiers were present.
"Is everyone here partaking in the mission?" he asked, as there were twenty-three soldiers, excluding him.
"That's right. This is your first time doing this sort of mission, correct? This number of gatherers is pretty common. In fact, there are usually more."
"What about the reward distribution? Do we all share, or are we only credited for what we find?"
"Of course, we share. This is a team effort and a mission, so we all receive a share of the total Unknown Ores."
"I see..."
"Alright, now that everyone's here, we'll split into four squads. Squad 1 will head south, Squad 2 north, Squad 3 west, and Squad 4 east."
After some management, Yuan ended up in Squad 3 with five other soldiers.
"We will meet here in two weeks. Until then, good luck with your gathering, and stay safe."
While the others went in their respective direction, Yuan's squad made their way to the western gates.
Once outside the city walls, they began rushing to the Orange Zone, ignoring all of the Void Specters they encountered.
"It must feel awkward not to clean the Void Specters, Corporal Yuan," someone in the squad remarked as they flew past the Void Specters.
"Not really," he said with a smile.
"Wait... Corporal Yuan, you just joined the military, right? And you were exempted from boot camp."
"That's right."
The soldiers in the squad suddenly stopped moving and looked at him with concerned expressions.
"What is the problem?" he asked.
"If you just joined and didn't go to boot camp... that means you didn't have the chance to learn Void Control yet, which would make this mission much more difficult and dangerous for you."
"Ah, that? Then you don't have to worry, because I can use it."
"Huh?"
The soldiers' eyes widened with surprise.

A new soldier begins training in Void Control during their first week of boot camp, but only the most gifted geniuses can use it by the time they graduate. As for everyone else, it usually takes another three to five years of training before they can wield it proficiently.
So how was Yuan, who had skipped boot camp and thrown himself into nonstop cleanup missions almost immediately after joining the military, already capable of using Void Control?
"There's no way you could've learned Void Control with such limited time..."
In order to get rid of their doubt, Yuan used Void Control directly in front of them, teleporting left and right with ease.
"My word! He can actually use it!"
"When did you learn to use it? Surely, you didn't learn it before joining the military, right?"
Yuan chuckled. "No, I learned it during the downtime between missions. It only took me a few days to grasp it."
"A few days...?"
The soldiers' eyes widened at the outrageous claim, their mouths hanging open in disbelief.
Not only were they awestruck by such an achievement, but they also felt insulted, as though their own years of effort meant nothing in the face of such overwhelming talent.
"What are you all waiting for? If we linger any longer, we'll lose to the others," Yuan said as he started moving again.
"This is not a competition..."
They shook their heads inwardly before following him.

chapters.title: Chapter 2607 Void Hunter
paragraphs: After ignoring every Void Specter they encountered, Yuan's group reached the Orange Zone in just a day. Since Unknown Ores were rarely found near its outskirts, they continued venturing deeper.
Before long, Yuan had gone farther into the Orange Zone than he ever had during any of his cleanup missions.
"Alright, let's begin our search here," the squad leader said.
"Wait. Since this is Corporal Yuan's first mission of this kind, shouldn't we explain how it works first?"

"Oh, right." The squad leader turned to Yuan. "It's quite simple. We'll form a line with some distance between each person, then advance together. If anyone spots an Unknown Ore, they let the others know so we can stop and wait for them to retrieve it."

Yuan raised an eyebrow after hearing the explanation, unable to ignore how inefficient the method seemed. However, he also understood the need for order. If everyone searched independently, it would be easy for someone to get lost.
Thus, Yuan decided to try their method first before suggesting an alternative.
Soon, they formed an orderly line, leaving several hundred miles between each person, and advanced deeper into the Orange Zone, gradually drawing closer to the Red Zone.
Shortly after they began moving, Yuan asked, "Wouldn't this method be more efficient with more people? Why did we split the group into several squads and send them in different directions?"
"Huh? You don't know about 'that'?" The soldiers turned to look at him with surprised faces.
"What is 'that'?"
"We call it the Void Hunter. It's an abnormal and mysterious being that appears when too many people are gathered in one place to hunt them."
"It's so powerful and dangerous that meeting it is essentially a death sentence. Because of this, we tend to keep our numbers as small as possible."
"Is it anything like the Void Specters?" Yuan asked.
"Yes, but it takes the form of a human being.
"And how strong is it... roughly?"
"So strong that nobody has been able to defeat it. I heard that even the strongest cultivator in history, Tian Yuchen, was completely helpless against it."

"That strong?" Yuan's eyes widened at this information, as Tian Yuchen was able to climb all the way to the 50th floor in Endless Assault. This meant that the Void Hunter was likely several times stronger than his bottleneck on the 46th floor.
However, he couldn't fathom why such a being even exists. What was its purpose? Why does it only appear when many people gather in one place?
About two hours later, Yuan sensed an Unknown Ore not far away in the distance, but it was located ahead of another soldier.
Rather than announcing his finding, Yuan waited to see how long it'd take before they noticed.
Some time later, the soldier finally noticed the Unknown Ore and said, "Found one!"
The others immediately came to a halt and waited for the soldier to retrieve the Unknown Ore using Void Control, as the place was crawling with Void Specters.
'As expected... since they cannot sense Eternal Essence, they won't be able to detect the Unknown Ores from afar and can only rely on their sight...' Yuan thought to himself.
This meant that Yuan had an immense advantage when it came to finding Unknown Ores.
As they ventured deeper into the Orange Zone, they began encountering Unknown Ores more frequently.

However, they could have found far more, as Yuan sensed numerous Unknown Ores buried beneath the ground. Unfortunately, he couldn't reveal their locations without raising questions about how he knew they were there.
Over the next several days, Yuan considered how he could collect the Unknown Ores buried underground without arousing suspicion.
An idea soon came to him, and he decided to put it to the test.
"I think I see something," Yuan called out.
When the others stopped to wait for him, Yuan used Void Manipulation to travel beyond their line of sight. Taking advantage of the opportunity, he quickly dug up several Unknown Ores.
However, in order not to go overboard, he did not dig up every Unknown Ore he sensed.
"Huh? You found three in one go?!"
The soldiers were shocked when Yuan returned with three Unknown Ores in his grasp.
Although it wasn't unheard of to find more than one Unknown Ore at once, it was incredibly rare. As for three Unknown Ores... it had only happened two times so far.
"Damn! To find three Unknown Ores in one go during his first gathering mission! What a lucky dog!"
"How lucky are we talking about?" Yuan asked.
"As far as I know, it has only happened twice before, and the last time it happened was seventy years ago."
"Oh, I am only talking about the Orange Zone," he quickly added. "It's common to find more in the Red Zone and beyond."
"Is that so? I should try going on those missions next then."

"It's not that simple," one of them replied. "Even though they may be available on your mission list, you will need to pass a test before you're allowed to partake in missions within the Red Zone. There's a reason why many of us are doing this mission instead."
"What sort of test?"
"Your Void Control. Since the Void Specters become aggressive in the Red Zone, you will be required to use Void Control frequently."
"I see..."

"If you're going to try, don't bother. You may have learned Void Control in a few days, but the tests are a different kind of beast. Most people qualify only after decades of training. Even with your heaven-sent talents, you'll likely still need at least a few years."
"I'll keep that in mind. Here are the Unknown Ores," said Yuan as he handed the Unknown Ores to the squad leader, who was in charge of accounting for them.
Of course, he didn't forget to absorb all of the Eternal Essence from them before doing so.
Time continued to pass, and in the blink of an eye, it was time for them to return to the city.

chapters.title: Chapter 2608 Learning Void Control
paragraphs: "Welcome back, everyone."
The soldiers greeted one another as the four squads returned from their gathering mission.
After a quick headcount confirmed that everyone had returned safely, the four squads pooled their loot.
"Three hundred and twenty-seven Unknown Ores, huh? Looks like we got lucky, especially the third squad, who contributed over a hundred ores."
"You can thank Corporal Yuan for that, as he'd gathered more than half of our total alone."
"Regardless, everyone did a good job. Hope to see you all in the next one again."
The group was disbanded soon after.
Although Yuan could've absorbed all of the Unknown Ores of their Eternal Essence, he decided against it, as he did not want to be too greedy. Above all, he wanted to be cautious.
After leaving, Yuan went to look for Sergeant Quang.
"I want to partake in missions within the Red Zone, but I heard that one must take some kind of test."
"That's correct. Your Void Control will be evaluated by a group of examiners to see if you qualify to enter the Red Zone."
"Where do I go to take the test?" Yuan then asked.

"You can—" Sergeant Quang suddenly paused, his eyebrows raising as he realized something. "You're trying to take the test? Now? That implies you already know Void Control, but as far as I am aware, you did not have the time or opportunity to learn such a technique," he said.
Besides Wu Wang and Shi Fa, neither Sergeant Bing nor Sergeant Quang were aware that Yuan could use Void Control.
"I just want to know for future reference—for when I learn Void Control," Yuan said, concealing the fact that he had already mastered it, let alone knew it.

"Then you're looking quite far into the future. Void Control isn't something you can learn in a day—or even a month. Most people need years just to grasp it, let alone reach a level that would allow them to traverse the Red Zone. Even for a genius like you, it would likely take several years."

"Then I'd better start learning now, huh?" Yuan said with a calm smile. "I still have a training session with an elite soldier as a reward for my performance during recruitment. Could I ask them to teach me Void Control?"
Sergeant Quang nodded.
"You can. Are you going to ask me to teach you?" he then asked.
However, to his surprise, Yuan shook his head and said, "No, I already have someone in mind."
"Who?"
"Sergeant Wu."

"Seriously? Instead of Wu Wang, I'd recommend Shi Fa. He's a much better teacher—not that I'm trying to badmouth Wu Wang. Hell, since you can technically ask anyone to train you, you might as well choose an actual instructor. They're trained to teach, after all."
However, Yuan shook his head and refused.
"I have my reasons for choosing him."
"If that's what you really want..."
"I'll let Wu Wang know," Sergeant Quang said a moment later.
"Thanks."
Yuan returned to his living quarters to rest afterward.

Although the idea might have seemed sudden, he had already planned to pretend to learn Void Control from either Wu Wang or Shi Fa. Revealing that he already knew it would raise too many suspicions, and he knew he couldn't fool everyone as easily as he had the soldiers before.
A few days later, Yuan received merit and money from the gathering mission, and on the same day, Wu Wang appeared at his doorstep with a frown on his face.
"Is it true that you requested for me to train you?" he questioned the moment Yuan opened the door. "Please tell me that's not true and that bastard Quang Qing is just messing with me."
A wide smile tugged at Yuan's lips as he responded, "No, it's true. I want you to teach me Void Control."
"Are you fucking with me?! You want me to teach you Void Control?! If anything, I should be asking to be your student!" Wu Wang exclaimed in disbelief.
After all, he was fully aware of how profound Yuan's Void Control was—that it was far superior to his own.
"Lower your voice. Are you trying to let the entire residential area hear you?" Yuan sighed, shaking his head.

"Calm down. I'm not seriously asking you to teach me. Aside from you, Shi Fa, and a few others who aren't a concern, no one knows I can use Void Control. If I suddenly use it, people would grow suspicious, so I need to pretend that I learned it from you."
"Don't worry, I won't take up much of your time. Only a few days. Hell, I won't mind training you, either."
"You? Train me?" Wu Wang stared at Yuan with one of his eyebrows raised.
"Are we still talking about Void Control?" he inquired.
"If you think Void Control is the only advantage I have over you, you're sorely mistaken," Yuan replied with an arrogant smile.
Wu Wang fell silent for a moment, visibly irritated by his claim.
"In that case, I'd love to see what else you think you're better than me at!"
"Does that mean you accept my request?"
"Yes. Even if you didn't provoke me, I would've agreed, since I will get merit for training you."
"Is that so? Then let's go."
Yuan and Wu Wang made their way to a private training room.
Once they were inside, alone, they began sparring.

Before the match, Wu Wang had been certain there was no way he would lose to Yuan in a fair fight. Yet only a few minutes later, he found himself sprawled on the ground, having failed to touch even a single hair on Yuan's body.
Wu Wang stared at the ceiling with a bewildered expression on his face, looking like he was having trouble comprehending what had just happened.
"Want to go again?" Yuan asked.
Wu Wang immediately sprang back to his feet, and their second round began.
The two continued sparring for several rounds without pause.
In the end, Wu Wang lost every match—each defeat more crushing than the last.
"So, how about it? Still going to refuse my guidance?" Yuan asked with a cheeky smile as he looked down at Wu Wang, who lay sprawled on the ground.
Wu Wang gritted his teeth in frustration, but instead of giving in to his anger, he swallowed both his pride and his resentment before asking Yuan for guidance.
Thus, Yuan started training Wu Wang.
Six days later, Sergeant Quang and Sergeant Bing showed up at their training room together to check on Yuan's progress.
"It's much harder than you expected, isn't it?" Sergeant Quang asked Yuan with a faint smile, his expression practically saying, 'I told you so'.
Before Yuan could even respond, Sergeant Bing chuckled and said, "Even with your talents, there is no way you can learn Void Control so quickly!"
"Um... actually, he's already learned it."
Rather than Yuan, it was Wu Wang who spoke.
"What did you just say?"
Sergeant Quang and Sergeant Bing both stiffened, their eyes widening in shock and disbelief.
"I said he's already learned Void Control," Wu Wang repeated in an awkward voice, feeling a little guilty about fooling his comrades.
"Surely you're just messing with us," Sergeant Bing eventually responded. "There's no way someone can learn Void Control in just a few—"
Before she could even finish her sentence, Yuan used Void Manipulation, teleporting directly in front of her.
"You were saying?" he said, a smile tugging at his lips.
"Heavens!"
Sergeant Bing was so surprised that she fell backward, hitting the hard ground with her buttocks.
"That was... Void Control?!" Sergeant Quang exclaimed, looking like he'd just seen a ghost.
"You actually managed to learn Voice Control in just six days?! Just what kind of monster are you?!"
"I am just good at learning things," Yuan calmly replied. "Really, really good."
"Even so, there should be a limit to such nonsense!"
Yuan silently shrugged.
"Just what kind of training did you do?" Sergeant Bing suddenly asked as she stood back up, one hand rubbing on her buttocks.
"Just normal training," Yuan replied.
"And how did you train, exactly?"
"Normally."

Sergeant Bing gave up on trying to receive a proper answer from Yuan and turned to look at Wu Wang, who quickly said, "He isn't lying. He just sat there and watched me use Void Control over and over again. Then, after a few days, he was able to use Void Control."
"He learned it just by watching? That's beyond ridiculous?" Sergeant Bing shook her head.
"I don't know what else to tell you," Wu Wang shook his head.

"Regardless..." Sergeant Quang started speaking, "Even if you managed to learn Void Control in just a few days, you'll likely need at least several months of training before you become proficient enough for the test."
"Perhaps, but I want to take the test and see just how difficult it is," Yuan responded. "If I fail, I can just retake the test in the future."

"I just want to know for future reference—for when I learn Void Control," Yuan said, concealing the fact that he had already mastered it, let alone knew it.
"Then you're looking quite far into the future.
Void Control isn't something you can learn in a day—or even a month.
Most people need years just to grasp it, let alone reach a level that would allow them to traverse the Red Zone.
Even for a genius like you, it would likely take several years."
"Then I'd better start learning now, huh?" Yuan said with a calm smile.
"I still have a training session with an elite soldier as a reward for my performance during recruitment.
Could I ask them to teach me Void Control?"
Sergeant Quang nodded.
"You can.
Are you going to ask me to teach you?" he then asked.
However, to his surprise, Yuan shook his head and said, "No, I already have someone in mind."
"Who?"
"Sergeant Wu."
"Seriously?
Instead of Wu Wang, I'd recommend Shi Fa.
He's a much better teacher—not that I'm trying to badmouth Wu Wang.
Hell, since you can technically ask anyone to train you, you might as well choose an actual instructor.
They're trained to teach, after all."
However, Yuan shook his head and refused.
"I have my reasons for choosing him."
"If that's what you really want..."
"I'll let Wu Wang know," Sergeant Quang said a moment later.
"Thanks."
Yuan returned to his living quarters to rest afterward.
Although the idea might have seemed sudden, he had already planned to pretend to learn Void Control from either Wu Wang or Shi Fa.
Revealing that he already knew it would raise too many suspicions, and he knew he couldn't fool everyone as easily as he had the soldiers before.
A few days later, Yuan received merit and money from the gathering mission, and on the same day, Wu Wang appeared at his doorstep with a frown on his face.
"Is it true that you requested for me to train you?" he questioned the moment Yuan opened the door.
"Please tell me that's not true and that bastard Quang Qing is just messing with me."
A wide smile tugged at Yuan's lips as he responded, "No, it's true.
I want you to teach me Void Control."
"Are you fucking with me?!
You want me to teach you Void Control?!
If anything, I should be asking to be your student!" Wu Wang exclaimed in disbelief.
After all, he was fully aware of how profound Yuan's Void Control was—that it was far superior to his own.
"Lower your voice.
Are you trying to let the entire residential area hear you?" Yuan sighed, shaking his head.
"Calm down.
I'm not seriously asking you to teach me.
Aside from you, Shi Fa, and a few others who aren't a concern, no one knows I can use Void Control.
If I suddenly use it, people would grow suspicious, so I need to pretend that I learned it from you."
"Don't worry, I won't take up much of your time.
Only a few days.
Hell, I won't mind training you, either."
"You?
Train me?" Wu Wang stared at Yuan with one of his eyebrows raised.
"Are we still talking about Void Control?" he inquired.
"If you think Void Control is the only advantage I have over you, you're sorely mistaken," Yuan replied with an arrogant smile.
Wu Wang fell silent for a moment, visibly irritated by his claim.
"In that case, I'd love to see what else you think you're better than me at!"
"Does that mean you accept my request?"
"Yes.
Even if you didn't provoke me, I would've agreed, since I will get merit for training you."
"Is that so?
Then let's go."
Yuan and Wu Wang made their way to a private training room.
Once they were inside, alone, they began sparring.
Before the match, Wu Wang had been certain there was no way he would lose to Yuan in a fair fight.
Yet only a few minutes later, he found himself sprawled on the ground, having failed to touch even a single hair on Yuan's body.
Wu Wang stared at the ceiling with a bewildered expression on his face, looking like he was having trouble comprehending what had just happened.
"Want to go again?" Yuan asked.
Wu Wang immediately sprang back to his feet, and their second round began.
The two continued sparring for several rounds without pause.
In the end, Wu Wang lost every match—each defeat more crushing than the last.
"So, how about it?
Still going to refuse my guidance?" Yuan asked with a cheeky smile as he looked down at Wu Wang, who lay sprawled on the ground.
Wu Wang gritted his teeth in frustration, but instead of giving in to his anger, he swallowed both his pride and his resentment before asking Yuan for guidance.
Thus, Yuan started training Wu Wang.
Six days later, Sergeant Quang and Sergeant Bing showed up at their training room together to check on Yuan's progress.
"It's much harder than you expected, isn't it?" Sergeant Quang asked Yuan with a faint smile, his expression practically saying, 'I told you so'.
Before Yuan could even respond, Sergeant Bing chuckled and said, "Even with your talents, there is no way you can learn Void Control so quickly!"
"Um... actually, he's already learned it."
Rather than Yuan, it was Wu Wang who spoke.
"What did you just say?"
Sergeant Quang and Sergeant Bing both stiffened, their eyes widening in shock and disbelief.
"I said he's already learned Void Control," Wu Wang repeated in an awkward voice, feeling a little guilty about fooling his comrades.
"Surely you're just messing with us," Sergeant Bing eventually responded.
"There's no way someone can learn Void Control in just a few—"
Before she could even finish her sentence, Yuan used Void Manipulation, teleporting directly in front of her.
"You were saying?" he said, a smile tugging at his lips.
"Heavens!"
Sergeant Bing was so surprised that she fell backward, hitting the hard ground with her buttocks.
"That was...
Void Control?!" Sergeant Quang exclaimed, looking like he'd just seen a ghost.
"You actually managed to learn Voice Control in just six days?!
Just what kind of monster are you?!"
"I am just good at learning things," Yuan calmly replied.
"Really, really good."
"Even so, there should be a limit to such nonsense!"
Yuan silently shrugged.
"Just what kind of training did you do?" Sergeant Bing suddenly asked as she stood back up, one hand rubbing on her buttocks.
"Just normal training," Yuan replied.
"And how did you train, exactly?"
"Normally."
Sergeant Bing gave up on trying to receive a proper answer from Yuan and turned to look at Wu Wang, who quickly said, "He isn't lying.
He just sat there and watched me use Void Control over and over again.
Then, after a few days, he was able to use Void Control."
"He learned it just by watching?
That's beyond ridiculous?" Sergeant Bing shook her head.
"I don't know what else to tell you," Wu Wang shook his head.

"Regardless..." Sergeant Quang started speaking, "Even if you managed to learn Void Control in just a few days, you'll likely need at least several months of training before you become proficient enough for the test."
"Perhaps, but I want to take the test and see just how difficult it is," Yuan responded.
"If I fail, I can just retake the test in the future."

chapters.title: Chapter 2609 Red Zone Exam
paragraphs: "Before I apply for the test, I would like to know the level of Void Control required to pass it," Yuan said.
"Does it really matter? You either pass or don't," Sergeant Quang remarked.
"It does to me."
After a moment of silence, Sergeant Quang sighed out loud before speaking, "Watch. This is the level you must reach to pass the test."
The next moment, Sergeant Quang used Void Control, teleporting left and right in a steady rhythm. Each teleport covered exactly one hundred meters—not a single meter more or less.
"You'll be required to do more than just teleport left and right," Sergeant Quang said afterward.
"There will be obstacle courses," Sergeant Bing elaborated.
"I see..."
Yuan nodded, committing Sergeant Quang's demonstration to memory. He wanted a proper benchmark so he wouldn't go overboard during the test and completely obliterate it.

After all, he needed to make it as believable as possible. Learning Void Control so quickly was already outrageous enough. If he displayed a level of mastery that would normally take eras to achieve immediately after learning it, it would undoubtedly raise a lot of eyebrows.
Yuan turned to Wu Wang and spoke with a smile, "Thanks for the training. I will do my best not to disappoint you."
"S-Sure..." Wu Wang nodded with a stiff expression, looking a bit embarrassed.
"Now... where do I go to take the test?" Yuan asked.

"You can do it by attempting to accept a Red Zone mission," Sergeant Bing explained. "If you don't meet the qualifications, you'll be prompted to take the test. Once you accept, you'll be scheduled for the next available session."
"The mission hall, it is."
Yuan immediately made his way to the mission hall.
While he entered the queue to wait for his turn, soldiers would come up to him and ask, "What mission will you be accepting this time, Corporal Yuan? Another cleanup mission?"
"Haven't you heard? He's doing gathering missions now."
"Perhaps he'll do something different this time."
"Haven't you heard? He's doing gathering missions now."
"Perhaps he'll do something different this time."
Yuan replied, "It's a secret.
Once it was his turn to use the machine, Yuan immediately picked the mission that required him to gather Unknown Ores in the Red Zone.
<Checking soldier's qualifications>
<You currently lack the permit to enter the Red Zone>
<Would you like to schedule the Red Zone Exam for the permit?>
<You have been accepted to partake in the next Red Zone Exam, scheduled to begin in 77 hours and 32 minutes>
When Yuan returned, Sergeant Quang asked, "When is the test?"
"In 77 hours."
"What are you going to do until then? Keep on practicing your Void Control?"
He nodded.
"But I intend on doing it alone. Since I already learned it, I can practice by myself," he then said.
"Are you sure? I don't mind training you for a few days," Sergeant Quang said.
Yuan smiled and said, "Just your thoughts are enough."
"If you insist."
Once Yuan returned to his living quarters, he said, "I'll be training in my room, so you don't need to escort me anywhere until the day of the exam."
"Training inside your room?"
They looked at him with raised eyebrows. Although they all lived alone, none of their homes were spacious enough to practice Void Control.
Of course, Yuan had no intention of actually practicing Void Control.
"See ya in 77 hours."
Before they could question him, Yuan hastily retreated into his living quarters and closed the door, leaving them speechless.
"The more time I spend with him, the more mysterious he feels," Sergeant Bing remarked with a dazed expression.
"Now that I think about it, he never goes anywhere in between missions, always remaining inside his home," Sergeant Quang remarked.
"He did go to the training area... once," said Sergeant Bing.
They left shortly afterward, still wondering what Yuan did with his spare time.
Meanwhile, back in his room, Yuan sat in the lotus position with his eyes closed, cultivating using the Limitless Cultivation Technique.

One of the main reasons Yuan could use Limitless continuously without exhausting himself, unlike everyone else, was the Limitless Cultivation Technique, which he cultivated whenever he had the opportunity.
The deeper Yuan's understanding of the technique grew, the more he realized just how powerful it was, especially when paired with his Perfect Heavenly Refinement physique.
'Although it appears simple at first glance and is relatively easy to learn, the deeper I study it, the more profound and difficult it becomes!'
An excited smile tugged at Yuan's lips. It had been a long time since he had encountered something that truly challenged him.
Time passed swiftly, and 77 hours later, Yuan left his living quarters and followed Sergeant Bing to the exam area.
An hour before Yuan showed up at the exam site, several individuals suddenly appeared, startling the examiners there.
"G-General Mei?! And Officers?!"
General Mei and some of her officers had shown up unannounced.
"Don't mind us. We're here to spectate today's examination. That's all," said Mei Feng.
"O-Of course! Please, let me show you to the spectator's room!"

Since it was a simple exam held several times a month, it rarely drew spectators, especially those of higher rank. As for someone of General Mei Feng's standing, this was the first time a person of her rank had ever attended, hence why the examiners were bewildered by her presence.
Once Mei Feng and her associates left for the spectator room, the remaining examiners began openly wondering why she had come.
"It must be one of the examinees! That's the only reason to come here! Check the list again! Find out who she's here to see!"
"I-I think I found him! Corporal Yuan! That's the super rookie who aced the last recruitment and broke all of its previous records!"
"Huh? The last recruitment was only a few months ago, and he's already a Corporal?"
"I'm more interested in why he's already taking this exam. Does he even know what he's walking into? There's no way his Void Control is anywhere near the level needed for this exam."
"Perhaps he's just taking it to see how much work he needs to reach such a level."
"I guess we'll see in an hour..."

chapters.title: Chapter 2610 Void Control Evaluation
paragraphs: "I can't believe Corporal Yuan is already taking the Red Zone Exam right after his first gathering mission," one of the officers with Mei Feng remarked after taking a seat in the spectator's room.
"And to think we thought he was taking it too slow not long ago," someone else remarked.

Another then spoke up, asking, "Aren't you all curious? Since when did he learn Void Control? As far as I am aware, he skipped boot camp and has been on missions since joining, so he doesn't have any time to learn it—at least, he shouldn't."
"Now that you mentioned it..."

They all turned to look at Mei Feng, who calmly replied, "He used his 20,000-meter reward a few days ago, requesting Sergeant Wu to train him, so I can only assume that he learned Void Control in that time."
"Huh? A few days ago? There's no way anyone can learn Void Control that quickly, let alone reach the level required for this exam."
"We'll never know what that guy is thinking."
Some time later, the participants for the Red Zone Exam started showing up at the test site, and in the blink of an eye, hundreds of people gathered.
"This is my seventh time taking this test. I have a good feeling about today!"

"According to my analysis, the difficulty of the Red Zone Exam varies, with some sessions being much easier than others. If my calculations are correct, today's exam should be the easiest one this year!"

The soldiers chatted among themselves as they waited for the exam to begin, unaware that, because of a certain high-ranking officer, they had walked into the most difficult exam ever recorded because the examiners did not want it to look too easy.
"Good luck," Sergeant Bing said to Yuan before going to the spectator's room—one that was different from the private room used by Mei Feng and the other officers.
"Welcome, everyone. Before we begin the evaluation, we will give you a quick run-through of how it works."

"There will be three tests in total. For the first, you'll need to catch balls using Void Control. You don't have to catch all of them—only eighty out of a hundred. For the second test, you must avoid attacks for ten minutes using nothing but Void Control. The final test will assess your precision. Ten people will go at a time.
Soon, the examiners began calling the participants onto the testing ground.

"One more thing, in case this is your first time taking the exam. Aside from moving your arms and body to catch the balls, all physical movement is strictly prohibited. You may only reposition yourself using Void Control, even if you need to move only a few inches."
Once the exam began, a machine positioned at the opposite end of the field started firing glowing green balls at nearly the speed of sound, launching one every three seconds.
Before each ball was fired, a red laser appeared, indicating the general direction it would travel.

Although the test started relatively easily, the firing rate increased after the first twenty balls, with one ball launched every two seconds instead of three. After forty balls, the remaining sixty were fired at one-second intervals.
"W-What's going on?! Why is the test so difficult?! It was supposed to be easy today!" exclaimed the soldier who had done the analysis.
"How can you tell?" someone asked.

"Normally, it doesn't switch to two-second intervals until after fifty balls, and the one-second interval doesn't start until eighty! This time, it switched to two-second intervals after only twenty balls, then to one-second intervals after forty! This is the hardest exam ever recorded!"
"That's crazy... No wonder why half of them dropped out already..."
By the end of the first test, only three of the ten participants managed to catch at least eighty balls, moving on to the second test.
At the end of the first test, the participants were given five minutes to rest while seven more soldiers entered the testing ground to begin theirs.

"For those of you taking the second test, your objective is to avoid all damage for ten minutes. Even a single graze will result in immediate disqualification. After all, against a Void Specter, even the slightest touch means death, so there is absolutely no room for error."

When the second test began for the first three participants, the machines that had previously fired balls began shooting bullets instead, each one aimed directly at them. As before, red lasers indicated where the bullets would travel, appearing first as thick lines that gradually narrowed as the machines prepared to fire.

Each laser represented a single bullet. During the first minute, only one laser appeared every three seconds. At the start of the second minute, two appeared at once, and by the third minute, that number had increased to three.

As the number of bullets increased, the participants had less room to dodge and fewer chances to rest. Since the shots were fired one after another rather than simultaneously, even when three lasers appeared every three seconds, they still had to use Void Control once every second.
At the start of the fourth minute, the number of bullets had suddenly doubled, going from three bullets to six.
Although the speed at which they were fired didn't increase, they shot two bullets at once.
Upon reaching the fifth minute, the number of bullets doubled again.
The same happened after the sixth minute, and the number of bullets increased to twenty-four.

After the seventh minute, the number of bullets didn't merely double—it tripled, now firing seventy-two bullets every three seconds. Moreover, the rate at which it shot them also increased, now shooting twelve bullets at a half-second interval.

This meant the participants could no longer teleport wherever they pleased. Instead, they had to anticipate the bullets' trajectories and identify a safe location to teleport to before the next volley arrived.
By the eighth minute, the participants had to deal with two hundred and sixteen bullets.
During the final minute, however, the exact number no longer mattered, as the machines fired without pause, unleashing a continuous barrage like machine guns.
Ultimately, none of the three participants managed to last all ten minutes and were disqualified in the final minute.

chapters.title: Chapter 2611 Void Control Evaluation(2)
paragraphs: "Hey, analyst, is the second test harder or easier than usual?" one of the participants asked at the end.

The analyst, who had been anxiously biting his nails, stopped to respond, "Harder. Much harder. Just like the first test, this is the first time it's this difficult! Just what in heaven's name is happening today?!"
"Maybe they decided to modify the difficulty, so this will be the new norm."
"That's outrageous! It was already hard enough to pass the exam! There's no reason to make it even harder!"
"Actually, I think I know why this exam is harder than usual..." someone suddenly said before turning to look at a certain individual among the participants.
The others followed his gaze to a handsome man with silky black hair tied neatly into a single ponytail.
"Who is that?" one of them asked in a puzzled voice.
"T-That's Corporal Yuan, the Cleaning Maniac!"
"Cleaning Maniac? What kind of nickname is that? And why would they make the exam harder just because of him?"
"He's called the Cleaning Maniac because he's famous for willingly joining others' cleanup missions ever since he joined the military, even insisting on doing all of the cleaning alone."
"That's impressive in its own right, but that still doesn't explain—"

"Let me finish!" The soldier who was explaining interrupted before continuing, "Not only was he handpicked by General Mei, he even broke all of the records during his recruitment! They're calling him the upcoming Ironman who could rival the Ironwoman!"
Yuan raised an eyebrow as the soldier recounted his background to everyone while staring at him as though he were some rare treasure on display in a museum.

"I appreciate the introduction, but there's no reason to increase the difficulty of the exam solely because of my presence. If anything, they should be lowering it, as I had only learned Void Control a few days ago."
"The hell? Why are you here if you've only learned Void Control a few days ago? Most of us here have trained for over a decade!"
"I guess most of you here have also broken records during your recruitment, huh?" Yuan responded in a sarcastic tone, which immediately ticked off the soldier.
However, the soldier realized he had nothing to argue against Yuan's words, so he quickly fell silent, his face still slightly flushed.
A moment later, Yuan said, "I don't know why they decided to increase the difficulty of this exam, but it has nothing to do with me."
Despite his words, Yuan couldn't help but wonder whether General Gu had arranged it as another attempt to make things difficult for him.
After more than fifty soldiers had attempted and failed the exam, someone finally advanced to the final test, where the precision of their Void Control would be assessed.
On the participant's testing ground, two red circles materialized a mile apart, each barely large enough to fit a pair of feet.

"For the final test, you must use Void Control to teleport between the two circles one hundred consecutive times, with no more than a quarter of a second between each teleport. To pass, you must achieve an accuracy rate of at least ninety percent."

Although the test appeared easy at first glance, the participant was already exhausted from constantly using Void Control throughout the previous two tests. That fatigue greatly diminished both their precision and consistency, making the final test far more difficult than it seemed.
"N-Ninty percent?! That's the requirement for the Purple Zone!" The analyst cried out loud in disbelief. "It's always been eighty percent for Red Zones!"
"It's doomed. Nobody will pass this month's exam."
"We might as well just leave now..." someone muttered out loud. "We can always retake the test at a later date, anyway."
And surprisingly, a few soldiers actually took that advice and left, quitting the test without even attempting it.
The examiners did not stop these soldiers, merely shaking their heads in disappointment.

As for the officers in the private spectator's room, they couldn't care less about the other soldiers, as they were solely there to watch Yuan. Moreover, they knew that this month's exam was cranked up to an unprecedented degree.
"Should we really let them continue the exam at this level of difficulty? To be honest, it seems excessive," one of the officers voiced their concern.
Mei Feng calmly responded, "As long as this doesn't become the new standard, let it continue. It's good to shake things up once in a while. This experience may even benefit them."
Some time later, the participant who reached the final test received his result.
<Accuracy: 80.13%>
The soldier fell to his knees in shock. Had the examiners not raised the passing threshold to ninety percent, he would have barely passed the exam.
"Failed. Please exit the testing grounds."
As if to rub salt into the wound, the examiner coldly announced his failure.

Unwilling to accept the result, the soldier turned toward the examiners and shouted angrily, "Why the hell did you suddenly raise the passing score to ninety percent when it has always been eighty percent?! And without any sort of announcement, either! This is unacceptable!"
As though they had anticipated such backlash, the examiners calmly replied, "The world is evolving, so we soldiers must evolve alongside it."
"What kind of explanation is that?! That's complete nonsense!"
Sure enough, such an excuse was pure bullshit. However, the examiners refused to elaborate.

"Please leave the testing grounds. There are still soldiers who need to take the test. If you're not satisfied with the results, you may take the examination again in the future... once you improve a little more."
"Fuck! This is bullshit!" The soldier cursed out loud as he stomped away.
However, before the soldier left the testing grounds, Yuan could feel the man's gaze fixed on him, as though he blamed Yuan for everything that had happened.
Yuan pretended not to notice, as there was no way for him to prove his innocence.
