chapters.title: Chapter 2612 Void Control Evaluation(3)
paragraphs: After waiting around an hour, Yuan's ears twitched when he heard his name being called.
"Corporal Yuan! Lane number nine!"
Yuan was slightly surprised to hear his name, as he thought he would be called last again, but there were still plenty of people after him.
He calmly walked to his lane while wondering how he should deal with the exam.
'The exam unexpectedly became even more difficult than anticipated... should I just fail on purpose and try again on the next one? They have a test every month, anyway...'
However, after some contemplation, he decided that it wasn't worth waiting another month, and that he might as well get this thing over with today.
When Mei Feng and the officers noticed Yuan entering the testing grounds, they subconsciously sat up with straightened backs.
"What kind of performance will you show us today?" Mei Feng mumbled in a low voice, a subtle smile on her face.
Once Yuan stepped into lane number nine, the test began shortly afterward.
The moment Yuan began using Void Control, the spectators collectively sucked in a breath of cold air. Seeing someone wield it after only a few days of training was simply too astonishing.
Even Mei Feng had harbored some doubts. However, once Yuan demonstrated the technique—even with movements that appeared somewhat amateurish—everyone was left speechless.
"I can't believe it... He's really using Void Control. It's still somewhat unrefined, but that's only natural considering he learned it just a few days ago."

At first, Yuan deliberately made it seem as though he was struggling to catch the balls, which was actually the most difficult part of the exam. However, as the test continued, his Void Control gradually became more refined, giving the impression that he was improving with every use.
"How is he improving so quickly that we can see it with our own eyes?! That kind of talent should be illegal!" One of the participants exclaimed in disbelief.
Soon, Yuan reached his 50th ball, catching all of them. However, after that point, he started to miss a few of them, especially towards the end.
In the end, he'd only managed to catch eighty-one balls in total, which was just slightly passing.
"My word! He's actually passed the first test!"
"Even if he fails the second test, nobody would blame him."
"What if he also passes the second test?
"Unfortunately, I don't think he has any energy to continue. If you hadn't noticed, he slowed down quite a bit toward the end."
After his first test, Yuan was given five minutes to rest, but it was over in the blink of an eye, and his second test began.
'I won't be able to barely pass this test as I did with the first test...' Yuan thought to himself as he dodged the first bullet.
Five minutes later—
"Hey, who was it that claimed he won't have enough energy to continue? He's doing just fine."
"He was given some time to rest, after all. But I'm sure he'll drop within the next two minutes."
Two minutes later, Yuan continued dodging the bullets with the same consistency.
"It's been two minutes..."
"O-One more minute! He will definitely fall within the next minute!"
Yet, two more minutes passed, and after lasting ten minutes, Yuan passed the second test.
"What?! How is that possible?! He was clearly out of breath after the first test! Even if he was given five minutes to rest, that isn't nearly enough time to recover that much! That makes no sense!"
"Your first mistake was to use common sense against a genius like that..."
Although every participant was given five minutes of rest after the first test, there was no rest after the second, so Yuan had to immediately start the third test.

"As amazing as his performance was for someone who'd learned Void Control just a few days ago, this is where he fails," said the analyst. "Even if he has the stamina to keep going, his precision is another subject. I have been watching him closely, and I noticed that his precision has been all over the place. I would be surprised if his accuracy is above 30 percent."
"That low?"
"I guess we'll see..."
The moment the third test started, Yuan started using Void Control to teleport between the two circles.
"H-Hey..."
"That's ridiculous!"
Only seconds after Yuan began, everyone realized he was performing exceptionally well—better than anyone who had taken the exam before him.
The spectators watched with wide eyes as Yuan teleported with astonishing precision, displaying a level of mastery that far surpassed anything he had shown up to that point.
One hundred teleports later—
<Accuracy: 90.05%>
"What?!"
Many exclaimed simultaneously, unwilling to believe their eyes.
"P-Pass..." The examiners swallowed nervously before announcing the result, their voices filled with disbelief.
The spectator room was eerily silent, as everyone needed a moment to process what they had just witnessed.

"His precision during the first and second tests was nowhere near this level... Was he deliberately hiding his abilities, or did he truly improve that much in such a short time?" one of the officers muttered thoughtfully.
"He has no reason to conceal his skills. Considering he learned Void Control in only a few days, it's more likely that he simply improved that quickly," someone replied.
Meanwhile, on the training grounds—
"Corporal Yuan, you've already finished the test. You can leave now."
However, Yuan turned to face the examiners and uttered words that nobody there could've anticipated even in a billion years.
"Is it possible for me to retake the test?" he asked with a calm expression.
"Excuse me?"
Everyone present stared at him with widened eyes.
"W-Why?" one of the examiners snapped out of his daze and asked.
"Because I am not satisfied with my results," Yuan responded in a serious tone.

After a moment of silence, another examiner spoke. "S-Since you passed, you may request a retake. However, you'll have to forfeit your current result, and whatever score you receive on your second attempt will become final—even if you fail. You won't be allowed to retake the exam again. Are you fine with that?"
Yuan silently nodded, leaving them speechless.

chapters.title: Chapter 2613 Retaking the Exam
paragraphs: "Is he crazy?! He barely passed the exam, which is already a miracle itself, but he wants to retake it?! Does he really think he can obtain a higher score?!" The officers were in disbelief at Yuan's arrogance.
"I don't understand why he even wants a higher score... It's not a competition, and he gains nothing from it."
"This must be some kind of illness for geniuses like him. They are never satisfied."
Mei Feng then spoke, "If he wants to do it again, let him. If he fails, then he can only blame himself."
Meanwhile, Yuan asked the examiners after having his request accepted, "Do I have to retake the test immediately? I'd like to get an hour of rest."
"You can retake it at any time as long as the exams are still going," replied an examiner.
"Alright."
Yuan left the testing grounds and began resting by the wall.
"That guy's truly crazy."
"Bastard is just trying to show off. I hope he fails the second exam."
The exam continued, but not a single soldier passed after Yuan.
Even after failing, however, none of them left the building. Instead, they chose to remain behind and watch Yuan retake the exam.
An hour later, Yuan got off the floor and approached the examiners.
"I am ready to retake the exam."
"O-Okay. We'll send you in once there's an available lane."
"Thank you."
A few minutes later, Yuan returned to the testing grounds and coincidentally stepped into lane number nine once more.
When the exam began, his performance during the first test was noticeably better than before—so much so that the difference was incomparable.
"What the hell?! It's like I am watching a different person!"
The officers nearly got off their seats after seeing how much Yuan had improved.
During his first attempt, Yuan had purposefully started missing after the 50th ball. This time, however, he was determined to catch every single one.
Some time later—
"He actually caught all hundred balls!"

"What the hell is going on?! Even if his mastery of Void Control had drastically increased, he shouldn't have the stamina to keep going! An hour of rest is nowhere near enough time to fully recover, either!
Five minutes later, Yuan began his second test.

Since he had passed it flawlessly during his first attempt, the spectators assumed there was nothing left for him to improve. However, rather than dodging preemptively like most participants, Yuan waited until the very last instant—just before each bullet struck—to teleport away, displaying both his extraordinary reaction speed and absolute confidence.
Ten minutes later, Yuan moved onto the third test.
<Accuracy: 99.96%>
Yuan looked at the results and silently nodded, satisfied with them.
"N-Ninety-nine point ninety-six percent?! That's practically a perfect score!"
"Heavens!"
The officers could no longer contain their excitement and stood from their seats, their eyes glued to Yuan's miraculous results.
"To improve this much in such a short time! What terrifying talents! It's practically otherworldly!"
Meanwhile, the examiners were so awestruck that they fell into a daze and forgot to announce the result.
The other soldiers could only stare at Yuan as if they had seen a ghost, their eyes widened and jaws hanging open in complete disbelief.

Although Yuan could have simply accepted the result of his first attempt, he wanted everyone present to witness firsthand how quickly he could improve. That way, even if he suddenly accomplished something outrageous in the future, no one would question it.
In other words, he wanted to drill one thought into their minds—that nothing was beyond his capabilities.
"I can leave, right?" Yuan asked the examiners, snapping them out of their daze.
"Y-Yes..."
"Do I get some sort of certificate to verify that I have passed this exam?" Yuan asked as he walked off the testing grounds.
"No, we'll update your information after the exam today, and you'll be able to partake in Red Zone missions by tomorrow."
"Sounds good."
Yuan began making his way to the exit but was promptly stopped by a familiar voice.
"Wait a second, Corporal Yuan."
Yuan turned around to follow the sound of the voice.
"General Mei?" he muttered in a surprised tone.
"General Mei?!" The other soldiers hastily raised their arms to salute her after taking a moment to comprehend the situation.
"Follow me to my office. I'd like to have a word with you," she said to him.
"I understand."
Once Yuan followed Mei Feng to her office, she immediately asked him, "Tell me the truth. Did you already know Void Control before joining the military?"
"What makes you think that?"
Instead of directly answering her question, Yuan asked one of his own, a playful smile on his face.
Mei Feng sighed aloud before speaking, "Your expression confirms my suspicion. Where did you learn it? From your original world?"
Yuan nodded and answered truthfully, "That's correct, but in my world, it's called Void Manipulation."
Mei Feng rubbed her eyes and sighed again.
"What was the purpose of your performance today?"
"Well, it'd be odd for someone who just joined the military to know Void Control without doing proper training, right?"
"I mean, why'd you retake the test when your first one would've sufficed?"
"To put things simply... to raise my reputation."
"Even though pretty much everyone is already aware of your existence?"
"Not that sort of reputation. I want to reach a level where nobody will question anything that I do."
"That sounds like something someone with ulterior motives would say—a villain, so to speak."
Yuan chuckled at her words.
"What are you worried about?"

Mei Feng fell silent for a moment before responding, "To be perfectly honest, I suspected you might be a spy from another city. However, no spy would willingly draw this much attention to themselves."
"No response? You could at least try to deny it."
"What would be the point of that? You already implied that you don't think I am a spy." Yuan shrugged.
"You're really a handful..." Mei Feng sighed for the third time.

"To put things simply... to raise my reputation."
"Even though pretty much everyone is already aware of your existence?"
"Not that sort of reputation.
I want to reach a level where nobody will question anything that I do."
"That sounds like something someone with ulterior motives would say—a villain, so to speak."
Yuan chuckled at her words.
"What are you worried about?"
Mei Feng fell silent for a moment before responding, "To be perfectly honest, I suspected you might be a spy from another city.
However, no spy would willingly draw this much attention to themselves."
"No response?
You could at least try to deny it."
"What would be the point of that?
You already implied that you don't think I am a spy." Yuan shrugged.
"You're really a handful..." Mei Feng sighed for the third time.

chapters.title: Chapter 2614 Abnormalities
paragraphs: "Anything else?" Yuan asked a moment later.
After a brief moment of silence. Mei Feng spoke, "Now that you've acquired the authorization to enter the Red Zone, are you going there for your next mission?"
"Of course."
"What kind?"
"Gathering Unknown Ores, as there are no other options for a mere corporal like me."

"A mere corporal?" Mei Feng raised an eyebrow at his remark. "If you somehow didn't figure it out already, you're already allowed access to missions typically assigned to Sergeants, such as the one we just mentioned."
"I was aware," Yuan admitted. "But when do I get access to missions within the Purple Zone?"
"Let's slow down a little and take one step at a time. You've just passed the exam for the Red Zone, after all."

"I wouldn't call that a test... at least not from my perspective. Hell, it barely qualifies as a warm-up. When it comes to Void Manipulation—or Void Control, as you call it—I wouldn't be surprised if no one in this world can wield it better than I do," Yuan said.
Despite his seemingly arrogant declaration, there wasn't the slightest trace of arrogance in his eyes.

"Even if your Void Control is unmatched in this world, there are things beyond the Red Zone—dangerous entities that defy comprehension, especially for someone who came from another world," Mei Feng said, shaking her head.

"There's no need to be impatient. You're already progressing several times faster than other geniuses. If you continue at this pace, you'll definitely be able to enter the Purple Zone within a few years."
"A few years, huh?" Yuan mumbled.

He wouldn't be this impatient if he had concrete evidence that this world was merely an illusion or a dream. The same applied if he knew whether time here flowed faster or slower than in the Nine Heavens, as it did in the Demonic Realm.
Of course, he was still leaning toward this world being an illusion of sorts, hence why he wasn't too panicked.
'I have seen and experienced plenty of realistic illusions throughout my lives, and this one... although it is the most realistic one I've experienced so far, my gut tells me this world is fake...'
Despite those thoughts, Yuan still couldn't completely dismiss the minuscule possibility that this world was real.
"By the way, how's your daughter? Is she doing okay in boot camp?" Yuan suddenly asked about Mei Xiaoyun.
"What makes you think that I would be keeping an eye on her?" Mei Feng asked with a slight frown.
"You don't have to pretend to hate her since I am not your daughter," Yuan shook his head. "There's a reason you asked me to bring her into the military, after all.
After a moment of silence, Mei Feng sighed, "She's doing fine. A few had tried to recruit her, but they were all immediately shut down by her."
"Oh? Does that mean she's already decided to join one of your divisions?" Yuan smiled.
"Who knows?" Mei Feng suddenly spun her chair around so Yuan couldn't see her face.
"If there's nothing else, I am going to prepare for my mission in the Red Zone," Yuan then said.
"Go."
After leaving Mei Feng's office, Yuan returned home to rest for the day since the examiners said it would take at least a day for his status to be updated.
The following day, Yuan was escorted to the mission hall by Sergeant Quang.
"I heard about the exam from Sergeant Bing. You're one crazy bastard," he said with a bittersweet smile on his face.
"It's because I had an amazing teacher," Yuan laughed out loud.
"Yeah... sure..."

Of course, Sergeant Quang didn't believe for a moment that Wu Wang possessed such teaching ability. Instead, he suspected that Yuan had already learned Void Control before joining the military and was merely putting on an act.
However, since Yuan had been personally recruited by General Mei, Sergeant Quang chose not to question him, deciding it would only create unnecessary trouble.

However, when Yuan saw the missions available, his eyes stopped at the second mission.
'Unknown Crystals... If I recall correctly, Unknown Crystals are much rarer than Unknown Ores, so logically, they should contain even more Eternal Essence!
Although Yuan had planned on searching for Unknown Ores, he changed his mind and decided to look for Unknown Crystals instead.
Moreover, there was a good chance that they would pick up any Unknown Ores along the way—at least it was a logical assumption.

<Request has been approved>

After accepting the mission, Yuan went home to cultivate.
Meanwhile, in a facility somewhere within the military base—
"Senior! We've detected abnormalities with some of the Unknown Ores." A young woman called out to her supervisor while holding an Unknown Ore in her grasp.
"What sort of abnormalities?" The senior inquired for more information.

"Well, we noticed that we were receiving less Limitless than usual during extraction, and after a thorough examination, we discovered that some of the Unknown Ores had already been extracted of their energy."
"Are you sure someone didn't accidentally mix the old ones in with the new batch? It happens from time to time."

"No, we're certain that wasn't the case. These Unknown Ores had only just been delivered. Moreover, they retained their glowing appearance despite containing no energy, whereas the ones we extract always darken and turn into ordinary rocks."
The senior frowned upon hearing this and fixed her gaze on the Unknown Ore in the young woman's hand.
"Is that...?"
"Yes. This is one of them," the young woman replied as she handed it to the senior.

chapters.title: Chapter 2615 Red Zone
paragraphs: The senior examined the glistening Unknown Ore in her hands. Had her junior not pointed out the anomaly, she would never have realized that it contained no energy.
"How many Unknown Ores are like this?" she asked after a moment of silence.
"Sixty-one... so far."
"That many?" The senior's eyes widened at the number.
Since this was the first time they had encountered such an issue, she had expected only a handful of ores to be affected. However, the actual number far exceeded her expectations.
"Do we know where these ores came from?" she asked a few seconds later.
"We know they were collected by the military, but that's about it. We only record the basic details, so we don't keep track of their exact origins."
"Well, starting now, that's exactly what we're going to do. We need to trace their origins and rule out any possibility of foul play."
"Foul play...?" The junior looked surprised. "You think someone is responsible for this? It should be impossible for anyone outside this facility to extract Limitless from Unknown Ores."

"As I said, we need to rule out every possibility, even those that seem impossible. I also find it difficult to believe that anyone outside this facility can extract Limitless from Unknown Ores. However, if someone truly has discovered a way, we must find them as soon as possible. It would be catastrophic if the other cities learned of their existence and got their hands on them."
"Yes, Senior!"
"Also, I shouldn't have to say this, but this information doesn't leave this facility."
"What about the Generals?"
"No... at least, not right now. We'll do so once we gather more information and evidence."
"I understand."
Two days later, Yuan arrived at the Eastern Gate for his mission.
Before he arrived, Yuan expected to see a large group of soldiers just like his previous gathering mission. However, he was surprised to find only five other soldiers present.
"Is this everyone?" Yuan asked.
"No, there should be one more."

"Why are there so few participants? Is it because there aren't many soldiers permitted to enter the Red Zone?" Yuan asked. "As you can probably tell, this is my first time joining this kind of mission.

"Your first time, huh? Well, it has nothing to do with a shortage of qualified soldiers. Plenty of them are permitted to enter the Red Zone. However, we aren't searching for Unknown Ores—we're looking for Unknown Crystals. They're rarely found outside the tunnels, and the limited space inside means we can only bring seven or eight people at most."
"Tunnels...?" Yuan raised an eyebrow at this new information.
"Is this your first time entering the Red Zone, too?"
He nodded.
"No wonder. Tunnels only exist in the Red Zone and beyond. As its name suggests, it's a tunnel that goes underground."
"Are there Void Specters inside these tunnels?"
"Of course. And unlike gathering Unknown Ores, we cannot ignore them, so we'll have to get rid of them in order to reach the Unknown Crystals."

'Cleaning Void Specters while gathering resources at the same time? This mission offers the best of both worlds!' Yuan exclaimed inwardly, already feeling impatient to go out there and start absorbing more Eternal Essence.
A few minutes later, the seventh member of the squad showed up.
"Oh?" Yuan muttered in a somewhat surprised voice after seeing Shi Fa's face.
"Why do you look so surprised? Don't you take a look at who's in your squad before the mission?" Shi Fa asked as he approached the group.
"No," Yuan said as he shook his head. "I don't really care who is in the squad, either."
"Is that so? I won't get into the details here, but you really should start looking," Shi Fa said. "You want to make sure there aren't any bad apples in your squad, after all."
Some time later, once they confirmed everyone was present, Shi Fa said, "The system has appointed me as the squad leader. If there are any objections, speak up."
When no one voiced any objections, Shi Fa nodded and said, "Alright. Then let's go."
They teleported to the city walls shortly after, before traversing straight toward the Red Zone, ignoring every Void Specter they encountered along the way.
Of course, they also picked up every Unknown Ore they discovered.
"So this is the Red Zone, huh?" Yuan muttered as he entered it for the first time.
Beyond the barren landscape, a thin veil of crimson mist blanketed the sky, casting the entire region in an ominous red hue.
"If you're wondering about the red particles, you don't have to worry. It's not harmful," Shi Fa said to Yuan just in case he was concerned.
"What is it?" Yuan asked.
"We don't know, but we're fairly certain it doesn't affect us, as nobody has ever gotten sick from entering the Red Zone."
"I see..."
However, Yuan quietly examined the red mist with his divine sense.
'T-This is—!'
His eyes widened when he recognized it.
'This is Chaotic Essence!"
At least that was his first impression.
'No, something isn't right...'
He quickly realized something was different.

"Now that we're in the Red Zone, stay alert, especially you, Corporal Yuan, considering this is your first time here. The Void Specters behave differently in the Red Zone, and they are much more aggressive. However, if one attacks you, do not fight back and keep moving forward."
"I understand."
As they continued forward, Yuan kept half of his attention focused on the crimson mist and the other half on the Void Specters.

'This is definitely Chaotic Essence, but it feels incomplete—like it had just formed. Could this be what Chaotic Essence is like before it develops its chaotic attribute and becomes the energy I'm familiar with?' he speculated.
As Yuan spent more time examining the mist, he became more confident in his own theory.
He tried absorbing some of the red mist, but it had no effect on his Chaotic Essence. However, he could feel his energy being restored.
'It's not strong enough to benefit me even in the slightest...' he sighed inwardly, and he started to wonder if it was any different in the Purple Zone.

chapters.title: Chapter 2616 Red Zone(2)
paragraphs: An hour after entering the Red Zone, one of the Void Specters suddenly attacked a soldier, forming an arm that shot forward like a spear.
Fortunately, the soldier remained alert and evaded it using Void Control.
However, the nearby Void Specters also started attacking, forcing everyone to use Void Control to teleport to safety, ignoring the Unknown Ores scattered nearby.
"Are we just going to wander aimlessly and hope we find one of these tunnels?" Yuan asked after several hours.
"No."
Shi Fa responded by showing Yuan the small device he had been carrying ever since they entered the Red Zone.
"Areas containing Unknown Crystals cause subtle changes in the surrounding atmosphere. This device can detect those fluctuations and guide us toward their source."
"I've been wondering what that device was..." Yuan muttered.
"The only drawback of this device is its limited detection range," Shi Fa continued. "So, to answer your earlier question, yes—we're essentially wandering around until it detects something."
Several more hours passed, yet they still hadn't found a tunnel. None of the soldiers in the squad spoke, each remaining fully focused on their surroundings and personal safety.
The atmosphere was a stark contrast to the Orange Zone, where everyone acted far more relaxed and casual.
As for Yuan, he'd stopped studying the red mist to look for the tunnels with his own methods.
'If Unknown Crystals are anything like Unknown Ores and contain Eternal Essence, I should be able to detect them. The only problem is...'

Unknown Ores were abundant throughout the Red Zone, with most of them buried underground. Their sheer number interfered with Yuan's senses, making it difficult for him to distinguish any potential Unknown Crystals among them—or so he thought.
'What a tremendous amount of Eternal Essence! I can sense it all the way from here even though it's so far away!' Yuan cried inwardly when it suddenly entered his detection range.
However, there was a slight issue.
Rather than heading toward the source of the Eternal Essence, his squad was heading in another direction.
With no other choice, Yuan said to Shi Fa, who was the squad leader, "Hey, this is going to sound weird, but my gut is telling me to head that way."
Yuan pointed in the direction of the energy.
Shi Fa followed his gesture and aimed the device that way, but it showed no reaction whatsoever.
When Shi Fa turned to look at him again, Yuan quickly spoke, "My instincts are never wrong. Just trust me on this one."
"Alright."
Knowing just how abnormal an existence Yuan was, Shi Fa didn't doubt him for a moment and immediately instructed the squad to head in the direction he had indicated.
One... two... three...

Five more hours passed without the slightest reaction from Shi Fa's device. Just as he began to doubt Yuan's instincts, however, the device suddenly vibrated, and a red arrow appeared on its screen, pointing in the very direction they were already heading.
"A-A tunnel! There's a tunnel up ahead!" Shi Fa announced to the others, his voice sounding a little shaken.
He turned to look at Yuan, who remained silent, but there was a smile hanging on his lips that said 'I told you so'.
Another hour later, they finally arrived at their destination—a cave-like burrow that descended deep underground.
"I can't believe we found one so quickly," said one of the soldiers.
"Right? It's normal to go weeks without finding one."
"This is likely the fastest tunnel discovery in recent times."
"And we have Corporal Yuan to thank for that," Shi Fa said.
"What did it feel like when your instincts kicked in? You know, for future reference," one of the soldiers asked.

"You know that strange feeling you sometimes get when you're alone and suddenly feel like someone is watching you from afar? It felt something like that," Yuan replied, making up a random explanation on the spot.
"I don't get it... But I'll keep it in mind."
"Are we all ready?" Shi Fa asked them a few moments later.
Everyone nodded.
"Good. Then let's—"
Shi Fa suddenly stopped talking before looking at Yuan.
"Once we go inside, just clear any Void Specter that is in our path."
"Just my specialty," Yuan replied with a smile.
"Then let's go."
Shi Fa entered the burrow first, followed closely by Yuan and the others.

Once inside, the narrow passage widened considerably. What had initially been barely large enough for a single person to squeeze through soon became spacious enough for all seven members of the squad to walk side by side with room to spare.
However, it was incredibly dark inside. The light from the entrance only illuminated the first few meters, while everything beyond was swallowed by pitch-black darkness.
Of course, such darkness posed no obstacle to cultivators like them, whose vision in the dark was just as clear as it was under broad daylight.

It didn't take long for them to encounter Void Specters. After only a few minutes of traversing the tunnel, they came across a group clustered together like a pile of trash, completely blocking the path.
"I got it," Yuan said as he pointed his minigun at them.
"H-Hey... be careful with that thing. We don't want the tunnel to collapse—"
One of the soldiers tried to warn Yuan, but he had already opened fire.

The others instinctively stepped back and prepared to flee. To their surprise, however, every bullet struck the Void Specters with perfect precision before vanishing upon impact, preventing them from piercing through and hitting the tunnel walls.
"Hm? What were you saying?" Yuan asked the soldier after clearing the tunnel.
"N-Nothing..."
Shi Fa chuckled and said, "They don't call him the Cleaning Maniac without reason. Anyway, let's continue."

As they continued deeper into the tunnel, Shi Fa said to Yuan, "I know you like to clean alone, but the Void Specters are much tougher in here than outside. When you start feeling tired, let us know."
Yuan nodded.
"I know."

Knowing just how abnormal an existence Yuan was, Shi Fa didn't doubt him for a moment and immediately instructed the squad to head in the direction he had indicated.
One... two... three...
Five more hours passed without the slightest reaction from Shi Fa's device.
Just as he began to doubt Yuan's instincts, however, the device suddenly vibrated, and a red arrow appeared on its screen, pointing in the very direction they were already heading.
"A-A tunnel!
There's a tunnel up ahead!" Shi Fa announced to the others, his voice sounding a little shaken.
He turned to look at Yuan, who remained silent, but there was a smile hanging on his lips that said 'I told you so'.
Another hour later, they finally arrived at their destination—a cave-like burrow that descended deep underground.
"I can't believe we found one so quickly," said one of the soldiers.
"Right?
It's normal to go weeks without finding one."
"This is likely the fastest tunnel discovery in recent times."
"And we have Corporal Yuan to thank for that," Shi Fa said.
"What did it feel like when your instincts kicked in?
You know, for future reference," one of the soldiers asked.
"You know that strange feeling you sometimes get when you're alone and suddenly feel like someone is watching you from afar?
It felt something like that," Yuan replied, making up a random explanation on the spot.
"I don't get it...
But I'll keep it in mind."
"Are we all ready?" Shi Fa asked them a few moments later.
Everyone nodded.
"Good.
Then let's—"
Shi Fa suddenly stopped talking before looking at Yuan.
"Once we go inside, just clear any Void Specter that is in our path."
"Just my specialty," Yuan replied with a smile.
"Then let's go."
Shi Fa entered the burrow first, followed closely by Yuan and the others.
Once inside, the narrow passage widened considerably.
What had initially been barely large enough for a single person to squeeze through soon became spacious enough for all seven members of the squad to walk side by side with room to spare.
However, it was incredibly dark inside.
The light from the entrance only illuminated the first few meters, while everything beyond was swallowed by pitch-black darkness.
Of course, such darkness posed no obstacle to cultivators like them, whose vision in the dark was just as clear as it was under broad daylight.
It didn't take long for them to encounter Void Specters.
After only a few minutes of traversing the tunnel, they came across a group clustered together like a pile of trash, completely blocking the path.
"I got it," Yuan said as he pointed his minigun at them.
"H-Hey... be careful with that thing.
We don't want the tunnel to collapse—"
One of the soldiers tried to warn Yuan, but he had already opened fire.
The others instinctively stepped back and prepared to flee.
To their surprise, however, every bullet struck the Void Specters with perfect precision before vanishing upon impact, preventing them from piercing through and hitting the tunnel walls.
"Hm?
What were you saying?" Yuan asked the soldier after clearing the tunnel.
"N-Nothing..."
Shi Fa chuckled and said, "They don't call him the Cleaning Maniac without reason.
Anyway, let's continue."
As they continued deeper into the tunnel, Shi Fa said to Yuan, "I know you like to clean alone, but the Void Specters are much tougher in here than outside.
When you start feeling tired, let us know."
Yuan nodded.
"I know."

chapters.title: Chapter 2617 End of the Tunnel
paragraphs: As Yuan and his squad ventured deeper into the tunnel, it gradually widened, and the number of Void Specters they encountered steadily increased.

While the others moved cautiously, Yuan could barely stop himself from rushing forward. The Void Specters within the Red Zone offered several times more Eternal Essence than those in the Orange Zone, not to mention their abundance.
'This place is a treasure trove, and I haven't even encountered any Unknown Crystals yet!' Yuan smiled inwardly.
After spending nearly three hours inside the tunnel, they finally discovered an Unknown Crystal. However, it was embedded deep within the wall.
"So, is there a special process for extracting it, or can I simply yank it out?" Yuan asked as the squad gathered around the crystal.
"Stop! Don't touch it!" Shi Fa hastily said, even though Yuan wasn't even reaching for it.
He quickly explained, "Unlike Unknown Ores, Unknown Crystals contain so much energy that it's dangerous to touch with your bare hands."
"What's the worse that can happen?" Yuan asked out of curiosity.
"You explode like a balloon." Shi Fa responded with a dead seriously expression.
"I see."
Shi Fa retrieved a pair of gloves that had been reinforced with a powerful defensive formation and said, "You can harvest it with this."
After wearing the gloves, Yuan grabbed the crystal and yanked it out of the wall like harvesting a radish.
The Unknown Crystal was double-terminated and roughly the length of an adult's forearm, but most importantly, it contained an immense amount of Eternal Essence.
'This is about a million years' worth of Eternal Essence!' Yuan thought to himself as he quickly absorbed about fifty percent of it to see if it had any changes in its appearance.
After confirming that its appearance remained unchanged, just like the Unknown Ores, Yuan quickly absorbed another thirty percent of its energy.

Although he could have drained it completely, he chose to leave some behind. Unknown Crystals were far rarer and contained much more energy than Unknown Ores, so he would have felt far guiltier than absorbing a few Unknown Ores.
After storing the Unknown Crystal, they continued delving deeper into the tunnel, repeating the process of cleaning Void Specters and harvesting Unknown Crystals.
Four days later...
"Hey, are you really not exhausted?" One of the soldiers suddenly questioned Yuan, as he'd been cleaning thousands of Void Specters alone by this point.
"No.
Yuan clearly answered.
"How the hell is that even possible?"
"I'm starting to understand how he broke all of the Ironwoman's records." Another remarked.
A few more days went by.
"Seriously... there's no way you're not tired by now."
"But I feel fine."
Another week passed in the blink of an eye.
"This tunnel is much deeper than typical."
"That just means there'll be more reward in the end."
"What is the end of a tunnel typically like?" Yuan asked.
"It's usually where the majority of the Unknown Crystals are hidden, but it's protected by a powerful Void Specter. It's not something you can deal with alone, either."
"I see. So like a guardian."
Several more hours later, Yuan suddenly announced, "I can see the end."
"Huh? Really?"
However, even with their divine senses stretched to their limits, none of the others could perceive the end of the tunnel.
Despite their superior cultivation, their soul strength was incomparably weaker than Yuan's, preventing their divine senses from reaching nearly as far.
Eventually, the others also came within range of the tunnel's end, though it took another two hours of travel.
There, they found a pitch-black opening that plunged straight down into the depths.
"There's a good chance we'll be attacked the moment we arrive at the bottom, so remain alert and be ready to use Void Control," Shi Fa said.
"Are we ready?"
Once everyone was ready, Shi Fa moved first, leaping into the hole and vanishing into the darkness below.
Yuan and the others immediately followed.
After falling for several minutes, Yuan spotted a faint light beneath them. It rapidly grew brighter, signaling that they were nearing the bottom.
Soon, they were engulfed by the light and emerged into a massive enclosed cavern. Dozens of Unknown Crystals were embedded throughout the walls, their glow illuminating the entire chamber.
However, at the center of the cavern loomed an enormous Void Specter several times larger than any they had encountered before, its massive form resembling a small mountain.
Just as Shi Fa had predicted, the Void Specter detected their presence almost immediately and launched a barrage of hundreds of tentacles from its massive body.
"Scatter!" Shi Fa shouted.
While everyone else focused on evading the tentacles, Yuan calmly aimed his minigun at the Void Specter.
"Focus on defending yourself! Your bullets will likely be ineffective—"
Before Shi Fa could finish speaking, immense Limitless surged from Yuan's body as the minigun unleashed a relentless storm of bullets, firing tens of thousands every second at the Void Specter below.

The others assumed Yuan was panicking and expected him to exhaust his energy within moments. To their astonishment, however, he continued firing without pause for several minutes, completely overwhelming the Void Specter and riddling it with countless holes until its body ceased to exist.
"W-What just happened...?"
After confirming that the threat had been eliminated, the soldiers turned to Yuan with stupefied expressions, as though they had just witnessed the impossible.

As for Yuan, he completely ignored their stares and focused on absorbing the Eternal Essence left behind by the Void Specter. There was so much of it that, for once, he had to sit down and cultivate properly to absorb all of it.
The others didn't question it since they figured that he'd exhausted himself and needed to rest.
"L-Let's stop standing around and harvest the Unknown Crystals before the tunnel collapses," Shi Fa spoke after snapping out of his daze a moment later.
Shi Fa's voice snapped the others out of their daze, and they quickly started harvesting the Unknown Crystals while Yuan continued his cultivation.

chapters.title: Chapter 2618 Ironwoman
paragraphs: "I know we all just watched it happen right before our very eyes, but I still cannot believe that he'd managed to defeat a Void Guardian all by himself..." one of the soldiers remarked as he harvested the Unknown Crystals.
"I know exactly how you feel. It was such a surreal experience, especially considering that it normally takes a whole squad several hours to defeat one."
"It was pretty amazing, but it's not unprecedented. The Ironwoman defeated a Void Guardian by herself last year, too."
"Can you really compare the two of them? The Ironwoman has been in the military for many years now, while Corporal Yuan just joined!"
"Right? Don't downplay Corporal Yuan's achievement! Not even the Ironwoman was defeating Void Guardians by herself as a new soldier!"
"By the way, what do you think he's doing? I've never seen anyone sit in such a strange position before," one of the soldiers suddenly asked, referring to Yuan's lotus position.
"Isn't he just resting?"
"Is he? It feels like he's doing something more than that."
A few minutes later, Yuan opened his eyes and drew a deep breath.

'What a remarkable harvest. To think such an easy target would provide me with more than a billion years' worth of Eternal Essence,' he thought as he turned toward the others, who were collecting the last few Unknown Crystals.
Once every Unknown Crystal in the cavern had been collected, the squad gathered around Yuan.
"Let's leave as soon as possible. The tunnel usually collapses about a week after its guardian is defeated," Shi Fa said.
"Sure. Let me carry some of those Unknown Crystals as well," Yuan offered.
However, Shi Fa shook his head. "You've already done more than enough. Take it easy from here on and leave the chores to us."
"Just let me carry them for a little—until we reach outside. If I stay idle for too long, my hands start to itch," Yuan insisted.
"Fine..."
Shi Fa sighed as he handed Yuan about thirty Unknown Crystals.
As they climbed the tunnel and traveled back to the surface, Yuan absorbed some of the Eternal Essence from the Unknown Crystals.
Since he'd already absorbed plenty from the Void Guardian, Yuan decided not to absorb too much, only between twenty-five and sixty percent from each crystal, ensuring there was no obvious pattern.
Once they left the tunnel and returned to the surface, they immediately started making their way back to the city.
Upon returning to the city, Shi Fa collected all of the Unknown Crystals and said, "Thanks for the hard work, everyone, especially you, Corporal Yuan."
"This mission ended much faster than it normally would, and it's thanks to Corporal Yuan.
"Not only was it fast, but it was relatively relaxing."
"If you ever want to do another mission, you can contact me."
"Me too!"
"You want to lower the chances of encountering a shitbag, after all."
"A shitbag?" Yuan repeated with a questioning expression.
"To keep things simple, they are soldiers you don't want to go on missions with because they will make things more difficult for everyone."
"I'll keep that in mind, but if you want to do another mission with me, I don't mind."
"Oh? When?"
"Right now."
"Hahaha! Yeah, right." The soldiers laughed, assuming Yuan was merely joking.
"Good one, Corporal Yuan. But seriously, contact us the next time you want to take another mission."
The soldiers departed shortly afterward.
"See you next time." Shi Fa said, being the last to leave.
Unbeknownst to them, however, Yuan hadn't been joking. The moment they all left, he headed straight to the mission hall to accept another assignment.
<Request has been sent>
<Request has been approved>
[Mission Details: Gather Unknown Crystals in the Red Zone. Meet at the Northern Gate at 0800 in 13 hours]
The following day, Yuan left the city with his new squad and began his mission.
"Hm? He's already gone on another mission?" Mei Feng stared at the report before her with a dumbfounded expression. She had never encountered anyone so motivated—or so obsessed with taking missions.

"If he continues at this pace, he'll likely be promoted to Sergeant within a year..." She paused briefly before adding, "No, considering he has already completed a Red Zone mission, no one would question me even if I promoted him right now."
Suddenly, another voice rang out. "Keeping such close tabs on him... You really like this guy, don't you?"
"Are you jealous? I did the same thing with you when you first joined," Mei Feng replied calmly, turning toward the woman lounging lazily on the couch in her office.
"Since you're here, tell me what you think about him," Mei Feng said after a moment of silence. "I know you're also interested in him, 'Ironwoman'."
"I don't know what you want me to say, but I think he's someone with a lot of secrets," said the Ironwoman.
"Care to elaborate?"
"Remember his fight with Captain Gu during the recruitment?"
"Of course. You saved him."
"Who? Corporal Yuan?" The Ironwoman chuckled. "That man didn't need any saving. If I saved anything that day, it would be Captain Gu's reputation."
"What...?" Mei Feng muttered, her expression filled with bewilderment.
"That man was more than capable of defeating Captain Gu, yet he deliberately chose to lose. It's not something you'd expect from someone who appears so carefree and unrestrained."
"Where'd you find someone like that, anyway?"
"I didn't." Mei Feng shook her head before revealing the truth. "It was my daughter who found him."
"Oh?"
"Then..."
"Don't bother trying." Mei Feng suddenly interrupted. "I won't reveal any more information about him, even if it's you... No... especially because it's you."
"What are you worried about? That I might try and steal him from you?" The Ironwoman chuckled.
"No, not you. Your family."
The Ironwoman fell silent for a moment before speaking again, "Then you have even less of a reason to worry, as I haven't spoken to them since coming to this city."
"Anyway, enough about me. Although I don't know Corporal Yuan well enough to say for certain, he doesn't strike me as the type of person who would betray others."
"I already know that," Mei Feng said.
"Then why even ask me?"
"I wanted to see if you had any thoughts about adding him to your squad."
"My squad?" The Ironwoman mumbled with her eyebrows raised.

chapters.title: Chapter 2619 Ten Minutes Head Start
paragraphs: "You want to add Corporal Yuan to my squad? Did I hear you correctly?" The Ironwoman asked with a surprised look on her face.
"I'm just asking since you have full authority over your squad members. He has more than enough talent. Hell, if we're being honest, he's even more talented than you."

Ironwoman shook her head and said, "This isn't about talent alone. I admit that he is more talented than me—and everyone in my squad. However, his achievements are too lacking, and all he has on his record are some cleanup missions and two gathering missions. My squad specializes in extreme missions that most soldiers don't even know exist."

"I am well aware of that, but give him some time. It hasn't even been half a year since he joined. And although he started out slow, he's been picking things up lately. I wouldn't be surprised if he starts doing missions in the Purple Zone within five years."
"When and if he gets to that point, I'll consider it. But right now, he doesn't qualify."
A few days have passed since Yuan started his second mission in the Red Zone, and just as before, he led his squad to a tunnel using his instincts as an excuse.
"We really found a tunnel... I will never doubt you again, Corporal Yuan!" said the squad leader, who refused to listen to Yuan in the beginning and needed some convincing.
"Then, as promised, we'll clear the tunnel my way," Yuan said, as he'd made a bet with the squad leader on whether or not he'd find a tunnel.
"Of course. You'll enter alone, and we'll follow you after ten minutes."
"Good. Make sure to harvest any Unknown Crystals you see," Yuan reminded them before entering the tunnel alone.
Half a minute after Yuan disappeared into the tunnel, one of the soldiers asked, "Should we really let him go inside alone?"
"That's what he wants."
"What if he dies? That would look terrible for the rest of us, regardless of whether it was his request or not."
"I heard that General Mei had personally recruited him. If he dies..."
"Relax. It's only ten minutes. What the hell could he possibly do alone in such a short time?" said the squad leader.
Ten minutes later, the squad of six soldiers entered the tunnel.
"Looks like he cleaned up some of the Void Specters," one of the soldiers remarked when they traveled for half an hour without seeing a single Void Specter.
An hour later...
"I don't think we'll catch up to him if we keep moving at this pace. Let's pick up the speed," the squad leader suggested, and the others readily agreed.
The squad immediately started running forward, though they remained vigilant as they advanced.
However, even after several hours of nonstop running—with only occasional stops to harvest nearby Unknown Ores—the soldiers still failed to catch up to Yuan.
"How much farther ahead is he?! And how the hell is he clearing the Void Specters while still maintaining such a lead?!"
The soldiers could hardly believe it.
"Doesn't he wield a minigun? How does he even have enough energy to deal with so many Void Specters alone?"
"He's quite famous for that, actually."

Three more days passed without them encountering a single Void Specter or catching even a glimpse of Yuan. By this point, their initial shock had transformed into awe, accompanied by a faint sense of fear toward his unfathomable capabilities.
"I can see the end of the tunnel!" The squad leader announced.
"He's not here, either! Don't tell me that he went to face the Void Guardian alone?!"
The soldiers were expecting Yuan to wait for them at the end of the tunnel before facing the Void Guardian together.
"I underestimated his arrogance and recklessness! Let's hurry and hope he isn't dead already!"
The soldiers quickly steeled themselves before leaping into the hole and descending toward the chamber where the Void Guardian awaited.
When they finally emerged into the chamber, they expected to find Yuan locked in a fierce battle with the Void Guardian—or the creature alone after having already killed him.
What none of them expected, however, was to see Yuan standing there by himself, with the Void Guardian nowhere in sight.
"W-What's going on? Where's the Void Guardian?" The soldiers surveyed the chamber with dumbfounded expressions.
"Don't tell me there was no Void Guardian..." one of the soldiers muttered.
"A tunnel without a Void Guardian? That's never happened before.
"What happened, Corporal Yuan? Was the place already empty when you arrived?" the squad leader asked, turning to Yuan—the only person who could explain what had occurred.
"The Void Guardian? There was one, but I defeated it right before you all arrived," he responded in a calm voice, acting like what he'd done was nothing out of the ordinary.
"YOU WHAT?!"
The soldiers exclaimed simultaneously, their eyes popping out of their sockets in shock.
"Y-You defeated a Void Guardian... all by yourself?" the squad leader muttered in a daze.

As difficult as it was to believe Yuan, there was no other plausible explanation. A Void Guardian had never been absent while the chamber still contained Unknown Crystals, especially when it remained filled with them, as if nobody had touched them.
Eventually, the soldiers snapped out of their daze and harvested the Unknown Crystals while Yuan rested.
"We're done."
The squad gathered by Yuan some time later.
"Alright. Let's leave."
Yuan did not need to absorb the Eternal Essence since he'd already done so long before they arrived at the scene.
After they returned to the military base, Yuan asked them, "Since we're already here, want to go on another mission?"
The soldiers could only stare at him in silence, looking like they'd just heard something absurd.
"Even if you're being serious... I am mentally exhausted and need to rest."
"Me too."
The soldiers politely declined Yuan's offer before going their separate ways.
Yuan didn't mind and calmly made his way to the mission hall again.

sentences.text: "You want to add Corporal Yuan to my squad?
Did I hear you correctly?" The Ironwoman asked with a surprised look on her face.
"I'm just asking since you have full authority over your squad members.
He has more than enough talent.
Hell, if we're being honest, he's even more talented than you."
Ironwoman shook her head and said, "This isn't about talent alone.
I admit that he is more talented than me—and everyone in my squad.
However, his achievements are too lacking, and all he has on his record are some cleanup missions and two gathering missions.
My squad specializes in extreme missions that most soldiers don't even know exist."
"I am well aware of that, but give him some time.
It hasn't even been half a year since he joined.
And although he started out slow, he's been picking things up lately.
I wouldn't be surprised if he starts doing missions in the Purple Zone within five years."
"When and if he gets to that point, I'll consider it.
But right now, he doesn't qualify."
A few days have passed since Yuan started his second mission in the Red Zone, and just as before, he led his squad to a tunnel using his instincts as an excuse.
"We really found a tunnel...
I will never doubt you again, Corporal Yuan!" said the squad leader, who refused to listen to Yuan in the beginning and needed some convincing.
"Then, as promised, we'll clear the tunnel my way," Yuan said, as he'd made a bet with the squad leader on whether or not he'd find a tunnel.
"Of course.
You'll enter alone, and we'll follow you after ten minutes."
"Good.
Make sure to harvest any Unknown Crystals you see," Yuan reminded them before entering the tunnel alone.
Half a minute after Yuan disappeared into the tunnel, one of the soldiers asked, "Should we really let him go inside alone?"
"That's what he wants."
"What if he dies?
That would look terrible for the rest of us, regardless of whether it was his request or not."
"I heard that General Mei had personally recruited him.
If he dies..."
"Relax.
It's only ten minutes.
What the hell could he possibly do alone in such a short time?" said the squad leader.
Ten minutes later, the squad of six soldiers entered the tunnel.
"Looks like he cleaned up some of the Void Specters," one of the soldiers remarked when they traveled for half an hour without seeing a single Void Specter.
An hour later...
"I don't think we'll catch up to him if we keep moving at this pace.
Let's pick up the speed," the squad leader suggested, and the others readily agreed.
The squad immediately started running forward, though they remained vigilant as they advanced.
However, even after several hours of nonstop running—with only occasional stops to harvest nearby Unknown Ores—the soldiers still failed to catch up to Yuan.
"How much farther ahead is he?!
And how the hell is he clearing the Void Specters while still maintaining such a lead?!"
The soldiers could hardly believe it.
"Doesn't he wield a minigun?
How does he even have enough energy to deal with so many Void Specters alone?"
"He's quite famous for that, actually."
Three more days passed without them encountering a single Void Specter or catching even a glimpse of Yuan.
By this point, their initial shock had transformed into awe, accompanied by a faint sense of fear toward his unfathomable capabilities.
"I can see the end of the tunnel!" The squad leader announced.
"He's not here, either!
Don't tell me that he went to face the Void Guardian alone?!"
The soldiers were expecting Yuan to wait for them at the end of the tunnel before facing the Void Guardian together.
"I underestimated his arrogance and recklessness!
Let's hurry and hope he isn't dead already!"
The soldiers quickly steeled themselves before leaping into the hole and descending toward the chamber where the Void Guardian awaited.
When they finally emerged into the chamber, they expected to find Yuan locked in a fierce battle with the Void Guardian—or the creature alone after having already killed him.
What none of them expected, however, was to see Yuan standing there by himself, with the Void Guardian nowhere in sight.
"W-What's going on?
Where's the Void Guardian?" The soldiers surveyed the chamber with dumbfounded expressions.
"Don't tell me there was no Void Guardian..." one of the soldiers muttered.
"A tunnel without a Void Guardian?
That's never happened before.
"What happened, Corporal Yuan?
Was the place already empty when you arrived?" the squad leader asked, turning to Yuan—the only person who could explain what had occurred.
"The Void Guardian?
There was one, but I defeated it right before you all arrived," he responded in a calm voice, acting like what he'd done was nothing out of the ordinary.
"YOU WHAT?!"
The soldiers exclaimed simultaneously, their eyes popping out of their sockets in shock.
"Y-You defeated a Void Guardian... all by yourself?" the squad leader muttered in a daze.
As difficult as it was to believe Yuan, there was no other plausible explanation.
A Void Guardian had never been absent while the chamber still contained Unknown Crystals, especially when it remained filled with them, as if nobody had touched them.
Eventually, the soldiers snapped out of their daze and harvested the Unknown Crystals while Yuan rested.
"We're done."
The squad gathered by Yuan some time later.
"Alright.
Let's leave."
Yuan did not need to absorb the Eternal Essence since he'd already done so long before they arrived at the scene.
After they returned to the military base, Yuan asked them, "Since we're already here, want to go on another mission?"
The soldiers could only stare at him in silence, looking like they'd just heard something absurd.
"Even if you're being serious...
I am mentally exhausted and need to rest."
"Me too."
The soldiers politely declined Yuan's offer before going their separate ways.
Yuan didn't mind and calmly made his way to the mission hall again.

chapters.title: Chapter 2620 Growing In Reputation
paragraphs: Unlike Yuan's first squad, the soldiers from his second mission made no attempt to keep quiet about his capabilities.
As soon as they saw their friends, they began spreading word of everything that had happened, revealing that Yuan had practically cleared an entire tunnel by himself—including its Void Guardian.

Of course, few people believed such an outrageous rumor. In their eyes, no matter how talented Yuan was, he had only recently joined the military and had spent most of his time completing cleanup missions. There was simply no way someone so inexperienced could already clear an entire tunnel and defeat its Void Guardian all by himself.

"Come on, man. You'd have to be insane to believe such a fairytale. Even the Ironwoman had only managed to defeat a Void Guardian by herself a year ago, and she'd been in the military for over a decade!"

"I know very well what Corporal Yuan is capable of, considering I've accompanied him on a cleanup mission before. As much credit as I'm willing to give him, there's no way he has already reached a level where he can defeat a Void Guardian by himself."
"Who the hell is spreading these rumors? If a mere Corporal can defeat a Void Guardian by himself, I can defeat the Void Hunter by myself!"
However, even though the majority of soldiers did not believe the rumors, a few did.
"Where's Corporal Yuan?" Sergeant Bing asked Sergeant Quang.
"I haven't heard from him since his first mission in the Red Zone."
"Don't tell me that he already went on another mission?"
"It's very likely..."
A little over a week later, Yuan returned from his third mission. Once again, his squad members eagerly spread word of his achievements among their friends.
"What's with that disappointed look?" one of the soldiers asked after noticing his friend's reaction to the story.

"Do you have any idea how many times I've heard that rumor? It's been spreading for over a week now! At this point, there's probably nobody who hasn't heard it already, so you can stop exaggerating," the soldier's friend said, explaining his frustration.
"What are you talking about?"
Having been away on a mission the entire time, the soldier had no idea about the rumor, nor the fact that Yuan joined their mission literally right after his last one.
"How could it have been circulating for a week when we literally just returned from the mission?
"Huh? What do you mean?"

The soldier then explained that he had just completed a mission with Yuan and that everything he had said had happened during that very mission—not the one everyone had been talking about for the past week.
"What?! Are you serious?!"
"You don't believe me? You can ask the others!"
Thus, the rumor began spreading once more. This time, with a second squad corroborating the story, it became far more credible.
Shortly afterward, a third squad came forward and revealed that they had actually been the first to witness Yuan defeat a Void Guardian by himself.
"G-General! Have you heard of the rumors about Corporal Yuan yet?"
An officer asked General Mei over the phone.
"You're the sixth person to call me about this today," Mei Feng sighed.
"Do you think it's true?"
"Well, I'd certainly rather believe it than assume more than twenty soldiers conspired to lie and exaggerate Corporal Yuan's achievements."
"What if it's one of General Gu's schemes?" the officer asked.

"And what would he possibly gain from such a scheme? Making the other soldiers jealous of Yuan—or provoking them into targeting him? Also, half of the soldiers spreading the rumors are from my division."

"Are you going to do something about this?" the officer suddenly asked. "You should already be aware of how many officers are trying to recruit him into their squad. The only reason they haven't approached him yet is because of your influence. However, if his reputation continues to grow at this rate, they may decide to disregard you and try to recruit him themselves."

"So what?" Mei Feng replied calmly. "It's not like I have a squad for him to join. Whatever Corporal Yuan chooses to do as a soldier is no longer my concern—as long as he doesn't side with General Gu, not that I can imagine him ever doing so.
Meanwhile, several officers sat inside General Gu's office, each wearing a solemn, contemplative expression.
"If these rumors are true—that Corporal Yuan can already defeat a Void Guardian by himself—our initial plan to lure him into the Red Zone wouldn't work on him," one of them eventually sighed aloud.

"Then we adjust the plan! If the Red Zone won't do, we'll take him out in the Purple Zone! And if that doesn't work out, there's still the Black Zone!" General Gu shouted as he angrily slammed his desk.
"While you're all wasting your time here, that bastard is improving at an unfathomable pace! At this rate, he'll become so powerful that even we cannot touch him!"
"W-We can act swiftly, but that would be extremely risky—"
"I don't give a fuck anymore! We need to stop him from growing, or he'll become another thorn in my path like that Ironwoman!"
After a moment of silence, one of the officers said, "I understand. I'll expedite the plans and get rid of him as soon as possible."
While Yuan's reputation within the military continued to soar, he himself had gone on another mission, starting his fourth.
"Is it true? That you can clear a tunnel and defeat the Void Guardian by yourself?"
The soldiers in his squad asked him before they departed the city.
Yuan calmly nodded.
"So you can just sit back and let me do all of the work," he said with a smile.
The soldiers exchanged dumbfounded gazes with each other.
Suddenly, one of them asked, "If you don't mind me asking... why do you insist on doing all of the work by yourself? Even if you're capable, it doesn't make sense to push yourself this hard."
"It's quite simple, actually." Yuan faced the soldiers and responded with a serious expression, "Because it's much safer and faster if I do it alone."

chapters.title: Chapter 2621 Corporal Yuan
paragraphs: "Safer? How is it safer?" one of the soldiers couldn't help but ask.
"I have heard from others that deaths are not uncommon when fighting the Void Guardian," Yuan said. "Since I can defeat them alone, why risk others' lives?"
"But wouldn't that just put your own life at risk?"
Although the soldiers were grateful that Yuan cared enough about their safety to endanger himself, the thought of him doing so still didn't sit right with them.
Yuan chuckled and said, "My life is not at risk. I can fight a dozen of them alone if I wanted to, let alone a single one."
The soldiers' jaw dropped to the ground at his arrogant claims, but they decided not to comment on it.
They left the city shortly afterward and began their mission.
Meanwhile, inside the facility that extracted Unknown Ores and Unknown Crystals for energy, a group of individuals gathered to discuss a certain issue.

"So, the anomaly isn't limited to Unknown Ores, and even some of the newer Unknown Crystals have been found to be missing some of their energy," one of them muttered in a troubled tone as a small mountain of Unknown Cores and Unknown Crystals lay piled on the table before them.
"Are the Unknown Crystals truly missing energy? What if they're simply of lower quality? Not every Unknown Crystal contains the same amount of energy, after all," someone asked.

"Did you even read the report before coming here? They aren't missing just a small amount of energy. Most have lost at least twenty-five percent, while some are missing more than half of what they would normally contain! The discrepancy is far too great to dismiss as a difference in quality!"
"Are these all the affected ores and crystals?"
"They are... so far. The amount may seem insignificant for now, but if we fail to identify the cause and the anomaly continues to spread, we could be facing a catastrophe in the near future."
"Have we learned anything about this anomaly yet? Could it simply be a natural phenomenon? If that's the case, I'm not sure there's anything we can do about it."
"Not yet. However, we have discovered a coincidence—or a connection."
One of the individuals snapped her fingers, causing a screen to materialize before the group. Displayed on the projection was the profile of a certain individual.
"Corporal Yuan?" another individual read aloud, a puzzled look crossing his face.

"After discovering the anomaly, we began tracing the origins of the affected resources. According to the records, every one of them was collected by soldiers during missions, and Corporal Yuan was the only one who had participated in all of said missions."
"That is certainly suspicious."
"Wait until you hear more about this Corporal Yuan..."
The screen flickered, revealing more detailed information about him.
As the individuals examined the new information, their expressions gradually shifted from curiosity to disbelief.
"As you can see for yourself, there's practically no information about him, except that he'd joined the military a few months ago and broke multiple records during his recruitment."
"No records before joining the military? It's like... he materialized out of thin air..."
"Look at those data! There's no way someone this talented could be a nobody! I'm willing to bet that someone erased his data to keep his identity a secret."
"Haven't we seen something like this before?"

"You mean the Ironwoman? She's a different story. Her information wasn't erased, but sealed. There's a big difference. Also, nobody has the authority to completely erase an individual's background from the system."
"I beg to differ." Someone said. "There is one person who can do that—the one who made the system."
The room suddenly fell silent.
"Are you suggesting that Gaia is responsible for erasing Corporal Yuan's information? Why would they do something like that?"
"You already know that no one but Gaia could answer that question."
"So, are we supposed to assume that Corporal Yuan is somehow connected to Gaia now?"
"What? Of course not. There's no evidence that—"
"There is, though. Corporal Yuan's lackluster record that looks like it'd been deliberately cleaned."
"That's just an assumption."
"It's also an assumption that he has anything to do with the anomaly. We can't go around accusing someone like that, especially if they're connected with General Mei."
"Speaking of General Mei, looks like she recruited him... just like she recruited the Ironwoman."
"Must be a coincidence. That woman attracts the strangest but also the most talented people, after all."
"In the end, it all points to Gaia.
"Then how should we proceed with this new information?"
"If Gaia is truly already involved, then there's nothing for us to do."

"Haa..." The most senior there sighed while rubbing her eyes. "In any case, since we still lack concrete evidence that Corporal Yuan is connected with the anomaly, we will continue monitoring the situation and Corporal Yuan closely."
The meeting ended shortly after with no real progress.
"Corporal Yuan, huh? Just who are you... and where did you come from?"
A week later, Yuan returned from his fourth mission.
"My lord, Corporal Yuan! You're even more capable than the rumors give you credit!"
The soldiers in his squad praised him as they returned to the military base.
"If you ever want to go on another mission, don't hesitate to find me!"
"Sure."
Yuan didn't bother trying to ask them to go on another mission this time.
The squad disbanded shortly afterward.
Instead of heading straight to the mission hall to accept another assignment as one would expect, Yuan made his way to the training hall.
Of course, he wanted to see how much closer he'd gotten to defeating the entity on the 46th floor.
A few hours and many attempts later, Yuan emerged from the training hall.

'Although I am still nowhere near defeating it, I can at least see clear progress. If I continue defeating Void Guardians and absorbing energy from Unknown Crystals, it won't be long before I have enough Eternal Essence to conquer it!' Yuan thought to himself as he made his way toward the mission hall.

chapters.title: Chapter 2622 A New Mission
paragraphs: When Yuan arrived at the mission hall, he immediately noticed that nearly everyone inside was glaring at him.
Of course, there was no malice behind their stares. They were simply curious and a little awestruck to finally see Corporal Yuan, who had been a hot topic lately.
"Is that him?"
"Yep. That's the Cleaning Maniac."
"This might sound strange, but he looks... out of place. Like he doesn't belong here."
"I know what you mean. He's practically a monster walking among humans."
"No, I mean something about him feels otherworldly."
The soldiers chatted among themselves without pause, yet for some reason, not a single one dared to approach Yuan.
Eventually, just as Yuan was about to reach the machines to accept a mission, several soldiers finally gathered the courage to approach him.
However, before they could reach him, another group suddenly cut them off.
"Hey, watch where you're—" The soldier who had been shoved aside was about to curse, but the words died in his throat the moment he saw their faces and recognized who they were.
Then, without a word, they backed away and silently watched as this group of soldiers approached Yuan.
"Are you Corporal Yuan?"
The group consisted of five individuals, and the one who addressed him was a tall, broad-shouldered man.
Yuan turned toward them. "Who's asking?"
The man frowned. "Is that any way to speak to your superior?"
Yuan glanced at the insignia on the man's chest. Two black bars. It was the same rank that Captain Gu had.
However, before Yuan could respond, another soldier from the group stepped forward with a friendly smile.
"There's no need to be so tense. I'm Captain Chen, and this large, stern-looking fellow is Captain Dung. You don't need to be overly formal with us, either."
"In that case... what do you want from me?"
"We have a proposition for you, but it's not something we can talk about here. Can we go somewhere more quiet?
"Can it wait until I grab my mission?" Yuan asked.
Captain Chen chuckled and said, "You won't even care about your mission once you hear what we have in store for you."
"Is that so?"
After pondering for a moment, Yuan nodded.
"Sure, let's go."
Captain Chen wasn't expecting Yuan to agree so readily, but he remained calm and said, "Follow us."
Once Yuan left with the group, the soldiers began mumbling to each other.
"Wasn't that...?"
"I wonder what sort of business they have with Corporal Yuan."
"They're probably going to confirm the rumors."
"You mean whether he can really defeat a Void Guardian by himself or not?"
Meanwhile, after leaving the mission hall, Yuan followed Captain Chen and the other four soldiers to a private room.
"Before I reveal our offer to you, I must ask you something. I heard that you've been doing missions nonstop. Is there a reason you're working so hard?" Captain Chen asked Yuan.
"To receive fast promotions, of course."
"Is it really so simple?"
"Why else would I be doing so many missions? Isn't it the goal of every soldier to raise their ranks?" Yuan shrugged.
"Fair enough, as I was once just like you." Captain Chen gave a hearty laugh. "Anyway, let's get to the point."
"Corporal Yuan, how would you like to join us on a mission?"
"I'm listening," Yuan responded, looking like his interest was piqued.

"It's a gathering mission, similar to the ones you've been doing, but on a much larger scale, and it will take place in the Purple Zone. If you want to receive fast promotions, then you can only go above and beyond."
"The Purple Zone, huh? That does sound interesting... However, don't I need to pass an exam before I can accept missions there, as I did for the Red Zone?" Yuan asked.
"Normally, yes. However, with the approval and supervision of at least three captains, you can receive special permission to enter the Purple Zone, and as you can see, there are five of us here."

Yuan pondered for a moment before asking, "May I ask why you're inviting a mere corporal like me to join your mission? If you're short on members, surely there are plenty of more qualified soldiers available."

"To be honest, we've heard a lot of stories about you, and we'd like to see for ourselves if they're true. More importantly, we want to find out where your limits truly lie. If you're worried about the danger, don't be. We'll make sure nothing happens to you."
Yuan closed his eyes and seemed to be pondering again.

"I was waiting for you to say that." Yuan opened his eyes and said with a smile. "When do we start?"
"We can leave for the mission right now."
"Then what are we waiting for? Let's get started!" Yuan exclaimed excitedly, showing a level of impatience that might lead one to think it was his first mission.
"Alright. Then let's leave for the mission now."

Upon reaching the gate, they headed straight for the teleporter, bypassing the soldiers stationed there.
This was a first for Yuan, as the guards normally checked the identity of everyone in the squad and their mission details before allowing them to use the teleporter.

Seeing this, Yuan confirmed his suspicions.
'Looks like they've finally decided to act,' he smiled inwardly, as he'd been waiting for this opportunity.

Despite knowing full well that he was walking into a trap, Yuan stepped into it willingly—even gleefully. After all, this opportunity would allow him to enter the Purple Zone far sooner than he had anticipated.
