chapters.title: Chapter 2623 Scorpion Squad
paragraphs: "Say that again for me."
A deep frown formed on Mei Feng's face when she heard the news.

"T-There have been reports that several officers under General Gu approached Corporal Yuan in the mission hall and took him somewhere. We're currently trying to locate them," one of Mei Feng's officers reported after barging into her office.
After a moment of silence, Mei Feng turned her gaze toward Sergeant Bing and Sergeant Quang, who were also in the room, their heads lowered, as if trying to hide the shame on their faces.
"Where were the two of you when that happened?" Mei Feng asked them in a calm yet cold voice.
"We have no excuses," Sergeant Quang said as he raised his head to look at Mei Feng with a resolute face, as if he accepted his fate.

Sergeant Bing spoke up a moment later. "I'm not trying to make excuses, but Corporal Yuan always heads straight to the mission hall after returning from a mission. We never expected them to make a move in such a crowded, public place. Besides, we usually don't even learn that he's back until he's already accepted and left for another mission."
Mei Feng rubbed her eyes and sighed. "As much as I want to blame you, I can't ignore my own complacency. I should have seen this coming, especially after his reputation began rising so rapidly."
She had already known that General Gu felt threatened by Yuan's talent. Once Yuan's reputation started soaring, she should have anticipated that General Gu would eventually make a move.
"And for it to be the Scorpion Squad... It's like they don't even care about hiding their intentions..." Mei Feng sighed again.
"Did you say the Scorpion Squad?!" Sergeant Bing exclaimed in shock.
The Scorpion Squad was infamous for its ruthlessness. Its members constantly disregarded regulations and were widely regarded as nothing more than a band of troublemakers.
However, because they were talented and came from influential backgrounds, none of them had experienced any real accountability, especially with General Gu protecting them.
Suddenly, someone knocked on the door and spoke loudly from outside, "General! I have information on Corporal Yuan's whereabouts!"
"Enter!
Once the soldier was inside, he revealed that some soldiers witnessed Corporal Yuan at the northern gate.
"Some even claimed they saw Corporal Yuan using the teleporter!"
Hearing this, Mei Feng immediately searched the system to determine whether Yuan had officially accepted a mission. As she had expected, however, no such record existed.
"Bring the soldiers from the northern gate to me for questioning!" Mei Feng commanded the soldier.
"Yes!"

"They must have lured Corporal Yuan outside the city. However, I doubt they'd be foolish enough to kill him outright. They'll most likely try to make his death look like an accident," said the other officer in the room.
Mei Feng turned to her and said, "Discreetly dispatch several squads to search for Corporal Yuan. If my guess is correct, they're likely headed to the Purple Zone."
Then, she stood up and started walking toward the door.
"Where are you going?"
"A little chat with General Gu. You can bring the soldiers on duty to his office," she said before disappearing entirely.
"I'd like to volunteer for the search," Sergeant Quang said to the officer.
"Me too," said Sergeant Bing.
"Even if you didn't ask, I would've sent you so."
While Sergeant Quang and Bing prepared for their mission, Mei Feng went to General Gu's office.
When the guards saw Mei Feng, they said nothing and silently stepped aside, allowing her to enter General Gu's office.
However, unlike her previous visit, Mei Feng did not enter calmly. She kicked the door off its hinges, startling everyone inside.
"G-General Mei?! What are you doing?!"
"Even if you're a General, you can't just barge in here like a bandit!"
General Gu was not alone in the office, and several other officers were present.
"What brings you here this time, General Mei?" General Gu greeted her calmly, as though he had been expecting her arrival.
"You know damn well why I am here," she responded as she walked into the room, ignoring the others. "Where did you take Corporal Yuan?"
"You're making it sound as though I had him kidnapped." General Gu raised an eyebrow, appearing genuinely puzzled by the accusation.
"Numerous witnesses saw the Scorpion Squad take Corporal Yuan out on an unauthorized mission."

"An unauthorized mission? How can you be certain they're even on one? And even if they are, I fail to see why that warrants such concern—much less why you would assume I ordered them to abduct him. They may belong to my division, but they are also officers with the authority to bring soldiers on missions at their own discretion."

"As we're all likely aware, Corporal Yuan has become quite the topic of discussion lately. I wouldn't be surprised if they took him to a tunnel to see for themselves whether he can truly defeat a Void Guardian alone. Besides, with five captains accompanying him, I highly doubt anything will happen."

Mei Feng sneered. "If a group of notorious troublemakers secretly taking away a talent you failed to recruit—and nearly killed during the recruitment—isn't enough to warrant my concern, then I don't know what is."

General Gu shook his head and sighed. "That is another serious accusation, General Mei. I understand that you're still upset about what happened during the recruitment, but Captain Gu had no intention of killing him."

He continued, "And while I admit that the Scorpion Squad has earned a certain degree of infamy, that alone does not justify treating them like criminals. Moreover, they have been making an effort to improve their behavior lately, and their increasingly positive reputation is proof that they genuinely wish to change for the better."

Suddenly, another officer in the room spoke up. "General Gu is right, General Mei. At this point, you're merely hurling baseless accusations. Unless you have solid evidence that supports your claim, please leave for now and allow us to finish our meeting that you'd so brazenly disturbed."
One might have assumed that everyone present supported General Gu, but in truth, many of the officers remained neutral and had taken neither side.
However, their presence there was not a coincidence.

chapters.title: Chapter 2624 Purple Zone
paragraphs: "I've heard your concerns, General Mei, and I will personally look into the matter. For now, I must ask that you leave us," General Gu said solemnly. "Unless, of course, you intend to threaten me as you did before."
However, Mei Feng made no move to leave. Moments later, the guards stationed at the northern gate were escorted into the office.
"What is it now?" General Gu sighed.

"These soldiers were on duty when the Scorpion Squad escorted Corporal Yuan out of the city. I would like to know why they ignored protocol and allowed them to leave without verifying their identities and mission details."
"Well? What do you soldiers have to say for yourselves?" General Gu turned to the guards.
The soldiers immediately lowered their heads.
"W-We were in the wrong! We were slacking off and did not bother to verify their identities!"
"And... they were all officers with well-established reputations..."
Rather than making excuses or attempting to lie, they openly admitted their negligence and accepted responsibility.

General Gu turned to Mei Feng and said, "It's not as though this is the first time soldiers have grown complacent and neglected their duties. It was simply an unfortunate coincidence that it happened under these circumstances."
He continued, "I'll personally see that they're punished accordingly. Of course, if it would ease your concerns, I'm willing to let you decide their punishment yourself."
"Don't worry. I'll make sure they receive the harshest punishment permitted, so others will think twice before making the same mistake," Mei Feng said before turning toward the destroyed doorway.
Just as she reached the exit, she stopped.
"If anything happens to Corporal Yuan..."
However, she left the threat unfinished and walked away.
Once Mei Feng's presence could no longer be sensed, the officers in the room turned toward General Gu with perplexed expressions.

Although they agreed that Mei Feng lacked sufficient evidence to directly accuse him, they were also well aware of General Gu's character. Deep down, many of them suspected that he had something to do with the Scorpion Squad secretly taking Yuan out of the city, especially considering that they were 'coincidentally' present during Mei Feng's appearance.
Eventually, one of them spoke up. "I don't know what kind of conflict the two of you are caught up in, but please leave us out of it from now on. You practically dragged us into it today."
None of them were fools. They understood perfectly well that General Gu had used their presence as both witnesses and a shield against General Mei.
General Gu offered no response, neither confirming nor denying their suspicions. Instead, he simply resumed the meeting as though nothing had happened.
Meanwhile, as Mei Feng walked away, she reflected on her own misstep.

'I was too rash today and walked straight into that man's trap...' she sighed inwardly. 'At least I confirmed that he had something to do with Yuan's disappearance... Now I just need to find him before anything happens..."
When Mei Feng returned to her office, she raised an eyebrow upon noticing a masked figure standing outside.
Unfazed by their presence, she asked, "What do you want now?"
"I heard about the situation."
"And?"
"I happen to have nothing to do now, so I could help with the search."
"The Ironwoman willingly going on a search mission? Aren't you worried that might affect your reputation?" Mei Feng said. "You've always refused to accept such missions, after all."
"This is different. It'd be a pity for someone who is being called my future rival to die so soon."
"Well, if you're going to help, I have no reason to refuse."
Thus, the Ironwoman decided to join in on the search.
Meanwhile, Yuan and the Scorpion Squad arrived at Red Zone after a few days of traveling without rest.
As they approached the Purple Zone, Yuan noticed the crimson mist in the air gradually darkening, its color slowly shifting toward a light shade of purple.
That light purple darkened as they got closer to the Purple Zone.
'As expected, the further we go, the more closely this mist resembles Chaotic Essence...' Yuan thought to himself after examining it.
However, it was still nowhere near the point where it'd strengthen his Chaotic Essence.
"How are you feeling, Corporal Yuan?" Sergeant Chen suddenly spoke to Yuan for the first time since they left the city. "Feeling nervous... or scared yet?"
"Honestly, I am a little nervous," Yuan calmly lied.
"With us with you, what is there to be worried about?" Captain Chen laughed.
Some time later, they arrived at the Purple Zone, where the color of the mist was a deep violet.
"Let's go. We have already located a tunnel, so it won't be long before we arrive at our destination," said Captain Chen.
Without any questions, Yuan followed them into the Purple Zone.
He glanced at the Void Specters that wandered below.
Even without fighting them, he could tell that they were incomparably stronger than the ones in the Red Zone, but this also meant they would have more Eternal Essence.
'Can't wait to absorb their Eternal Essence.' Yuan thought to himself as he smiled inwardly.
However, before they could even reach the tunnel, they had to survive the countless Void Specters that relentlessly attacked them.
As they traveled through the Purple Zone, Yuan and the others had to use Void Control almost constantly.
Although the Scorpion Squad had known from the start that getting rid of Yuan wouldn't be simple, they had still hoped he would meet an early end.
But alas, to their disappointment, several days passed, and the group arrived at the tunnel safe and sound.
"That wasn't as bad as I was expecting," Yuan casually remarked after they cleaned up the Void Specters around the tunnel.
"We are still in the outer areas of the Purple Zone, so it's not too bad," said Captain Chen.
"But things will get dangerous once we enter the tunnel, so make sure you stay alert."
"I get to clear the tunnel by myself, right?" Yuan then asked.
"Of course. How else are we supposed to see what you're really capable of?" Captain Chen replied with a smile. "But don't worry. If things get too dangerous, we'll step in."

chapters.title: Chapter 2625 Elite Void Specter
paragraphs: Yuan entered the tunnel shortly afterward, with the Scorpion Squad following close behind.

At first glance, the tunnel looked no different from the ones he had explored before. However, the deeper they ventured, the more apparent the differences became. The passage gradually widened, and before long, it branched into two separate paths.
"Which way do we go?" Yuan asked Captain Chen. "I've never seen tunnels branch like this before."
"I'm not surprised. This only happens in the Purple Zone," Captain Chen replied.

"As for which path to take... it doesn't really matter. Well, it does, but they all eventually lead to the same destination. The only difference is what you'll encounter along the way. Some paths have far more Void Specters than others, while some have tougher ones. Of course, if you're unlucky, it could be both."
They hadn't encountered a single Void Specter up to this point, but Yuan had a feeling that would change very soon.
Without giving much thought to it, Yuan picked the right path.
The Scorpion Squad didn't say anything and quietly followed.
As expected, it didn't take long before they encountered their first Void Specter.
However, even without engaging it, Yuan could tell at a glance that this Void Specter was vastly different from any he had encountered before, including those roaming the Purple Zone outside.
Not only did it emit a unique aura unlike the others, but its form was also far more humanoid.
'An Elite Void Specter!'
The members of the Scorpion Squad cried inwardly the moment they saw the Void Specter. There was only one, yet its mere presence sent chills down their spines.

Elite Void Specters were, as their name implied, the elite among Void Specters. Although they were not as powerful as Void Guardians, they were still exceedingly difficult to deal with in their own right due to their speed and high durability.
Under normal circumstances, encountering an Elite Void Specter—especially as their first encounter—would be considered incredibly unlucky.
However, given their current circumstances, the Scorpion Squad couldn't help but rejoice at Yuan's misfortune, seeing it as a stroke of good luck for themselves.
'To think we'd encounter an Elite Void Specter so soon! The heavens must also want to see this guy dead as much as we do!' Captain Chen laughed inwardly.
"Good luck, Corporal Yuan."
Captain Chen said, not even bothering to explain to Yuan what he was facing.
Rather than fighting it immediately, Yuan examined the Elite Void Specter from afar.
"What's wrong? Cold feet?" Captain Dung asked when Yuan did not move after moments of stillness.
"No, I was just thinking that my minigun won't be effective on it," Yuan calmly remarked.
Despite his near-limitless reserves of energy, Yuan's cultivation was still lacking, which meant there was only so much power he could draw from Limitless at once.

His minigun was devastating against large groups and could shred through them with ease, but only because the strength of his Limitless was sufficient to overwhelm them; hence why it took him several minutes of nonstop attacking to defeat the Void Guardian during his first gathering mission.
"Then how are you going to fight it? With your fists?" Captain Chen inquired with a puzzled face.
"Nope."
Yuan raised his minigun toward the Elite Void Specter, raising the others' eyebrows.
"I thought you said it wasn't going to be effective," Captain Chen remarked.
"Correct, but that doesn't mean it won't work. I also want to test out its limits."

Yuan's words left them speechless, as nobody would be foolish enough to test the capabilities of an Elite Void Specter if they knew about it. However, they kept quiet, and moments later, Yuan began firing a barrage of Limitless bullets at the Elite Void Specter.
"Oh?" Yuan muttered in surprise a few seconds later.
Although his bullets initially struck their target, the Elite Void Specter began evading them the moment it realized it was under attack.
Yuan immediately increased his output, but that only worked for several bullets before the Elite Void Specter adapted to it and began evading them perfectly again.
Soon, the Elite Void Specter was right in front of Yuan, and it swung its scythe-like arms at him.
'Die!' Captain Chen prayed inwardly.
However, Yuan used Void Manipulation and avoided the attack with ease.
"Looks like this weapon won't work on you..."
Without hesitation, Yuan dropped the minigun and proceeded to raise two fingers.
The members of Scorpion Squad were puzzled by his actions, wondering if he really intended on fighting the Elite Void Specter with his hands.

When the Elite Void Specter attacked again half a second later, Limitless suddenly surged from Yuan's hands. However, instead of dispersing in every direction like an unrestrained aura, the energy condensed into a distinct shape—a sword.
Sha!
Before the members of the Scorpion Squad could even comprehend what they had witnessed, the Elite Void Specter abruptly froze in front of Yuan.
A split second later, dozens of cuts appeared across its body before it dispersed into the air like smoke.
"W-What just happened?!" Captain Chen exclaimed in shock, turning to the others for an explanation.
However, the others shook their heads, as none of them saw what Yuan did just now.
Meanwhile, Yuan quickly absorbed the Eternal Essence left behind by the Elite Void Specter.
'That was about a hundred million years' worth of Eternal Essence! Although not as much as a Void Guardian, it's still plenty!' Yuan thought to himself.
A moment later, Yuan turned to the Scorpion Squad and said, "Alright, let's keep going."
They nodded in a dazed manner before quietly following him.
However, one of the members could not contain her curiosity and asked, "Um... what did you do to that Void Specter just now?"
"What does it look like I did?" Yuan replied with a question of his own.
"I'm asking because I don't know! Your movements were too fast just now, and I couldn't see anything!" she snapped, clearly irritated at having to admit that she had failed to follow his movements.

chapters.title: Chapter 2626 Elite Void Specter(2)
paragraphs: "I apologize in advance if this sounds rude, but it's not something that you can learn through an explanation, so I'll save my breath," Yuan said a moment later.
"What?!" The captain cried out loud, unable to believe her ears.
"Surely, a brief explanation wouldn't hurt," Captain Chen urged, as he was also interested in Yuan's powers.
After all, since he was going to die, they might as well learn his secrets before then.
"It's a family secret," Yuan calmly replied.
Then, without waiting for them, immediately started heading deeper into the cave.
'This little bastard! I want to strangle him to death right now!'
'That would definitely make things a lot easier.'
'Calm down. You know he has to die an 'accidental' death.'
The Scorpion Squad spoke to each other using voice transmission as they continued to follow Yuan.
'I know that, but can't we make it look like an accident? Instead of waiting for him to make a mistake, one of us could "accidentally" bump into him during a fight,' Captain Dung suggested.
'The system isn't stupid. It can sense your killing intent, even if you try to disguise it as an accident,' Captain Chen replied.
'If it can detect our killing intent that easily, then wouldn't it still hold us responsible if he dies later, even if we never lay a hand on him?'
'Right? We're technically luring him to his death right now.'
'The system isn't that powerful.'
'What if we tie him up and move as far away as possible?
Captain Chen sighed, 'Do you really think nobody has tried that before? If it was so simple, we wouldn't be doing this right now!'
Soon, Yuan reached another fork in the tunnel, but this time, three separate paths stretched out before him.
However, rather than choosing one at random, Yuan extended his senses as far as possible, searching for whichever path carried the strongest aura.

Instead of avoiding danger, he deliberately sought out the most dangerous route. Not only would stronger Void Specters benefit his cultivation, but he also wanted to give the Scorpion Squad a taste of their own medicine.
Although the Scorpion Squad had done an excellent job concealing their killing intent, they slipped up during Yuan's battle with the Elite Void Specter and allowed a trace of it to leak out.
Naturally, Yuan did not fail to notice it.
Moreover, even though Yuan was almost certain that they had been sent by General Gu to kill him, there remained a minuscule possibility that this wasn't the case... until just now, that was.
'A-Another Elite Void Specter?! He's encountered two Elite Void Specters in a row!'
The Scorpion Squad was baffled by Yuan's misfortune.
But since they've already witnessed Yuan defeat one in the blink of an eye, they didn't have any hope that he would fall to this one.
Sure enough, Yuan ended the fight in the blink of an eye, using the same technique he'd used before.
'Just what sort of technique is that?' asked one of the captains, as they grasped a slight glimpse of it this time.
'I don't know, but he's condensed his Limitless on his hand...'

The soldiers secretly tried to replicate Yuan's technique, and while they managed to condense their Limitless and even form a shape with it, it was nowhere near as refined or compressed as his. The difference was like comparing a solid steel blade to one made of jello.
Yuan noticed what they were doing and smiled inwardly, 'Not bad. If only they could use Supreme Sword Aura.'
Indeed, he had imbued his Supreme Sword Aura with Limitless, strengthening it multiple times over.
He also used the same technique to defeat the Void Guardians. Otherwise, he wouldn't have been able to defeat them in time before the other soldiers caught up with him.

Some time later, Yuan cleared several more paths. Unfortunately, not every path had an Elite Void Specter, and besides the first two, he only encountered ordinary Void Specters. Though even the ordinary ones were more powerful than the ones outside the tunnel.
"What do you think?" Yuan suddenly turned around to face the Scorpion Squad.
"What do you mean?"
"Are you satisfied with my capabilities so far?"
"Y-yes..." Captain Chen nodded with a stiff smile.
"Is that so? Well, I am just getting started, so try not to be too surprised later."

A day later, a cold smile crept across Yuan's face when he sensed an impressive aura emanating from one of the paths. Since he was walking ahead of the Scorpion Squad, none of them noticed his expression.
Not long after choosing that route, Yuan encountered not one... not two... or three... but four Elite Void Specters!
"T-This is—!" The Scorpion Squad visibly flinched when they saw this.
"Four of them, huh? As confident as I am in my abilities, I don't think I can handle more than two at once, so I'll leave the other two to you guys," Yuan said.
Captain Chen's eyes widened at Yuan's words, and he hastily said, "You're still thinking of fighting in this situation?! That's insane! No! We will go back and take another path!"

Even though this was the perfect opportunity to get rid of Yuan, there was no way they could deal with the aftermath. After all, once the Elite Void Specters killed Yuan, they would inevitably turn their attention to the Scorpion Squad next.

However, Yuan then said, "Surely, you're saying that just to mess with me. They're not that difficult to fight, so there's no way the five of you cannot handle two of them. Don't worry, I'll help out as soon as I defeat my targets."
"Yo—"
Captain Chen opened his mouth, but before he could even utter a complete word, Yuan rushed into the detection range of the Elite Void Specters, immediately drawing their attention.
"This fucking suicidal maniac is going to drag us down with him!" Captain Dung cursed out loud, his face flushed with anger as they immediately prepared for battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 2627 Elite Void Specter(3)
paragraphs: Once the Elite Void Specters noticed their presence, one of them charged at Yuan while the other three made their way towards the Scorpion Squad behind him.
Even though Yuan said he'd take care of two of them, he completely ignored it and focused on the Elite Void Specter before him.
Of course, if he wanted to, Yuan could easily defeat the Elite Void Specter in a split second, but he purposefully took his time with it.
Meanwhile, the Scorpion Squad began to panic as they found themselves facing three Elite Void Specters at once.
With only five members, they were forced to split into three groups, with Captain Chen taking on one of the Elite Void Specters by himself while the remaining four paired up against the other two.

Although Captain Chen was the strongest member of the squad, even he knew that defeating an Elite Void Specter alone was beyond him. His only option was to stall for time until the others could come to his aid.
With all of his attention focused on surviving, he had no room to spare for Yuan, who was essentially pretending to struggle against his own Elite Void Specter.
A full minute later, Yuan defeated his Elite Void Specter and went to assist Captain Chen.
"What took you so long?!" Captain Chen shouted at Yuan, his forehead bulging with veins.

"That Void Specter was much stronger than the previous ones I fought," Yuan calmly responded before defeating the one before him in less than a second, which only enraged Captain Chen even more when he saw this.
But before Captain Chen could even say anything, Yuan left to assist the others.
In the end, nobody died, but the Scorpion Squad definitely received a scare.
Once all of the Elite Void Specters were defeated, the Scorpion Squad surrounded Yuan and screamed at him.
"WHAT THE HELL WAS THAT?! WERE YOU TRYING TO GET ALL OF US KILLED?!" Captain Dung roared, the veins in his neck bulging with rage.
"I told you we should've taken another path! Why did you ignore my order and rush in?! That could've ended badly for all of us!"
Despite their anger, Yuan remained remarkably calm.

After a moment, he looked at them with genuine confusion and asked, "I don't understand. Why are you so upset? Sure, those Void Specters were stronger than expected, but why did you struggle so much against them? I thought all of you were strong enough to handle them yourselves."
"That wasn't any ordinary Void Specter, but an Elite Void Specter! They're not something one can defeat alone!"
"Elite Void Specter? This is new information for me," Yuan said before questioning, "If they were so dangerous, why'd you let me fight them alone?"

"They may be dangerous, but they're still weaker than a Void Guardian. Since you've claimed that you can defeat a Void Guardian by yourself, we weren't worried about you losing to a single Elite Void Specter. Even if you couldn't defeat it, the rest of us could handle one together. What we can't handle is several of them at once. What you did was incredibly reckless and foolish!"

"Is that so? I'll keep that in mind," Yuan said with a nod. "But you can't expect me to know something if you never explain it beforehand. Also, if there's something you can't handle, you should tell me in advance. That way, I won't recklessly put myself in another situation where you won't be able to protect me if things go wrong."

Although Captain Chen wanted to punish Yuan for his actions, he had no real justification for doing so. After all, they had deliberately withheld information about the Elite Void Specters from him, giving Yuan the perfect excuse to claim that he simply hadn't known any better.
"Anyway, let's continue." Yuan turned around and started venturing deeper into the tunnel.
'That bastard must've done that on purpose!' Captain Dung suspected.
'Unless he knows our true objective, he has no reason to do such a thing,' said Captain Chen.
'What if he knows?' another officer asked.
'Even if he knows, there's nothing he can really do about it. Not only does he lack proof, but it's not like he can kill us, either.'
'The real question is... how the hell are we supposed to kill him and make it look like an accident now? He can defeat four Elite Void Specters by himself...' someone asked.
'Damn it... I don't understand how he's doing it! How the hell is he defeating these Void Specters so easily when his cultivation is far lower than ours?! It makes no sense!

'Right?! I've been watching him closely this entire time, and the amount of Limitless he uses isn't anything extraordinary! He must possess some kind of technique that allows him to draw out the hidden power of Limitless, just like Tian Yuchen!'
'If that's the case, we must acquire that technique before we kill him!'
'And how do you intend to do that when we're not even sure we can kill him without touching him?!'
The Scorpion Squad argued with each other while Yuan continued to clear the tunnel alone.
Eventually, they arrived at the end of the tunnel.
"What are you waiting for?" Captain Dung asked when Yuan stood at the edge of the hole without moving for a long time.
"Don't tell me you're getting cold feet because you can't actually defeat a Void Guardian by yourself?" Another member said in a somewhat mocking tone.
Yuan, who had been staring at the hole, turned around and spoke with a calm smile, "As if."
Then, without another word, jumped into the hole.
Seeing this, the members of Scorpion Squad gave each other a quick glance before following Yuan down the hole.
A few minutes later, they arrived at the chamber with the Void Guardian.
However, their eyes widened with shock the very next moment.
"T-Two... There are two Void Guardians?!"
Captain Chen exclaimed in shock when he saw two massive silhouettes standing beside each other.

'And how do you intend to do that when we're not even sure we can kill him without touching him?!'
The Scorpion Squad argued with each other while Yuan continued to clear the tunnel alone.
Eventually, they arrived at the end of the tunnel.
"What are you waiting for?" Captain Dung asked when Yuan stood at the edge of the hole without moving for a long time.
"Don't tell me you're getting cold feet because you can't actually defeat a Void Guardian by yourself?" Another member said in a somewhat mocking tone.
Yuan, who had been staring at the hole, turned around and spoke with a calm smile, "As if."
Then, without another word, jumped into the hole.
Seeing this, the members of Scorpion Squad gave each other a quick glance before following Yuan down the hole.
A few minutes later, they arrived at the chamber with the Void Guardian.
However, their eyes widened with shock the very next moment.
"T-Two...
There are two Void Guardians?!"
Captain Chen exclaimed in shock when he saw two massive silhouettes standing beside each other.

chapters.title: Chapter 2628 Double Void Guardians
paragraphs: "Why are there two Void Guardians here?! That shouldn't be possible in the Purple Zone!" Captain Chen cried out loud.
"Who cares about that?! We need to get out of here before they attack!" Captain Dung shouted as he immediately flew back up the hole.
The others did not hesitate and quickly followed after him, abandoning the chamber without a second thought.
Captain Chen gritted his teeth and prepared to retreat as well. Before leaving, however, he glanced back at Yuan, who was still falling and showed no intention of turning back.
'What a fool. It's a shame we won't be able to uncover his secrets before he dies, but at least our mission is finally complete,' Captain Chen mocked inwardly before leaving the chamber.
Meanwhile, Yuan merely shook his head inwardly at the Scorpion Squad. He didn't even bother looking back at them, keeping his attention fixed on the two Void Guardians before him instead.
An excited smile slowly appeared on Yuan's face. In his eyes, two Void Guardians only meant double the reward!
Shortly after the Scorpion Squad began making their way back up the tunnel, an immensely powerful and unfathomable aura suddenly erupted from the chamber below, catching their attention.
"W-What the hell is that energy?!" Captain Dung exclaimed in shock.
"Did that guy really stay behind to fight two Void Guardians at once?! Suicidal!"
"That works in our favor, anyway. There's no way he's getting out of this one alive."
Captain Chen said nothing and merely glanced back down the tunnel, an ominous feeling stirring in the pit of his stomach.
'Will that really be enough to kill him?' he wondered inwardly.
The energy surging from the chamber continued to rise, eventually reaching a level that felt almost surreal.

Not only were the Void Guardians in the Purple Zone vastly stronger than those in the Red Zone, but there were also two of them. Even for someone like Yuan, this was not a situation he could resolve in the blink of an eye.

That being said, Yuan wasn't exactly struggling, either. Although the Void Guardians were stronger, that merely meant they were faster and far more aggressive. With Yuan's mastery of Void Manipulation, however, neither posed any real threat to him.
In other words, defeating them simply required a little more time than usual.
A few minutes later, just as the Scorpion Squad reached the top of the hole and returned to the tunnel, the energy suddenly stopped.
"Hm? Did he finally die? That took longer than I expected."
"Should we go back down and check?"
"And risk our lives? Don't be stupid. There's no way he could defeat two Void Guardians by himself. He's definitely dead.
"Chen? What are you thinking about, staring down that hole so intensely?" Captain Dung suddenly asked after noticing his unusual behavior.
After another moment of silence, Captain Chen finally spoke.
"Call me crazy, but I don't think he's dead."
"Huh? That's definitely crazy, all right. Did you hit your head on the way out or something?" One of the members mocked him openly.
"I'm going to take a look. You can stay here if you want."
Before the others could respond, Captain Chen jumped back down the hole.
"C-Chen?!"
Captain Chen could hear Captain Dung's shocked voice echoing from above but ignored it and continued falling.
A few minutes later, Captain Chen returned to the chamber.
"I-Impossible..." he muttered in a daze when he realized that the two Void Guardians were nowhere to be seen.
His gaze instinctively shifted toward the center of the chamber, where Yuan sat quietly absorbing the Eternal Essence they had left behind.
If a Void Guardian from the Red Zone contained roughly a billion years' worth of Eternal Essence, then each one in the Purple Zone possessed more than ten billion years' worth.
Since Yuan had defeated two of them, he had gained over twenty billion years' worth of Eternal Essence in a single battle.
Captain Chen silently stared at Yuan from a distance for a full minute before calling out to him.
"C-Corporal Yuan...?"
However, there was no response from Yuan.
"Corporal Yuan!" he called out again, this time in a much louder voice.
"I heard you the first time," Yuan responded without moving.
"What are you doing? What happened to the Void Guardians?" Captain Chen asked.
"I'm a little busy right now, so let's talk later.
A few minutes later, Captain Chen turned around after sensing Captain Dung and the others entering the chamber behind him.
Sure enough, every single one of them wore a bewildered expression, as though they were struggling to comprehend the scene before them.
"W-What is going on here...? Where are the Void Guardians?" Captain Dung asked in a dazed voice.
"He's actually still alive..." another member mumbled as she stared at Yuan, who was still cultivating in silence.
"What is he doing?" a third member asked.
"I don't know, but he's been in that position since I arrived."
"Is he sleeping?"
"Hey, wake up!" Captain Dung suddenly yelled at Yuan.
When Yuan ignored him, Captain Dung began walking toward him with a deep frown.
Just as he reached Yuan and extended a hand toward his shoulder, Yuan suddenly turned and fixed him with a calm yet piercing gaze.
"You're still here? I thought you would've run all the way back to the tunnel entrance by now."
"W-What did you just say...?" Captain Dung muttered, his eyebrows twitching with anger. "I dare you to say that again!"
"Why are you getting so angry? It's true that you ran away the moment you saw two Void Guardians. Or are you going to deny it and call me a liar?" Yuan said, shaking his head.
He then stood up to face Captain Dung and the others.
"Why did you come back? To collect the Unknown Crystals or... to confirm my death?"
The members of the Scorpion Squad widened their eyes in shock at Yuan's words.
"W-What are you talking about, Corporal Yuan?" Captain Chen spoke a moment later, trying his best to sound confused. "There must be some kind of misunderstanding."
Yuan looked at him and sneered, "You can drop the act. I know that you brought me out here with the intention of killing me."

chapters.title: Chapter 2629 Dropping the Act
paragraphs: "W-We brought you out here to kill you? That's a serious accusation, Corporal Yuan!" Captain Chen exclaimed, continuing to insist that it was nothing more than a misunderstanding. "What reason could we possibly have to want you dead?! We only wanted to verify the rumors!"

"You may have no reason to kill me, but your boss, General Gu, definitely does," Yuan said with a smile. "However, if you truly have no intention of killing me, then you'd have no problem with us returning to the city now, right?"
Captain Chen fell silent for a moment before releasing a deep sigh.
"Unfortunately, we cannot do that," he said with a serious expression, finally deciding to drop the act.
The members of the Scorpion Squad suddenly moved, surrounding Yuan from all sides.

"Are you going to kill me now?" Yuan asked calmly, even though he already knew they wouldn't dare dirty their own hands. After all, if they could kill him directly without consequence, they would've done so long ago.
However, Captain Chen and the others remained silent.
'What should we do now that we've been exposed?' one of the members asked through voice transmission.
'Do we just... kill him now?'
Although killing Yuan themselves seemed to be their only remaining option, none of them wanted to be the one to actually dirty their hands.
"I will do it. I will kill this bastard with my own hands!" Captain Dung suddenly said out loud.
"I have a suggestion."
Captain Dung froze at Yuan's words.
"A suggestion, you say? Unless you're offering to kill yourself, I don't want to hear it," Captain Dung sneered with a look of disdain on his face.
Yuan smiled and said, "That's exactly what I was going to suggest."
"Excuse me?" Captain Chen raised his eyebrows in puzzlement.
"Although I don't know why you're so hesitant to kill me yourselves, it wouldn't matter even if you tried. After all, none of you are capable of killing me," Yuan said with a confident smile.
"What did you just say?" Captain Dung frowned.
"We'll give you credit for being able to defeat Elite Void Specters and Void Guardians on your own, but fighting other humans is an entirely different matter," one of the members said.
Yuan chuckled and said, "In that case, let's put that to the test."
Before any of them could even react to Yuan's words, he suddenly used Void Manipulation, vanishing from his spot and appearing right behind Captain Chen.
"Catch me if you can," Yuan said.
"G-Get him! Don't let him escape!" Captain Chen hastily shouted as he lunged toward Yuan.
"Don't worry. I have no intention of leaving this tunnel," Yuan said as he teleported a few meters away.
The next moment, the members of the Scorpion Squad found themselves playing an absurd game of tag with him, and despite having five people, none of them could so much as touch his shadow.
"Hahaha! Is this really the level of captains?! I was expecting much more!"
"Slow! Too slow!"
"Are you sure you even qualify to enter the Purple Zone? Your Void Control barely qualifies for the Red Zone!
Yuan continued taunting them relentlessly as they desperately tried—and repeatedly failed—to catch him.
One hour... two hours... five hours passed—
"Enough! We get your point!" Captain Chen finally came to a halt and shouted, his voice trembling with frustration.
The other members of Scorpion Squad also stopped trying to catch Yuan and started taking deep breaths from exhaustion.
Yuan then said, "As I was saying... since none of you are capable of killing me, you might as well return to the city and give up trying to kill me."
"Do you really think that's an option for us?" Captain Chen responded with a frown.

"Well, what other options do you have? If I wanted to return to the city, there's nothing any of you here could do about it. And if I wanted to kill you... it'd be easier than dealing with Void Specters."
"Then—"
"With that being said..." Yuan interrupted Captain Chen before he could respond. "I don't actually want to return to the city. At least not yet."
"What the hell are you talking about?"

A profound smile tugged at Yuan's lips as he explained, "I've been wanting to explore the Purple Zone alone—and even the Black Zone—for quite some time now. Unfortunately, with my low rank and status as a new soldier, that isn't possible."
His smile deepened.
"But thanks to you lot, I now have the perfect excuse to venture as far as I want, and I have no intention of wasting such a valuable opportunity."
Yuan approached Captain Chen and continued, "Therefore, here is my real suggestion. Go back to the city and tell General Gu that you have succeeded in your mission and that I am dead."
"You... are you crazy...?" Captain Chen muttered with a dumbfounded expression.
"You want us to lie to General Gu?! And what do you think will happen to us when you return alive?!" one of the members exclaimed.
Yuan shrugged and nonchalantly replied, "I fail to see how that is my problem. In fact, I couldn't care less."
"You—!"

"What other choice do you have?" Yuan interrupted them again. "You can either return without me and hope I somehow die on my own, or we can go back together, where you'll have to explain to General Gu why you failed your mission—and answer to General Mei for trying to kill me."
The members of the Scorpion Squad swallowed nervously at Yuan's words and fell silent as they weighed their options.

If they returned to the city with Yuan still alive, they would undoubtedly have to face the wrath of both General Gu and General Mei. However, if they followed Yuan's suggestion and returned without him, they would at least retain a slim chance of survival.
Though it wasn't as if they really had a choice in the first place, as they were incapable of killing Yuan.
"Are you... really going to go deeper into the Purple Zone and even enter the Black Zone?" Captain Chen asked out of curiosity.
"That's right." Yuan nodded with a genuine-looking expression on his face.
"Why?"
"That's none of your business."
Captain Chen closed his eyes and took a deep breath before turning to look at the other members.
"We're returning to the city," he announced in a defeated tone.
None of the members said anything and silently nodded.
Shortly afterward, the Scorpion Squad left the tunnel, leaving Yuan behind, who went on to absorb the Eternal Essence from the hundreds of Unknown Crystals still glistening along the walls.

"Are we really going to return to the city and lie to General Gu? What if that bastard was lying and plans to return immediately as well?" Captain Dung asked as they made their way back toward the surface.
"Of course not," Captain Chen said. "I want to confirm with my own eyes that he truly intends to venture deeper into the Purple Zone, and regardless of his actions, we're going to ambush him."
"How are we supposed to do that when we can't even catch him?"
"That's why I said we'll ambush him! We don't stand a chance in a direct confrontation, so our only option is to catch him off guard."
After leaving the tunnel, the Scorpion Squad hid their presence and waited for Yuan to come out.
Some time later, Yuan emerged from the tunnel.
However, instead of leaving immediately, he remained by the entrance and glanced from side to side, as though searching for someone nearby.
After looking around for a minute, Yuan started venturing in the direction that led him deeper into the Purple Zone.
'He's really going deeper into the Purple Zone!'
'Should we keep following him?' Captain Dung asked.
'Of course. For all we know, he could simply be putting on an act because he suspects we're still watching him,' Captain Chen replied.
Thus, the Scorpion Squad began secretly following Yuan, completely unaware that he had sensed their presence long before he even emerged from the tunnel.

Despite knowing they were there, Yuan had no intention of confronting them. In his eyes, the Scorpion Squad wasn't worth his time or effort. Moreover, if they insisted on following him deeper into the Purple Zone, they would only be putting their own lives at risk.
'Now that I am alone...'
A wide grin slowly spread across Yuan's face as his aura began to rise.
'What is he doing...?'
The members of the Scorpion Squad watched with puzzled expressions, unable to understand what Yuan was planning.

The next moment, his aura erupted violently. Limitless surged outward in every direction like a colossal tidal wave, sweeping across the barren landscape and instantly annihilating every Void Specter caught in its path.
Captain Chen and the others stared with their mouths agape, their eyes filled with utter disbelief at what they had just witnessed.
However, Yuan wasn't finished.

After clearing the area of Void Specters, he made a simple gesture with two fingers, pointing them toward the heavens. The next moment, hundreds of Unknown Ores shot into the air and gathered before him, as though invisible ghosts were collecting them on his behalf.

After gathering all of the Unknown Ores, including the ones inside the ground, Yuan took a moment to absorb all of their Eternal Essence before moving deeper into the Purple Zone, leaving the Unknown Ores behind.
'W-What was that just now?!' Captain Chen exclaimed inwardly, having trouble comprehending what he'd just witnessed.
Unfortunately, they had no time to stand around and process what they had witnessed, as Yuan was already leaving them behind.

With no other choice, the Scorpion Squad hurried after him. Yet as they continued following Yuan, he repeated the same astonishing feat again and again—slaughtering countless Void Specters and gathering thousands of Unknown Ores in ways none of them had ever seen before.

chapters.title: Chapter 2630 Black Zone
paragraphs: A hundred million years... a billion years... ten billion years... a hundred billion years...

Yuan's Eternal Essence soared as he wreaked havoc across the Purple Zone, annihilating every Void Specter in his path while absorbing the energy contained within the thousands of Unknown Ores scattered throughout the land.
However, such rapid growth did not occur over the span of merely a few days. Even at Yuan's pace, it still required several weeks of relentless effort.
Of course, the Scorpion Squad followed him the entire time.
'This guy... he's not human!' Captain Chen clenched his fists tightly, desperately trying to suppress the trembling in his body.
'Chen... It's obvious now that he truly intends to enter the Black Zone,' one of the members remarked. 'Maybe we should... head back to the base?'
'I agree with Mung. At this point, I don't see any reason to keep following him. Hell, I don't even think we'll be able to ambush him!'
Captain Chen pondered for a moment before responding, 'We'll keep following him until he enters the Black Zone.'
The others exchanged concerned looks.
'I know what all of you are thinking—and I feel the same way. I'm afraid of him too... but at the same time, I can't help feeling curious. I want to see what other secrets he's still hiding.'
Captain Chen turned to look at them and continued, 'It won't be too long before we reach the Black Zone. Moreover, it's clear that he isn't aware of our presence.'
A few days later, Yuan slowed down when he noticed that the purple mist had darkened so much that it had turned black.
'Am I in the Black Zone?' he wondered.
He examined the black mist a moment later.
'Oh?'
Although it was not by much, his Chaotic Essence had improved slightly after absorbing the mist!
Meanwhile, Captain Chen and the others finally stopped following Yuan.
'He's really entering the Black Zone.'
'I've been watching him for the last several weeks, but I still cannot fathom his actions.'
'There's no point thinking about it. Let's go back and report his death.'
Thus, the Scorpion Squad turned around and began their journey back to the city.

As they traveled, they couldn't help but feel that, all things considered, the situation had turned out far better than they had anticipated, especially after they'd been exposed. After all, Yuan could've returned to the city after learning of their schemes, but for some reason, he decided to enter the Black Zone on his own.

'I-Isn't that the Ironwoman?! To think we'd encounter her out here! How unlucky!' Captain Chen cried inwardly after seeing her.
'Chen! What should we do?! Should we just ignore her?' one of the members asked anxiously.
'No. Greet her normally, then leave as quickly as possible.'
The Scorpion Squad approached the Ironwoman and her squad, who had already come to a stop after noticing their presence and were now watching them closely.
Once they were close enough, Captain Chen and the others greeted them.
"We greet the Ironwoman and the Stellar Squad!"
The Ironwoman nodded in acknowledgment before asking, "Are you returning from a mission?"
"Y-Yes, we are," Captain Chen replied, unable to hide his surprise at the question. The Ironwoman was well known for minding her own business, so he hadn't expected her to show any interest in them.
The Ironwoman fell silent.
"Then, if you'll excuse us—"
Just as Captain Chen and the others prepared to leave, the Ironwoman spoke again, "Where do you think you're going?"
Captain Chen's movements instantly froze at the sound of her cold tone.
"Excuse me?" he turned to look at her.
"Is this all of you?" she then asked.
"Yes." Captain Chen nodded.

Despite his seemingly calm demeanor, Captain Chen's back was already drenched in cold sweat. The Ironwoman hadn't said much, but she had said enough for him to realize that her appearance—and their encounter—was no mere coincidence.
"That's funny."
"Why would it be funny?" Captain Chen frowned.
"You see... before coming out here, I heard that your squad had secretly brought a new soldier out on a mission."
The Ironwoman scanned the members with a cold gaze before continuing, "So, where is this soldier? Surely, you didn't leave a mere corporal who'd just joined the military behind in the Purple Zone."
Captain Chen subconsciously clenched his fists.
'Fuck! To think they'd send the Ironwoman to search for Corporal Yuan!' he cried inwardly, realizing that he'd underestimated how important Yuan was to General Mei.
However, Captain Chen quickly replied, "There must be some kind of misunderstanding. We didn't bring anyone who wasn't supposed to be out here with us."
"That's right!" Captain Dung added. "What you heard was nothing more than a baseless rumor. Unless you personally saw us bringing this corporal out here, you shouldn't be making such accusations!"
The Ironwoman merely shrugged. "The gate guards have already admitted what happened, and they're willing to testify that they saw you use the teleporter with Corporal Yuan."

Captain Chen narrowed his eyes. "For argument's sake, even if we did bring Corporal Yuan out here, it wouldn't be against the rules. As officers, we have every right and authority to take soldiers with us on missions."

"You're right. It isn't against the rules," the Ironwoman replied. "However, his safety would then be your responsibility. If he dies under your supervision, you'll have to answer for your negligence and failure to protect him. And, of course, we'd also have to investigate whether his death was truly accidental."
"Anyway, Scorpion Squad, you're under arrest on suspicion of conspiring against a fellow soldier. Are you going to surrender peacefully, or do you want to make this difficult?"
Captain Chen glanced at the others before slowly raising his hands in surrender. The rest of the Scorpion Squad followed suit without resistance.
Even if they chose to fight, they stood no chance against the Stellar Squad—much less the Ironwoman, who was more than capable of defeating all of them by herself.
"Arrest them." The Ironwoman commanded, and her squad swiftly restricted their movements and cultivation with a golden chain.
"Take them back to the city. I'll stay out here for a little longer," said the Ironwoman.
"Yes, squad leader."
Her squadmates had complete faith in her abilities and did not question her decision to remain behind and venture through the Purple Zone alone.
Once the Stellar Squad departed with the Scorpion Squad in custody, the Ironwoman turned toward the direction they had come from and flew off.
'The chances of Corporal Yuan still being alive are slim...' The Ironwoman had realized this the moment she saw that he wasn't with the Scorpion Squad.
Even so, an inexplicable feeling in her gut urged her to keep searching.
A few days later, the Ironwoman arrived at the border between the Purple Zone and the Black Zone.
She hovered silently in the air, a thoughtful expression on her face.
Throughout the past few days of travel, she had noticed a disturbing lack of Void Specters. No, it would be more accurate to say that they were completely absent.
'I've never seen the Purple Zone this quiet before... Just what the hell happened here?'
However, that wasn't even the strangest part.
The Ironwoman lowered her gaze toward the ground, where thousands of Unknown Ores lay scattered openly across the barren landscape.
It was such a bizarre sight that she could only imagine seeing something like it in a dream.
The Ironwoman scratched her head, utterly bewildered by the situation before her.
Eventually, she decided to stop dwelling on it and entered the Black Zone, where the trail of Unknown Ores continued into the distance like bait deliberately laid out to lure unsuspecting prey.
Unsurprisingly, the Black Zone was no different. Not a single Void Specter could be sensed anywhere, as though some unknown force had swept through the region and completely eradicated them.
One day... three days... five days...
Time passed quickly, and after nearly an entire week of following the trail of Unknown Ores, the Ironwoman suddenly came to a halt when she sensed an immensely powerful presence in the distance.
The moment she detected it, she immediately increased her speed and rushed toward its source, which also happened to be where the trail ended.
"T-That's..."
Her eyes widened beneath her mask, filled with shock and disbelief as she stared at the lone figure standing at the end of the trail.
"C-Corporal Yuan?!" she cried out in disbelief.
Hearing her voice, Yuan turned around to face her.
"You are..." He quickly recognized her.

"What are you doing out here alone?! And what the hell is up with the Unknown Ores on the ground?!" the Ironwoman asked as she slowly approached him, unable to suppress the faint wariness she felt toward his presence.
Yuan hesitated, unsure how to respond.

chapters.title: Chapter 2631 Black Zone(2)
paragraphs: 'I wasn't expecting anyone to find me so soon...' Yuan sighed inwardly.

He had finally been given the freedom to roam outside the city alone and train to his heart's content, and while he'd already gained a lot, he was nowhere near satisfied. Returning now would feel like wasting such a rare opportunity.
"Corporal Yuan? Why are you remaining silent?" The Ironwoman asked a moment later.
"Ahem." Yuan cleared his throat and responded, "I'm training right now."
"Excuse me?"
Ironwoman raised her eyebrows behind her mask, wearing a puzzled look on her face.
"You're... training?" she muttered in a dumbfounded tone.
"What about the Scorpion Squad? Weren't you kidnapped by them? At least, that's what half the military believes right now!"
Yuan chuckled and said, "I wouldn't call it kidnapping since I willingly agreed to come out here with them."
"So what you're telling me is that the Scorpion Squad is innocent?"
"Well, that depends on what you're charging them with. If it's kidnapping, then yes, that would be inaccurate. But if you're charging them with conspiracy to commit murder, then you'd have a case."
"If they were really trying to kill you, why did they leave without you? We encountered them on the way here and have arrested them, you know?" said the Ironwoman.
"Whether they are capable of killing me or not is an entirely different story," Yuan responded with a calm smile. "They tried to kill me, but they lack the capability, so they gave up."
The Ironwoman released a weak sigh before asking, "What about the Unknown Ores on the ground? Where did they come from?"
Yuan looked at the Unknown Ores scattered across the ground and replied with a poker face, "I don't know."
He couldn't come up with a convincing excuse, so he decided it would be better to simply feign ignorance.

The Ironwoman stared at Yuan in silence. Although she could tell that he was withholding information from her, she ultimately decided not to press him for answers. After all, the most important thing was that he was still alive. Moreover, it was not her mission to question him.
"Let's return to the city now. You can explain everything to General Mei," she said a moment later.
However, just as she turned around and prepared to leave, Yuan spoke, "Sorry, but I don't want to return to the city."
"What did you just say?"
The Ironwoman's movements froze for a second before she turned to look at him with a puzzled expression.

Yuan sighed and explained, "If I wanted to return to the city, I would've done so already. But as I mentioned earlier, I am training. Do you have any idea how hard it is for a new soldier like me to come out alone? Now that I have the opportunity to do so, I don't want to return until I am finished."
"Do you have any idea how many people are waiting for your return? Many of them probably already think you're dead."

"That's even better," Yuan chuckled. "If they already think that I am dead, I might as well stay out here for a little longer. As for General Mei, you can tell her that I am still alive and doing well—that I will return as soon as I finish my training. I'm sure she'll understand."

After another moment of silence, the Ironwoman shrugged. "My mission was to find you, and since I've done exactly that, I've technically completed it. Whether you return with me or stay out here is none of my concern."

She paused briefly before continuing, "That being said, I want to at least make sure you can take care of yourself in the Black Zone before I head back and get an earful from General Mei for leaving you out here alone."
"Thanks," said Yuan.
Knowing the Ironwoman's identity, Yuan already had a feeling that she wouldn't force him to go back to the city, so he wasn't too surprised by it.
Some time later, Yuan resumed his training, eliminating every Void Specter he encountered. However, now that he was no longer alone, he stopped gathering Unknown Ores.

He hadn't minded letting the Scorpion Squad witness his unusual methods, since there was a good chance no one would believe anything they said anyway. The Ironwoman, however, was a different story. Even though Yuan trusted her, explaining everything would be far more trouble than it was worth.
'This guy... he's defeating the Void Specters with ease!' The Ironwoman quickly found herself stunned by Yuan's unfathomable prowess.

The Void Specters within the Black Zone were on an entirely different level from those in the Purple Zone. Not only did they possess humanoid forms similar to Elite Void Specters, but their strength was comparable as well.

'I knew he was hiding his strength, but I could've never imagined it was to such a degree! A corporal dominating the Black Zone that even top officers are not able to do so? It's no wonder that General Mei cares so much about him!
The more the Ironwoman watched Yuan, the less she understood him—his very existence.
"Where'd you learn to fight like that?"
The Ironwoman could no longer hold her tongue and asked Yuan.
"Would you believe me if I said that I learned it from another world?" Yuan responded with a smile.
"Another world, huh? Is that a metaphor for another city, or are you telling me that you came from beyond this sky—from another star?"
"What do you think?"
"I think you're pulling my leg," she said.
Then, she asked, "Anyway, I noticed that you've stopped digging up Unknown Ores. You don't have to mind me and just keep doing what you've been doing, you know?"
"Are you going to question me about it?"
"Well, I am questioning you now precisely because you stopped. If you're worried about revealing your secrets, I promise I won't tell anyone."
After a moment of silence, Yuan started gathering Unknown Ores and absorbing their Eternal Essence again.
The Ironwoman quietly picked up a few of the Unknown Ores Yuan had left behind and examined them closely, but she couldn't find anything unusual about them.
This only left her more puzzled. From her perspective, Yuan was simply pulling the ores out from underground before tossing them aside like worthless trash—an utterly pointless action.
'Is he looking for a specific Unknown Ore or something?' she wondered inwardly.

chapters.title: Chapter 2632 Black Zone(3)
paragraphs: "Are you looking for something specific?" asked the Ironwoman.
"I thought you weren't going to question me," Yuan said with a smile.
"Did I say that? I only remember saying that I won't tell anyone about your secrets," she replied with a smile of her own, but it was concealed by her mask.
"Is that so? Well, I'm not really looking for anything."
"Then what's the purpose behind your actions?"

Yuan fell silent for a moment before answering, "I... figured I'd make things easier for the soldiers who come out here on gathering missions. There are far too many for me to carry by myself, so I thought I'd bring them to the surface and make them easier to find."
It wasn't the most convincing explanation, but Yuan had at least managed to come up with an excuse for his strange actions.
"You don't have a storage cube?" the Ironwoman suddenly asked.
"A storage cube? No."
"They're issued to every soldier after completing training. Since you skipped training, you should've received one already. Have you even visited the supply warehouse since you joined?"
"Why am I not surprised?" The Ironwoman shook her head before taking out a pebble-sized, cube-shaped object and holding it up for Yuan to see.
"This is a storage cube," she explained before demonstrating how it worked.
The moment she injected Limitless into it, the cube glowed with an azure light and began drawing in all of the Unknown Ores scattered across the ground.
"It can hold up to ten thousand Unknown Ores," she said after gathering all of the Unknown Ores on the ground.
Yuan raised an eyebrow at the sight. "If there's such a convenient tool, why didn't the others use one during our missions? This is my first time seeing it."

"Probably because a storage cube can only be used so many times before it needs to be repaired, which costs money. Using one on an ordinary gathering mission that only yields a few hundred ores simply isn't worth the cost, so most soldiers just carry it.

This was Yuan's first time encountering a storage treasure that could only be used a limited number of times before requiring repairs. He couldn't help but imagine how inconvenient it would be if spatial rings and storage pouches worked the same way.
"I'll help you collect as many Unknown Ores as I can while I'm with you," said the Ironwoman.
"Thanks..."
Unfortunately, that also meant the ores she collected would eventually be handed over to the military for extraction, preventing Yuan from completely draining all of their Eternal Essence.
Since he was technically the one responsible for uncovering them, it would immediately draw suspicion if every single Unknown Ore he gathered turned out to be completely devoid of energy.
They continued venturing deeper into the Black Zone shortly after.
"How vast is the Black Zone?" Yuan asked the Ironwoman a few hours later.
"If you continue traveling at your current pace, you'd need at least five years to reach the Purple Zone on the other side."
"The Black Zone takes up far more space than I anticipated..."
"The Black Zone makes up the majority of this world, after all. There are even levels to Black Zones, and the one we're currently in is considered the least dangerous—a level 1 Black Zone."
"How many levels are there?"
"Four."
"How much more dangerous is level 2 compared to level 1?"

"Incomparably more dangerous. Even though the Void Specters in the Green Zone can kill someone with the slightest touch, their movement speed and awareness are practically nonexistent compared to those in the Black Zone," the Ironwoman explained.

"In a level 2 Black Zone, the Void Specters fight like seasoned human experts. Their durability also increases dramatically—to the point where an entire squad of captains may need several hours just to defeat a single one."

"As for level 3... we're currently incapable of defeating the Void Specters at that level. That being said, it's not as though they've never been defeated before. Throughout history, there have been a handful of individuals powerful enough to accomplish such a feat.
"Who are these individuals?" Yuan inquired.
"Have you been to Gaia's Sanctum?" she suddenly asked.
"Of course."

"Then you must have seen the Endless Assault rankings. Everyone who has surpassed the 40th floor was capable of defeating the Void Specters in level 3. As for level 4, only Tian Yuchen—the man who has remained at the top of the rankings for over a thousand years—was powerful enough to defeat the Void Specters there."
Yuan swallowed nervously at this information.
'Does this mean that the Void Specters within level 3 are on par with Eternals?!' he cried inwardly. 'The Eternal Essence they leave behind must be tremendous! I need to train there!'
The Ironwoman narrowed her eyes at Yuan's expression and said, "You're not very good at hiding your intentions, are you? If you're thinking about going to a level 2 Black Zone—"
"No, I am thinking about level 3 and beyond," he quickly interrupted, which left her speechless and dumbfounded.
"Then you must have a death wish, because even I wouldn't dare to—"
The Ironwoman abruptly stopped mid-sentence, though not because Yuan had interrupted her again.
"I can sense other presences nearby," she said a moment later.

Of course, Yuan had sensed them as well. In fact, he had been aware of their presence for quite some time. He hadn't bothered mentioning it since there was nothing unusual about encountering other people in the Black Zone.
A few moments later, the Ironwoman spoke again. "Be careful. They're heading straight toward us."
Yuan raised an eyebrow. "You sound tense. Is there really a reason to be so wary?"
"I wouldn't be if they were from our city. Unfortunately, they're not," she replied.
"So they're from another city? This will be my first time meeting people from outside our city," Yuan remarked, a hint of excitement in his voice.
"Don't get too excited. Encountering soldiers from another city isn't always a good thing," she warned.

chapters.title: Chapter 2633 Scorpion Squad's Interrogation
paragraphs: Some time later, Yuan spotted six silhouettes approaching from the distance.

Once they drew close enough for him to make out their appearances, the first thing that caught his attention was their attire, which differed noticeably from the military uniforms he had grown accustomed to.
The Ironwoman moved to hover beside Yuan before addressing the approaching group in a calm yet cold tone.
"How can we help you?"
The group did not respond immediately. Instead, their gazes settled on the insignias worn by Yuan and the Ironwoman, silently examining them.
"A corporal and a major? Are the two of you lost or something?" one of them finally asked.
"No, we're not lost," the Ironwoman replied.
"I know you're trying to put on a brave front, but there's no shame in asking for help, even if we're from different cities."
In their eyes, there was only one reasonable explanation for why two soldiers would be wandering the Black Zone alone—the rest of their squad had perished.
"But still... sending a mere corporal into the Black Zone? Is Gaia's Heaven's military really in such a dire state right now?" another soldier remarked with a weird look on his face.
"I won't repeat myself. We're not lost, so you can leave us alone."
"Hey, asshole, we're only trying to help!" one of the soldiers snapped. "You should watch your mouth, especially when you're practically alone out here!"
"That sounds like a threat," the Ironwoman said calmly.
"So what if it—"
"Shut up!" another soldier suddenly interrupted, clamping a hand over his companion's mouth. "Look closely! A major wearing a mask—that's the Ironwoman!"
"Is it true? You're the famous Ironwoman of Gaia's Heaven?"
"And what if it's true?"
"T-Then there's no doubt that you don't need any help. We apologize if we'd offended you."
Without another word, these soldiers turned around and swiftly flew away.
"What was that about?" Yuan asked afterward.
"What do you mean?"
"Was that attitude really necessary? They were only trying to help us, weren't they?"
"Perhaps," the Ironwoman replied. "But nothing good ever comes from getting involved with soldiers from another city. It's better if we simply keep our distance from one another."
"Why is that? Are our cities at war with each other or something? What warrants so much caution?" Yuan asked with a raised eyebrow.

"We may not be at war, but we still compete over resources," she replied. "In this world, nothing is more valuable than Unknown Ores and Unknown Crystals, since they serve as the primary source of energy for practically everything."

"Soldiers from the same military are forbidden from harming one another, but that restriction doesn't apply to soldiers from different cities, which is why altercations between soldiers from different cities are extremely common and borderline expected."

"While it's entirely possible that they genuinely wanted to help, there's an even greater chance they were simply trying to confirm whether we were alone before deciding to rob—or even kill—us," she added after a brief moment of silence. "There's a reason they left the moment they recognized who I was.
"I'll keep that in mind the next time I have another encounter with soldiers from another city," Yuan said.
Some time later, Yuan resumed hunting Void Specters throughout the Black Zone while the Ironwoman quietly observed him and helped him pick up Unknown Ores.

A few weeks later, she finally said, "I think I've seen enough. It's obvious that you have no trouble surviving out here on your own, so I'll leave you be and return to the city. General Mei is probably losing her mind by now, especially since you never returned with the Scorpion Squad."
"I thought you'd never leave," Yuan joked.
After a moment of silence, the Ironwoman asked, "How long do you plan on staying out here?"
"A few more months, probably."
"Try to return within a year," the Ironwoman said before turning around to leave.

However, after moving a few meters, she suddenly stopped. Without looking back, she asked in a puzzled tone, "I was expecting you to ask about my mask. Aren't you curious why I wear it? Or what I look like underneath?"
Yuan smiled. "Not really."
Since he already knew what she looked like beneath the mask, there was no reason for him to ask. Of course, revealing that would only invite questions he'd rather not answer.
"That feels like a rejection for some reason," the Ironwoman remarked in a joking tone.

Just as she was about to leave again, the Ironwoman suddenly turned her head and reached for her mask. Without saying a word, she removed it, revealing her beautiful face with a playful smile to Yuan.
Yuan raised an eyebrow at her actions and asked, "Are you sure you want to reveal your face to me?"
"Since you showed me some of your secrets, I figured that I'd show you one of mine to be fair."

The Ironwoman quickly wore her mask again and said, "Anyway, stay safe out here. If you die, I won't be able to face General Mei again. Oh, right. As for your Unknown Ores, I'll store them for you until you return."
Yuan silently nodded.
Once the Ironwoman left, Yuan returned to his training.
Meanwhile, back at the military base, the Scorpion Squad was taken in for interrogation the moment they returned to the city.

To ensure the interrogation was conducted fairly, General Mei wasn't the only high-ranking officer present. Several other senior officers attended as witnesses, and even General Gu was required to be there.
"So you admit to bringing Corporal Yuan outside the city?" one of the interrogators asked.
"Yes," Captain Chen answered truthfully.
"Where did you take him?"
"To the Purple Zone."
"For what purpose?"
"To clear a tunnel.
"And why did you choose Corporal Yuan for that?"
"To verify the recent rumors."

The interrogator narrowed his eyes. "According to those rumors, Corporal Yuan is capable of defeating a Void Guardian by himself—but only one from the Red Zone. Yet you brought him into the Purple Zone. What was your reasoning behind that decision?"
"We initially planned only for the Red Zone, but Corporal Yuan insisted he wanted something more challenging, so we brought him to the Purple Zone instead."
"What happened in the Purple Zone? Why did you return without Corporal Yuan?" the interrogator asked.

"Everything went smoothly at first. We even managed to clear the tunnel in the Purple Zone. However, just as we were preparing to return, Corporal Yuan said he wanted to take a look at the Black Zone."
"Of course, we were against it at first, but he insisted that he wouldn't leave until he had seen the Black Zone for himself."
"And then? What happened?"

"We traveled to the Black Zone—or at least to its border. However, Corporal Yuan wasn't satisfied with merely looking at it from the outside and entered by himself. We tried to follow him, but he was too fast. The Black Zone was far too dangerous for us to pursue him any deeper, so we decided to return to the city and report what had happened."
Captain Chen paused briefly before continuing, "That was when we encountered the Stellar Squad and were arrested."
Once they finished interrogating Captain Chen, they brought in the next member of the Scorpion Squad. Each of them was questioned separately until every member had given their testimony.
Unsurprisingly, they all gave similar answers.
"A bunch of nonsense!" General Mei sneered in disdain after hearing their testimony. "Why the hell would Corporal Yuan enter the Black Zone all by himself?! That makes no sense at all!"
"I must agree with General Mei. Nobody would be stupid enough to enter the Black Zone alone, especially someone who'd just recently joined the military."
General Gu then spoke. "Corporal Yuan is an unusual and rather arrogant individual. It wouldn't surprise me if he entered the Black Zone purely out of overconfidence."
He paused briefly before adding, "It's unfortunate, but I highly doubt Corporal Yuan can survive in there alone."

Another officer then spoke. "We can discuss Corporal Yuan later. Right now, we should focus on the Scorpion Squad. Although they didn't break any rules by bringing Corporal Yuan outside the city, if he truly is dead, they should still be held responsible for failing to ensure his safety—regardless of the choices Corporal Yuan made while outside."

"That hardly seems fair to the Scorpion Squad. They didn't do anything wrong, and it was Corporal Yuan who insisted on entering the Purple Zone, let alone the Black Zone. I don't think they should be blamed for his death, much less held responsible for it," another officer argued, one publicly known to support General Gu.

"That's assuming the Scorpion Squad is telling the truth," remarked an officer seated beside General Mei. "For all we know, they could've deliberately brought Corporal Yuan, who didn't know any better, into the Black Zone and abandoned him there to die."
"That's a serious accusation, Colonel Jing. Do you have any proof that they intended to do such a thing?"
Colonel Jing sneered. "I could ask you the same question. Do you have any proof that they didn't bring Corporal Yuan outside with the intention of getting him killed?"
"The fact that the system hasn't branded any of them as traitors should be more than enough proof of their innocence!"
"There are plenty of ways to circumvent the system, and we all know that the Scorpion Squad is notorious for bending and breaking the rules."
For the next several minutes, the officers on both sides continued arguing back and forth, neither willing to concede to the other.
