chapters.title: Chapter 2634 Verdict
paragraphs: "Although the Scorpion Squad is infamous for causing trouble, that was a long time ago!" one of the officers on General Gu's side exclaimed. "Besides, what reason would they have to want Corporal Yuan dead? It's not as though they have any grudges against him!"
"We all know why they want him dead!"
The officers on General Mei's side immediately turned their gazes toward General Gu, who remained seated in silence with a calm, almost indifferent expression.
The reason was obvious to everyone in the room, especially after General Mei's recent accusations against him. Even so, not a single person dared to say it aloud.
Seeing this, General Gu turned toward Mei Feng.
"Do you see this, General Mei? Because of your baseless accusations, everyone now thinks I want Corporal Yuan dead."
"..." Mei Feng remained silent.
"Since we're already on the subject, let me ask you directly—have you found any evidence to support those accusations? Or do you intend to keep tarnishing my reputation with nothing but lies?"
The room instantly fell deathly silent, with many of the officers holding their breath as they waited for Mei Feng's response.
After what felt like an eternity, she finally spoke.
"Whatever evidence I possess is not something I intend to reveal here. Once everything is properly prepared, I'll hand it over to the appropriate authorities."
General Gu sneered in disdain at her response and said, "So you intend to drag the Supreme General into your lies, huh? I have underestimated your recklessness!"
"If you're truly innocent, you would have nothing to worry about, and I will bear all responsibility for my actions."
General Gu suddenly rose from his seat. "I'm leaving. As for the Scorpion Squad, I'll leave their fate in General Mei's hands, even if that means innocent soldiers may end up suffering for it."
He turned toward the exit.
"I want to see just how far her madness will go."
Without another word, he left the room shortly afterward.
A few other officers from General Gu's side also left, but some of them remained.
"What are you going to do about the Scorpion Squad, General?" someone eventually asked Mei Feng.
Mei Feng closed her eyes and took a deep breath before giving her verdict, "Release them."
"What?!"

Her own officers exclaimed in shock, as none of them expected her to let the Scorpion Squad go for killing Yuan. Even those from General Gu's side were surprised by her verdict and stared at her with widened eyes.

Mei Feng continued, elaborating on her decision. "Regardless of my personal opinion of the Scorpion Squad—or what I believe their true intentions were—the fact remains that we don't have enough concrete evidence to convict them."
"But—"

"Moreover!" Mei Feng interrupted before the officer could continue. "There's still no proof that Corporal Yuan is dead. The Ironwoman is out there searching for him as we speak, so we'll postpone the Scorpion Squad's final verdict until we know more."

As much as Mei Feng wanted to find the Scorpion Squad guilty and punish them for Yuan's presumed death, she was still a general. No matter how strongly she felt, even she couldn't ignore military procedure and pass judgment based solely on suspicion.

"Also, to prevent something like this from happening again, effective immediately, soldiers of any rank are forbidden from taking personnel into areas they are not qualified to enter. Furthermore, all soldiers leaving the city will be required to officially check out at the gate."
Before anyone could voice their thoughts on the decision, Mei Feng turned around and left the room.

Shortly afterward, the Scorpion Squad was released from custody. However, they were far from completely free. Until a final verdict was reached, every member was prohibited from leaving the military base.
It didn't take long before word of the situation spread like wildfire throughout the military base.
"Did you hear? The Scorpion Squad is suspected of luring Corporal Yuan outside the city to kill him!"
"The Scorpion Squad? Why am I not surprised it's them? But why would they do something like that? Did Corporal Yuan somehow offend them?"

"Don't tell anyone I told you this, but according to some people, the Scorpion Squad was acting on General Gu's behalf. Apparently, he holds a grudge against Corporal Yuan for refusing to join his division.
"General Gu, huh? I can believe that, especially considering how bitter he's been ever since the Ironwoman appeared."
"So what's going to happen to the Scorpion Squad?"
"They're released for now, but it's still possible for them to be responsible for Corporal Yuan's death."
"What a pity... Corporal Yuan's death, I mean. He was so talented and was likely to surpass the Ironwoman."
Meanwhile, in a private room, Sergeant Bing sighed aloud, "It's my fault. I should've kept a closer eye on him."
"No, it's my fault. It was my turn to look after him on that day..." Sergeant Quang shook his head.
"You're acting like he's already dead..." Wu Wang said. "Knowing that guy, he's probably still alive."
"No matter how talented he is, there's no way he can deal with five captains by himself," said Sergeant Quang with a frown on his face.
"I... wouldn't be so sure about that," said Shi Fa.
At the same time, the Scorpion Squad went to report the situation to their superior. Of course, this superior wasn't General Gu, as that would be too obvious.
"Tell me what I want to hear."
"Corporal Yuan is dead," said Captain Chen.
"Did you see it with your own eyes?"
"Are you certain? Because according to your testimony, he went into the Black Zone and vanished."
Captain Dung sneered. "What else were we supposed to tell them? That we made sure Corporal Yuan died before our eyes?"
After a moment of silence, Captain Chen asked, "What's going to happen to us now?"

"If you're worried that something might happen to you, then understand this—you would've already been punished if they had enough evidence. The delayed verdict is most likely just a way to buy them more time to continue investigating."

"Even if Corporal Yuan is ultimately presumed dead and you're held responsible for what happened to him, the most likely punishment would be a demotion for failing to ensure his safety, which is essentially a slap on the wrist. Of course, we'll help you regain your rank back as fast as possible."
"What if Corporal Yuan returns?" one of the members suddenly asked.
"Is there any reason why you would even have such a thought?"
The superior frowned.
"N-No... I spoke without thinking just now."
The other members glared at him, but none of them dared to utter another word, fearing the truth might get out.
"In any case, stay put and don't leave your living quarters until the situation dies down."
"Yes, Colonel Ran."

"I'm back."
The Ironwoman's voice resounded as the door opened a moment later.
Seeing the Ironwoman return alone, Mei Feng sank back into her seat and let out a defeated sigh.
"So... he really is dead, huh?"
However, the Ironwoman ignored the remark and asked, "What happened to the Scorpion Squad?"
"We don't have enough evidence to charge them with murder or conspiracy," Mei Feng replied. "At most, we can hold them responsible for negligence and failing to protect a junior soldier."
"Did you already give the final verdict?"
"No, I was just about to leave to do that. I have delayed it for as long as I could, too."
"Do as you please. It won't matter, anyway."

"I mean, Corporal Yuan is still alive."
"WHAT?!" Mei Feng slammed the desk as she stood up with a bewildered look on her face.
"H-Has he returned?! Where is he now?!"
However, the Ironwoman shook her head and said, "I'll tell you where he is as long as you promise me that you won't get angry at me."
"What the hell are you talking about? Why would I be angry at you?"
The Ironwoman suddenly removed her mask and rubbed her eyes.
"Corporal Yuan... is still outside the city. In fact, he's currently in the Black Zone."
"W-What...?" Mei Feng muttered with a dazed expression.
"He said it was the perfect opportunity for him to train alone, and he told me to return without him."
After a moment of silence, Mei Feng began to tremble.
"ARE YOU INSANE?!" she shouted, slamming her desk so hard that it smashed into countless pieces.
"Hey, you promised not to be angry."
"I made no such promise!" Mei Feng exclaimed before falling silent again.
"You actually left him behind? In the Black Zone? Alone?" she muttered in disbelief some moments later.
"Don't make it sound like I did it on purpose. He insisted on being left alone."
"I don't care what he said! You should've dragged him back, even if it was against his will!"
The Ironwoman shook her head and said, "You can say that because you don't know what he's fully capable of."
"What are you talking about?"
"You really think I didn't consider dragging him back here?" the Ironwoman sighed.
"I won't go into the details because I made a promise, but I don't think I could've dragged him back here without killing him, so I'd be bringing back his corpse if I went that route."
Mei Feng stared at her with a baffled face, as if unable to believe her own ears.
"In any case, there's no need to worry about him. He'll return in a few months once he's done," the Ironwoman continued in a confident voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 2635 Verdict(2)
paragraphs: "Unbelievable..." Mei Feng was at a loss for words after learning of Yuan's situation through the Ironwoman.
"And I mean both you and Corporal Yuan."
"Can you really blame me? I already told you that dragging him back by force would've been nearly impossible without killing him."
"You know, I'm having a hard time believing that someone who only recently joined the military could give you this much trouble..." Mei Feng muttered.
She paused before adding, "No, forget the military. If you knew what his cultivation was just a year ago, you wouldn't believe it either."
"What are you talking about?" the Ironwoman asked, raising an eyebrow as curiosity flickered in her eyes.
Mei Feng pondered for a moment whether she should really tell her this.
"That man... his cultivation was only at the First Ascension a year ago when I met him."
"Wh-What did you just say...?"
The Ironwoman's eyes immediately widened, looking like she'd just seen a ghost.
Mei Feng chuckled at the Ironwoman's reaction, as it was the first time she'd seen her look so surprised.

'I cannot even begin to imagine how she'd react if she knew that he also possessed the Perfected Heavenly Refinement physique...' Mei Feng thought to herself, but she had no intention of revealing this secret.
"I have so many questions..." the Ironwoman spoke after a long moment of silence.
However, Mei Feng shook her head and said, "Keep them to yourself because I won't be able to answer them."
The Ironwoman sighed before responding, "Anyways, what are you going to do now that he's alive?"

Mei Feng closed her eyes to ponder for several minutes before speaking again, "I will continue to act like he's dead until he actually returns to the city safe and sound. As for the verdict, there will be no change—at least until Corporal Yuan returns to testify against them. As for what comes after that... we can only wait and see."
"Alright." The Ironwoman nodded before retrieving a cube-shaped object and casually tossing it into Mei Feng's grasp.
"Give it to him when he returns," said the Ironwoman as she turned around and started leaving.
"If he doesn't return, his blood will be on your hands," Mei Feng said in a low voice.
Without stopping, the Ironwoman reached for the door.
"I know," she responded before leaving the room.
Mei Feng sat back in her chair and released a deep sigh.
"That brat..."
She looked at the storage cube in her grasp before taking a peek inside.
"So many Unknown Ores!"
Mei Feng's eyes widened with surprise to see its storage filled to the brim with Unknown Ores, wondering why the Ironwoman wanted to give them to Yuan.
'Did she gather these while looking for him...? There's no way, right?'

As far as Mei Feng knew, the Ironwoman never bothered to collect Unknown Ores herself, considering it a waste of her time and effort. She typically left such menial tasks to her squad members, so seeing her return with so many was rather unusual.
Some time later, Mei Feng left to give her final verdict on the Scorpion Squad—but not before calling someone to have her desk replaced.

Once Mei Feng gave her final verdict, every member of the Scorpion Squad was demoted by one rank, which may not seem like a lot, but going from Captain to Sergeant meant they'd lost at least two to three decades of their lives.
It didn't take long before the news spread.
"Doesn't this mean that Corporal Yuan is truly dead?"
"A pity... a true pity..."
The news got so big that it'd even reached the soldiers training in boot camp.
"What?! The monster from the same recruitment as us was killed?!"
Mei Xiaoyun's entire body froze upon hearing the news, her eyes widening in shock and disbelief.
'Yuan's dead...? There's no way...' she thought to herself.
Then, she approached one of the instructors and asked for more information.
"About Corporal Yuan... is it true that he's dead?"
"That's right. It was already known a few weeks ago, but it wasn't confirmed until recently.
"Do you know what happened?"
The instructor sighed and said, "Do you know of the Scorpion Squad?"
"No."

"Well, they're a group of troublemakers, and supposedly, they lured Corporal Yuan to the Black Zone to have him killed. Of course, that's what some people believe is the truth. Unfortunately, we may never know."
Mei Xiaoyun frowned. "Why would they want him dead? Did Corporal Yuan offend them somehow?"
The instructor looked at her with a hesitant expression.
"I normally wouldn't tell another soldier something like this, but considering you're General Mei's daughter, you would probably find out sooner or later anyway..."

The instructor proceeded to explain, "General Mei and General Gu are currently competing to become the next Supreme General. With General Mei already supported by the Ironwoman—one of the most talented and respected soldiers in the military—General Gu has been under immense pressure."

"He likely saw Corporal Yuan as someone who could balance the scales in his favor. Unfortunately for him, Corporal Yuan ended up joining General Mei's side instead. If Corporal Yuan grows into someone comparable to the Ironwoman, General Mei's promotion would be all but guaranteed. That gives General Gu plenty of reason to want him gone."
"Is that so..." Mei Xiaoyun muttered, looking dazed.
After a moment of silence, Mei Xiaoyun spoke again. "Instructor, I'm not feeling well today, so I won't be participating in training."
"O-Okay..."

Normally, soldiers weren't allowed to decide for themselves when to attend training. However, Mei Xiaoyun was General Mei's daughter and the top performer among the new soldiers, so the instructors tended to be far more lenient with her.
Moreover, it was obvious that the news of Yuan's presumed death had affected her deeply. Allowing her to train while she was emotionally distracted could potentially put her in danger.
Once Mei Xiaoyun returned to the barracks, the instructors began chatting among themselves.
"I wonder what her relationship with Corporal Yuan is."
"Do you really need to ask? Isn't it already obvious enough by how she reacted to the news of his death? I'd bet an entire year's salary that they're lovers!"

chapters.title: Chapter 2636 A Soldier Or a Bandit?
paragraphs: Another two months passed after news of Yuan's presumed death spread throughout the military.

Because of the incident, the Scorpion Squad had become one of the most hated squads in the entire military and were constantly harassed and bullied by other soldiers, particularly those aligned with General Mei.
At first, almost no one was willing to stand up for them. However, as time passed, more and more soldiers from General Gu's side began stepping in to protect them.
Whenever someone confronted the Scorpion Squad, the encounter almost always devolved into a heated argument or outright brawl.

Although Yuan was still a new soldier, he had already earned a favorable reputation among his peers, largely because he frequently helped others during gathering missions—work that most soldiers considered tedious and burdensome.
However, the Scorpion Squad couldn't care less about the situation or being targeted. They were simply relieved that Yuan had not returned to the city, as that could spell their end.
Meanwhile, in the Black Zone, Yuan had been hunting Void Specters nonstop, continuously increasing his Eternal Essence.

Though for efficiency, he did not simply wander the Black Zone killing Void Specters. Whenever he would encounter a tunnel, he would enter it and clear it alone, as the Elite Void Specters and Unknown Crystals found inside granted the most Eternal Essence.
One day, purely by coincidence, Yuan entered a tunnel that was already occupied by another group of soldiers.
The moment he sensed their presence, he concealed his own. However, rather than leaving, he decided to clear the tunnel before they did.
Fortunately, the tunnel branched into numerous paths, allowing Yuan to easily avoid the other group, slip past them unnoticed, and reach the end long before they could.

After defeating the Void Guardian at the end of the tunnel, Yuan absorbed all of the Eternal Essence contained within the Unknown Crystals before swiftly making his way out, leaving the other soldiers completely unaware that someone had beaten them to their destination.
Several days after Yuan secretly cleared the tunnel, the soldiers finally reached the end, but to their shock and puzzlement, the Void Guardian was nowhere to be seen.
"What the heck? Where's the Void Guardian?"=
"Did someone already clear this tunnel?" another soldier wondered aloud.

Although it wasn't unheard of for two groups to enter the same tunnel without realizing it until they reached the end, the soldiers quickly dismissed that possibility. If another group had truly arrived before them, the Unknown Crystals should have been harvested as well, yet every single one remained untouched.
"Don't tell me that this tunnel was created without a Void Guardian?"
"This would be an unprecedented event if that were the case!"
In the end, the soldiers decided to document the unusual occurrence before harvesting the Unknown Crystals and leaving the tunnel.
They then hastily returned to their city to report the discovery.
In the third month of wandering the Black Zone, Yuan had his second encounter with soldiers from another city.
Although Yuan could have easily avoided the soldiers, he decided to see for himself whether encounters with people from another city were truly as dangerous as the Ironwoman had warned.
"What the—?"
The soldiers froze the moment they saw Yuan. While encountering someone alone in the Black Zone was surprising enough, what shocked them even more was the insignia on his uniform.
"Am I seeing things, or is this guy a corporal?"
"He's definitely a corporal."
"What is a corporal doing out here alone—"
"Look around him! There are Unknown Ores everywhere!"
However, their curiosity about Yuan's presence vanished the moment they noticed the countless Unknown Ores glistening across the ground beneath him.
The soldiers exchanged glances, greed flickering in their eyes.
A moment later, one of them turned toward Yuan and shouted, "Kid, if you don't want any more trouble than you're already in, leave those Unknown Ores alone!"
Yuan calmly responded, "If you want the Unknown Ores, go ahead and take them."
Without a word, the soldiers immediately went to gather the Unknown Ores into their storage cube while Yuan quietly watched them.
Suddenly, one of them approached Yuan with a cold smile and said, "While we're at it, hand over all of your belongings."
In his eyes, the only reason Yuan would leave behind so many Unknown Ores was that his storage cube had already reached its capacity, leaving him with no way to carry the rest.
"Are you a soldier, or are you a bandit?" Yuan asked with a raised eyebrow.
"Who the hell gave you permission to question me?" the soldier frowned. "I will not ask again. Hand over all of your belongings!"
Yuan shrugged and said, "The only thing I have is this minigun. You can have it if you want."
"You dare mess with me?! Do you have a death wish?!" the soldier shouted, believing that Yuan was deliberately mocking him.

"So you're not only a bandit, but a murderer as well?" Yuan asked with an indifferent expression. "Which city are you from? So I know when to stay away from your people the next time I encounter them."
The soldier trembled in anger before lunging at Yuan with killing intent.
"There won't be a next time!"
Seeing this, Yuan released a disappointing sigh.
The next moment, a tremendous amount of Eternal Essence erupted from Yuan's body.

Although the soldiers were unable to sense the energy itself, they immediately felt the atmosphere around him change. In an instant, Yuan's entire presence became completely different—far heavier and more imposing than before.
"What—"
Before the soldier could even react, his head vanished from his neck.

The soldiers who had been busy collecting the Unknown Ores abruptly stopped and turned toward Yuan. However, the moment they saw their companion hovering before him without a head, they froze in stunned silence, struggling to comprehend what they were even looking at.
"C-Captain Hong!"
The soldiers eventually snapped out of their daze and cried out loud, their eyes wide with shock and disbelief.

After defeating the Void Guardian at the end of the tunnel, Yuan absorbed all of the Eternal Essence contained within the Unknown Crystals before swiftly making his way out, leaving the other soldiers completely unaware that someone had beaten them to their destination.
Several days after Yuan secretly cleared the tunnel, the soldiers finally reached the end, but to their shock and puzzlement, the Void Guardian was nowhere to be seen.
"What the heck?
Where's the Void Guardian?"=
"Did someone already clear this tunnel?" another soldier wondered aloud.
Although it wasn't unheard of for two groups to enter the same tunnel without realizing it until they reached the end, the soldiers quickly dismissed that possibility.
If another group had truly arrived before them, the Unknown Crystals should have been harvested as well, yet every single one remained untouched.
"Don't tell me that this tunnel was created without a Void Guardian?"
"This would be an unprecedented event if that were the case!"
In the end, the soldiers decided to document the unusual occurrence before harvesting the Unknown Crystals and leaving the tunnel.
They then hastily returned to their city to report the discovery.
In the third month of wandering the Black Zone, Yuan had his second encounter with soldiers from another city.
Although Yuan could have easily avoided the soldiers, he decided to see for himself whether encounters with people from another city were truly as dangerous as the Ironwoman had warned.
"What the—?"
The soldiers froze the moment they saw Yuan.
While encountering someone alone in the Black Zone was surprising enough, what shocked them even more was the insignia on his uniform.
"Am I seeing things, or is this guy a corporal?"
"He's definitely a corporal."
"What is a corporal doing out here alone—"
"Look around him!
There are Unknown Ores everywhere!"
However, their curiosity about Yuan's presence vanished the moment they noticed the countless Unknown Ores glistening across the ground beneath him.
The soldiers exchanged glances, greed flickering in their eyes.
A moment later, one of them turned toward Yuan and shouted, "Kid, if you don't want any more trouble than you're already in, leave those Unknown Ores alone!"
Yuan calmly responded, "If you want the Unknown Ores, go ahead and take them."
Without a word, the soldiers immediately went to gather the Unknown Ores into their storage cube while Yuan quietly watched them.
Suddenly, one of them approached Yuan with a cold smile and said, "While we're at it, hand over all of your belongings."
In his eyes, the only reason Yuan would leave behind so many Unknown Ores was that his storage cube had already reached its capacity, leaving him with no way to carry the rest.
"Are you a soldier, or are you a bandit?" Yuan asked with a raised eyebrow.
"Who the hell gave you permission to question me?" the soldier frowned.
"I will not ask again.
Hand over all of your belongings!"
Yuan shrugged and said, "The only thing I have is this minigun.
You can have it if you want."
"You dare mess with me?!
Do you have a death wish?!" the soldier shouted, believing that Yuan was deliberately mocking him.
"So you're not only a bandit, but a murderer as well?" Yuan asked with an indifferent expression.
"Which city are you from?
So I know when to stay away from your people the next time I encounter them."
The soldier trembled in anger before lunging at Yuan with killing intent.
"There won't be a next time!"
Seeing this, Yuan released a disappointing sigh.
The next moment, a tremendous amount of Eternal Essence erupted from Yuan's body.
Although the soldiers were unable to sense the energy itself, they immediately felt the atmosphere around him change.
In an instant, Yuan's entire presence became completely different—far heavier and more imposing than before.
"What—"
Before the soldier could even react, his head vanished from his neck.
The soldiers who had been busy collecting the Unknown Ores abruptly stopped and turned toward Yuan.
However, the moment they saw their companion hovering before him without a head, they froze in stunned silence, struggling to comprehend what they were even looking at.
"C-Captain Hong!"
The soldiers eventually snapped out of their daze and cried out loud, their eyes wide with shock and disbelief.

chapters.title: Chapter 2637 A New Type of Void Specter
paragraphs: "Bastard! What did you do to Captain Hong?!"
The rest of the squad swiftly acted, moving to surround Yuan.
"Isn't it obvious what I did to him just looking at his headless corpse?" Yuan responded in an indifferent tone.
"W-Why?! Why did you kill him?!" another soldier shouted.
"Why...? Are you asking me why I defended myself?" Yuan shook his head before continuing, "If you're going to continue uttering nonsense, then save your breath."
"You damn—"
The soldiers surged with killing intent at Yuan's words.
"Are you sure you want to do this? You can still walk away with your life," Yuan said.
"You only managed to kill Captain Hong by surprise! Do not think we will make the same mistake!"
"And there are five of us and one of you. Do you really think you'll be able to kill all of us with your cultivation? Laughable!"
"Forget about five. Even if there were five thousand of you, I'd still be able to kill all of you."
"I want to see you try!"
The next moment, one of the soldiers used Void Control and teleported behind Yuan.
"Die!"
The soldier struck with the intent to kill.
However, the instant his hand touched Yuan's body, his entire body abruptly disintegrated into nothingness, vanishing from existence before he could even let out a scream.
"What just happened?!"
The remaining four soldiers instinctively backed away from Yuan after witnessing such a horrifying scene.
"W-What the fuck was that?! What did he do to Captain Dean?!"
"This guy is not human! He must be a Void Specter in disguise!"
"Run!"
The soldiers swiftly turned and ran away, their faces twisted with fear.
Yuan watched them run away, not bothering to chase after them.
'So that's what happens when I use my affinity on another human...' Yuan thought, shuddering slightly.
This was his first time using his affinity on anything other than materials, and the result far exceeded his expectations. Quite frankly, even Yuan found it terrifying.
'Let's not use it unless absolutely necessary...' he sighed inwardly.
Yuan continued his training shortly after.

Meanwhile, the soldiers from the encounter went straight back to their city, not stopping to rest until they reached their military base. Upon their return, they reported their encounter with Yuan to their superior, describing him as a Void Specter who was indistinguishable from an ordinary human.
"What? A Void Specter indistinguishable from a human had killed Captain Hong and Captain Dean? That almost sounds like the Void Hunter!"
"No! This monster was something else entirely! The moment Captain Dean came into contact with this monster, his entire body disintegrated like ash!"
"Hell, it can even speak like a normal human!"
"This is definitely a new type of Void Specter!"
"Where did you find this monster?" the superior asked.
"In the level 1 Black Zone!"
The superior pondered for a long moment before speaking again, "I am going to prepare a squad of eight powerful soldiers, and I want one of you to bring them to the location."
"You want to fight that monster?! It's better to avoid it! I'm telling you!"
"Listen here. If another monster that is on par with the Void Hunter—especially if it is indistinguishable from an ordinary human—we need to investigate it properly, regardless of the risks."

The superior released a deep sigh before continuing, "I will let you guys discuss among yourselves who wants to take the job. I don't want to force anyone, but if a decision is not reached by the time the team is assembled, I will have all of you go. If you volunteer, I will make sure you're rewarded properly. Do I make myself clear?"
"Yes, Colonel..."
A few days later, the team was assembled, and one of the soldiers who'd encountered Yuan willingly volunteered to accept the mission.
"I'm Captain Heen, and I'll brief you on this monster while we make our way to its location.
Thus, Captain Heen and eight powerful soldiers—all holding the rank of major—set out for the Black Zone to investigate the newly discovered monster.
At the same time, the other soldiers who encountered Yuan handed in the Unknown Ores they'd gathered with his approval.
A few days later, all of these soldiers were summoned by the General of their military.
"Where did you acquire these Unknown Ores?" the General questioned them while pointing to the pile of glistening ores before him.
"We collected them during our previous mission," replied the soldiers.
"Why? Is there something wrong with them?" another asked.
However, the General didn't answer this question and continued to ask, "Did you do anything special with them?"
"No, not that I can think of. We immediately returned to the city after gathering them because of that monster who killed two of our members."
"Tell me how you managed to gather them again?"
The soldiers went on to reveal that the Unknown Ores originally belonged to the monster and that they'd taken them from him.
Once he was satisfied, the General spoke, revealing why he was questioning them, "The Unknown Ores you gathered... not a single one of them contains any energy!"
"What?!"
The soldiers exclaimed in disbelief.
"H-How is that even possible? If they truly lack energy, they wouldn't be glistening like that! At least, they shouldn't!"
"I don't know, but we can assume that this monster you encountered had something to do with it," said the General.
The soldiers swallowed nervously, as this monster was becoming increasingly incomprehensible.
Some time later, the special squad arrived at their destination in the Black Zone.
"This is the place. Look on the ground. The Unknown Ores left behind by him are still here!" Captain Heen said, pointing toward the trail of Unknown Ores Yuan had left behind.
"This is..."
The soldiers swallowed nervously as they stared at the scattered ores. There was something deeply unsettling about the sight, though none of them could quite put the feeling into words.
"It feels like a trap, as though someone deliberately left these ores behind to lure us in," one of them finally said, voicing what everyone else was thinking.

chapters.title: Chapter 2638 Following the Trail
paragraphs: "What should we do? It's clearly inviting—provoking us."
"There's only one thing we can do. Our mission."
"Stay alert, everyone. And don't engage without instructions."
The group of soldiers slowly followed the trail of Unknown Ores while keeping their presence concealed to the best of their abilities.
Meanwhile, not too far away, Yuan just finished clearing a tunnel all by himself. But before he could even exit the tunnel, he sensed several presences outside the tunnel.
'They are...'
Once he exited the tunnel, he could see several familiar-looking soldiers gathering the Unknown Ores that he'd left behind outside.
When Yuan came out of the tunnel, these soldiers stopped their movements to look at him.
"Huh? Aren't you that corporal with the Ironwoman? Did you just come out of that tunnel?" one of them asked out loud.
These soldiers were the ones that Yuan had encountered while he was still with the Ironwoman.
"Indeed, I did come out of the tunnel," Yuan replied.
The soldiers didn't say anything else and fell silent, but they continued to stare in Yuan's direction, almost as if they were waiting for someone else to show up.
Eventually, one of them asked, "Where's the Ironwoman?"
"She returned to the city," Yuan admitted.
"Huh? The Ironwoman left you—a mere corporal—all alone in the Black Zone? There's no way..."
"I don't believe you. I bet she's still inside that tunnel."

The soldiers found Yuan's explanation difficult to believe. Given the Ironwoman's reputation, they couldn't imagine her deliberately leaving a low-ranking soldier behind to fend for himself in such a dangerous place.
Yuan shrugged and said, "What do I gain from lying about this? You're free to check the tunnels if you don't believe me."
"N-No... It's fine..."
"But what were you doing inside the tunnel all by yourself? If you were looking for a place to hide, it's actually much more dangerous inside than outside."
"No, I was clearing it."
"You...? Clearing a tunnel? All by yourself?"
The soldiers fell silent again before they suddenly burst out laughing.
"Hahaha!
"Now that is definitely a lie!"
"There's no way a Fifth Ascension cultivator like you could accomplish something alone that would normally require an entire squad of Sixth Ascension cultivators!" one of them stated.
Yuan merely shrugged before turning to leave without another word.
"Hey! Where are you going?" one of the soldiers called out to him.
"Why does it matter where I am going?" Yuan asked.
"T-That's..." the soldier fell silent.
"If you have nothing else for me, I'll be taking my leave now."
"Aren't you going to ask about these Unknown Ores?" another soldier suddenly asked.
"Unless you're going to share them with me, I don't really care."
The soldiers raised their eyebrows. It should be obvious that they weren't going to share it with a soldier from another city.
"No? Then goodbye."
Yuan left shortly after, with nobody stopping him this time.
"Should we really have allowed him to leave?" one of the soldiers asked out loud after Yuan was no longer in their field of view.
"What else were we supposed to do? He's none of our business."
"I guess so..."
Some time later, the soldiers finally stopped gathering once their storage cubes were filled to the brim with Unknown Ores.
"After we clear this tunnel, let's return to the base and grab more storage cubes for the rest."

Although they wanted to continue collecting the ores, they simply had no space left to store them. Thus, they decided to clear the tunnel first and harvest the Unknown Crystals within before returning for the remaining ores.
"Just where the hell did all these Unknown Ores come from, anyways?" one of them asked as they ventured deeper into the tunnel.
"Why bother questioning it? Just treat it as some strange phenomenon—and a fortunate encounter for us."
"What are the chances that Corporal actually cleared the tunnel all by himself?" another wondered out loud.
"Seriously? There's literally no chance. If I am wrong, then I will eat my suit."
A few hours later—
"Hey... we haven't encountered a single Void Specter in hours..."
Although no one said it aloud, the same thought gradually began creeping into their minds.
'Could that corporal have really cleared this entire place by himself...?'

The deeper they ventured, the more believable the seemingly impossible feat became. Meanwhile, the soldier who had sworn he would eat his suit if Yuan had truly cleared the tunnel by himself began sweating more and more with every passing minute.
Eventually, they reached the end of the tunnel. Without encountering a single Void Specter, of course.
"What are the chances of a tunnel spawning without any Void Specters...?"
"Probably less likely than that Corporal clearing the tunnel alone..."
After staring down into the hole for a moment, the soldiers swallowed nervously before finally jumping through the opening.
Moments later, they landed at the bottom.
"N-No way..."
The soldiers stared at the empty chamber, their expressions dumbfounded, their eyes wide with shock and disbelief.
"He actually cleared the tunnel by himself?!"
"W-Wait! Let's not jump to conclusions!" said the soldier who swore he'd eat his suit. "If that were the case, why didn't he harvest the Unknown Crystals?!"
"How the hell would we know?"
"If he doesn't want them, we'll gladly take them for him!"
The soldiers started harvesting the Unknown Crystals after snapping out of their daze, unaware that they were essentially collecting pretty crystals with no energy.
Once they were done, they made their way back up the tunnel.
However, when they emerged from the tunnel, they were taken aback to find nine unknown soldiers wearing crimson uniforms surrounding the entrance.
"Soldiers of Ember City?!"
"W-We're being ambushed!"
The soldiers immediately armed themselves and prepared to fight.
"Wait! We're not here for you, soldiers of Spirit City!" exclaimed the soldiers of Ember City.
"What?"

"We're currently investigating a certain entity, and we've been following the trail of Unknown Ores it left behind," explained one of the soldiers from Ember City. "However, the trail abruptly ended here, so we suspected that it might have entered this tunnel."

chapters.title: Chapter 2639 Following the Trail(2)
paragraphs: "A trail of Unknown Ores...? In that case, it probably stopped here because we collected them," admitted one of the Spirit City soldiers.
"The tunnel was also empty. Hell, it'd been cleared even before we entered it."
"What sort of entity are you looking for, anyway?" another asked.
The soldiers of Ember City exchanged glances with each other, wondering if they should reveal any information to soldiers from another city.

However, after giving it some thought, they realized that if this mysterious Void Specter was anything like the Void Hunter, keeping the information to themselves would only put everyone at greater risk. It would be wiser to share what they knew so that the cities could work together to deal with the threat.
"As mentioned earlier, we're currently still investigating, but from what we know so far, this is a new type of Void Specter," said the Ember City soldier.
"Is that true?! A new type of Void Specter has been discovered?!"
The soldiers of Spirit City were shocked to hear this, which wasn't surprising, considering that it had been thousands of years since they had made such a discovery.
"Of course it's true. Why would we lie about something like this? This Void Specter has already killed two of our soldiers."
"What does this Void Specter look like? Any special characterization?"
"You'll probably find this hard to believe, but this Void Specter looks exactly like a human. Indistinguishable, too."
"A Void Specter with human features? Sounds like the Void Hunter."

"No, you don't understand. This Void Specter doesn't just look like a human. It is literally indistinguishable from a real human, meaning if it hid in a crowd of people, we wouldn't be able to tell it apart from the others. Hell, it can even speak the human language!"

"Is that even possible...? Are you sure this entity isn't a real human?" The soldiers of Spirit City wore doubtful expressions at this unbelievable information, wondering if this was just a big misunderstanding.
"It's possible, and that monster definitely wasn't human!" Captain Heen suddenly shouted.

"I—my squad encountered it, and the way that monster killed my squad member... there's no way a human is capable of vaporizing another human with a single touch!" Captain Heen's body trembled with fear just recalling the moment.
"Vaporized..."
"With a single touch...?
The soldiers of Spirit City muttered with a dazed look on their faces.

"Anyway, this Void Specter is currently disguised as a soldier from Gaia's Heaven. He has a tall, refined build, long black hair tied into a ponytail, brown eyes, and a strikingly handsome face. If you encounter him, do not engage under any circumstances. Run away immediately."
The soldiers of Spirit City raised an eyebrow at this familiar-sounding description.
"Oh, right. He's also wearing the insignia of a corporal," the Ember City soldier added.
"That reaction... did you see this monster?" asked Captain Chen after seeing their surprised face.
They nodded in slow motion before turning to look in the direction Yuan went.
"H-He went that way..."
"Thanks! Let's hurry up and chase after it!" Captain Heen said to the others.
"W-Wait!"
"What is it?"
"Are you really sure he's a Void Specter? I still think this is some kind of misunderstanding. After all, if he really is a Void Specter, why would he clear out a tunnel by himself?"
"What did you just say? That monster cleared out a tunnel by himself?" Captain Heen's eyes widened with disbelief at this unexpected information.

"That's right. We said this tunnel was empty, didn't we? Well, that wasn't our doing. That corporal came out of this tunnel while we were collecting the Unknown Ores. In fact, he even claimed that he had cleared the entire place by himself."
Captain Heen fell silent upon hearing this.
"What if this Void Specter grows stronger by consuming its own kind?" one of the Ember City soldiers suddenly suggested.
"Now that you mention it... we haven't encountered a single Void Specter since we started following the trail through the Black Zone!" another exclaimed at this realization.
"A Void Specter that devours its own kind...?"
The others swallowed nervously.
"Hm? Hold on. This is actually our second encounter with this corporal." One of the Spirit City soldiers suddenly remarked. "The first time we encountered him, he wasn't alone."
"Are you saying that there are actually two of these monsters wandering this land?!" Captain Heen exclaimed in shock.
"No...? That other individual with him is someone you should be familiar with, given her vast reputation."
"Who is this person?"
"It's the Ironwoman."
The place fell silent, and the soldiers of Ember City turned to look at Captain Heen, as even they were beginning to wonder if this had been a huge misunderstanding.
"T-That must be it!" Captain Heen suddenly exclaimed.
"What is?"
"The reason this monster looks exactly like a human! It must possess some kind of ability that allows it to perfectly imitate a human's appearance!"
The others stared at him with raised eyebrows, wondering if he'd gone crazy to think of such a crazy theory.

"Why are you all looking at me like I'm crazy?! Think about it! Would a mere corporal really be able to survive in the Black Zone for this long if he weren't actually a Void Specter in disguise?!" Captain Heen shouted, his voice growing louder with every word.
"That's..."
As ridiculous as Captain Heen's theory sounded, none of them could deny that it somehow seemed more plausible than a mere corporal surviving alone in the Black Zone for so long.
"Anyway, let's stop wasting time and continue pursuing that Void Specter. We can talk while we move."

"Do you mind if we come with you?" one of the Spirit City soldiers suddenly asked. "We've interacted with him several times without any issues, and I want to see for myself whether he's truly a Void Specter."
"Well..."

After a quick discussion, the Ember City soldiers said, "You can follow us if you want. However, keep some distance from us. With both groups together, we'd exceed ten people, and I'd rather not risk attracting the Void Hunter while we're already dealing with an unknown Void Specter."

sentences.text: "A trail of Unknown Ores...?
In that case, it probably stopped here because we collected them," admitted one of the Spirit City soldiers.
"The tunnel was also empty.
Hell, it'd been cleared even before we entered it."
"What sort of entity are you looking for, anyway?" another asked.
The soldiers of Ember City exchanged glances with each other, wondering if they should reveal any information to soldiers from another city.

However, after giving it some thought, they realized that if this mysterious Void Specter was anything like the Void Hunter, keeping the information to themselves would only put everyone at greater risk.
It would be wiser to share what they knew so that the cities could work together to deal with the threat.
"As mentioned earlier, we're currently still investigating, but from what we know so far, this is a new type of Void Specter," said the Ember City soldier.
"Is that true?!
A new type of Void Specter has been discovered?!"
The soldiers of Spirit City were shocked to hear this, which wasn't surprising, considering that it had been thousands of years since they had made such a discovery.
"Of course it's true.
Why would we lie about something like this?
This Void Specter has already killed two of our soldiers."
"What does this Void Specter look like?
Any special characterization?"
"You'll probably find this hard to believe, but this Void Specter looks exactly like a human.
Indistinguishable, too."
"A Void Specter with human features?
Sounds like the Void Hunter."
"No, you don't understand.
This Void Specter doesn't just look like a human.
It is literally indistinguishable from a real human, meaning if it hid in a crowd of people, we wouldn't be able to tell it apart from the others.
Hell, it can even speak the human language!"
"Is that even possible...?
Are you sure this entity isn't a real human?" The soldiers of Spirit City wore doubtful expressions at this unbelievable information, wondering if this was just a big misunderstanding.
"It's possible, and that monster definitely wasn't human!" Captain Heen suddenly shouted.

"I—my squad encountered it, and the way that monster killed my squad member... there's no way a human is capable of vaporizing another human with a single touch!" Captain Heen's body trembled with fear just recalling the moment.
"Vaporized..."
"With a single touch...?
The soldiers of Spirit City muttered with a dazed look on their faces.
"Anyway, this Void Specter is currently disguised as a soldier from Gaia's Heaven.
He has a tall, refined build, long black hair tied into a ponytail, brown eyes, and a strikingly handsome face.
If you encounter him, do not engage under any circumstances.
Run away immediately."
The soldiers of Spirit City raised an eyebrow at this familiar-sounding description.
"Oh, right.
He's also wearing the insignia of a corporal," the Ember City soldier added.
"That reaction... did you see this monster?" asked Captain Chen after seeing their surprised face.
They nodded in slow motion before turning to look in the direction Yuan went.
"H-He went that way..."
"Thanks!

"What is it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2640 Following the Trail(3)
paragraphs: "What do you guys think? What are the chances of that corporal being a Void Specter disguised as a human?" one of the Spirit City soldiers asked his squad mates as they followed the Ember City soldiers.
"I think it's entirely possible and, quite frankly, very likely. He always gave me a weird vibe, but I couldn't pinpoint it until now."
"Right? Something about him just felt off."
"Really? I, for one, don't think he's a Void Specter. I think I am just not ready to believe that a Void Specter has the capability to disguise itself as a human that perfectly... at least, not yet."
"That's reasonable. I also think he's not a Void Specter. After all, he didn't even try to attack us. A Void Specter that hunts its own kind and ignores humans? Hard to believe."
"Didn't he kill some of the Ember City's soldiers?"
"Well, we don't know the circumstances. They probably offended him or something. Did you see that captain's behavior earlier? There's definitely something very wrong with him."
Meanwhile, a few miles ahead of the Spirit City's soldiers, the Ember City's soldiers continued to follow the trail.

"If the Void Hunter can resemble humans, it's reasonable to believe that a special Void Specter who can perfectly copy a human's appearance exists!" Captain Heen spoke aloud, but he was mostly talking to himself.
"It's not that we don't believe you, but we'll reserve our judgment until we encounter—"
"I sense him!"
One of the soldiers there suddenly shouted, causing everyone to tense up and slow down.
"Hide your presence! We're going to inspect the subject first before engaging!"
Once everyone could see Yuan, they came to a complete halt to spectate him.
"Can you confirm that is the entity?" The majors turned to look at Captain Heen for confirmation.
"I-It's him! It's definitely him!" Captain Heen nodded vigorously, his body shaking nonstop.
Shortly later, the Spirit City's soldiers also came to a halt.
"That's the corporal, all right." They confirmed.
Meanwhile, Yuan sighed inwardly after detecting the Ember City's soldiers, 'There's even more of them now... Are they here for revenge?"
A moment later, he noticed the others.
'Hm? Aren't those guys from the tunnel? Why are they also here?'
Yet, Yuan decided to pretend that he hadn't noticed them, curious to see how the situation would unfold.
He continued to hunt Void Specters and absorb Unknown Ores, not caring if these soldiers could see everything.
"My lord! Do you see how fast he kills the Void Specters?! He's cleaning them up like trash!"
"And the way he collects Unknown Ores! I have never seen anything like that before!"
"Inhuman! Simply inhuman! He's definitely a Void Specter!"
It didn't take long for many of the Ember City soldiers to become convinced that Yuan wasn't human at all, but rather a Void Specter disguised as one.

"I told you that guy isn't human!" Captain Heen exclaimed, feeling vindicated now that the others were finally beginning to believe him, seemingly proving that his suspicions had been right all along.
As for the soldiers from Spirit City, they weren't as easily convinced. However, even they were beginning to understand why Captain Heen was so adamant that Yuan wasn't human.
"How is he using so much energy when his cultivation is only at the Fifth Ascension? Where is he getting his power from?"
"Isn't it obvious?!" Captain Heen responded. "He's recovering his energy from the Void Specters that he devours!"

"So he's the one digging up all those Unknown Ores and leaving them behind... No wonder he didn't seem the slightest bit interested in them before. But what could possibly be the purpose of doing that?" one of the Spirit City soldiers muttered.
"It's obviously a trap to lure us in! He knows how valuable Unknown Ores are to us, so he's using them as bait!"

"If that were really the case, then why didn't he kill us when he had plenty of opportunities to do so? We were literally collecting those Unknown Ores right in front of him—even talking to him while we did it!"
Captain Heen sneered. "How the hell would I know what it's thinking? Maybe you lot were simply too weak for it to even consider you prey."
The soldiers from Spirit City weren't particularly surprised by his remark. It was common for soldiers from different cities to mock or look down on one another, so they simply ignored the insult.

These soldiers continued to spectate Yuan from afar for several hours before one of them asked, "So, what now? Are we just going to keep watching him, or are we going to do something? There's only so much we can learn like this."
Captain Heen sneered and said, "If you're so impatient, why don't you go ahead and approach him yourself? In fact, anyone who thinks he isn't a Void Specter should just go ahead and approach him."
Even though some of these soldiers were still skeptical, they weren't willing to risk their lives for it, so they all fell silent and continued watching Yuan.
Eventually, another soldier suddenly asked, "What if the Void Hunter appears? Do you think he'll try to fight that, too?"
"Who knows? But I hope they do fight."
"Although we have more than ten people here, the chances of the Void Hunter appearing with our number are minuscule, so don't expect it to show up.
"It may not be likely, but it's not impossible, right? Besides, with all the commotion he's—"
The soldier abruptly stopped speaking as a chill ran down his spine.
The next moment, the atmosphere around them noticeably shifted. The temperature plummeted by several dozen degrees, and the once-scorching barren landscape suddenly became bitterly cold.
"T-This is!"
Everyone but Yuan immediately realized the reason for the sudden change.
"Th-This phenomenon! The Void Hunter... It's going to appear!"
"Shit! Shit! Shit! Do we run away?!"
"No!" Captain Heen shouted. "Not yet! Not until we see how that monster will respond to the Void Hunter!"
"What if they come after us together?!"
Meanwhile, Yuan came to a halt after sensing the sudden change in the atmosphere.
'The Void Hunter? Is it going to appear here? Now?' Yuan thought to himself after overhearing the others.
He contemplated how he should react. Should he stay and fight it? Or should he run away?
'If Tian Yuchen, who has reached the 50th floor of Endless Assault, cannot defeat this Void Hunter, there's practically zero chance I can defeat it...' he sighed inwardly.
Yet, he didn't want to run away just yet.
'Let's take a look at it before I leave...'
Since opportunities to encounter the Void Hunter were exceedingly rare, with everyone actively doing their best to avoid it, Yuan decided to remain a while longer and observe it for himself.
After a few moments of silence, he noticed a lone silhouette emerging in the distance, slowly making its way toward him while exuding an ominous and menacing aura.
Sure enough, the Void Hunter looked remarkably human. If Yuan hadn't known its identity beforehand, even he might have mistaken it for another human.
"Fuck... what a tremendous aura!" Yuan cursed aloud as cold sweat drenched his body.
The Void Hunter radiated a terrifying aura that surpassed that of every Eternal Yuan had encountered before, with the sole exception of Prime Eternals.

chapters.title: Chapter 2641 Void Hunter's Appearance
paragraphs: The moment the Void Hunter appeared, its overwhelming presence engulfed the entire area like an impossibly heavy blanket, bearing down with the weight of several mountains. The soldiers watching Yuan immediately felt as though their bodies were on the verge of being crushed beneath the immense pressure.

The Void Hunter—the ultimate and apex predator of this world. Even if every force in the world united against it, they would still have no chance of victory. That was precisely why everyone had long since chosen to avoid it rather than fight.
Yet, when faced with this unfathomable existence, Yuan did not think about fleeing. Rather, his blood boiled, and his bones itched with the intense desire to fight it!
Meanwhile, the Void Hunter showed no urgency as it slowly but steadily approached Yuan, almost as though it were certain that its prey had no chance of escaping its grasp.
With every step it took, the Void Hunter's already ridiculous aura increased further, as if there was no limit to its power.

Yuan was beginning to question whether he should really fight the Void Hunter in his current state. As much as he wanted to test himself against it, he knew that he had virtually no chance of defeating it.
Moreover, the Void Hunter's aura was gradually approaching the level of a Prime Eternal—or at least the level of power Deemo, the Demon God, had displayed during their battle.
"Are you going to run away?"
A calm voice suddenly echoed.
Yuan narrowed his eyes at the Void Hunter.
"Did it just speak?" he mumbled to himself.
"Did... Did the Void Hunter just speak?!" The soldiers watching from afar were just as shocked as Yuan—if not even more so. None of them had ever heard of the Void Hunter being capable of speech.
"What are you?" Yuan decided to try talking to the Void Hunter.
"I am... life."
"I am... death."
"I am... God!"
A voice responded.
Then, without warning, the Void Hunter's silhouette vanished into thin air.
Yuan instinctively pushed his senses to their absolute limit, but even then, he couldn't detect the Void Hunter's presence anywhere, as though it had truly disappeared from existence.
"Did it... leave?"
However, the moment those three words left Yuan's mouth, the Void Hunter suddenly reappeared directly in front of him, standing no more than a single step away.
Yuan immediately reacted, attempting to use Void Manipulation. However, before he could even activate it, a devastating punch slammed into his stomach, sending him flying into the distance.
Yuan quickly stabilized himself, coughing up a mouthful of blood afterward.
"They're really going to fight!" Captain Heen exclaimed in a gleeful manner.
But the other soldiers were focused on something else entirely.
"D-Did he just survive a punch from the Void Hunter?!"

Of course, they weren't referring to the sheer force behind the punch. Since the Void Hunter was classified as a Void Specter, it possessed the same terrifying ability as the rest of its kind—to kill anything it touched.
"This confirms it! There's no way he's human if he can survive being touched by a Void Specter!" Captain Heen said.
No human has ever survived a touch from Void Specters, especially not the Void Hunter, after all.
As annoying as Captain Heen was, the others had to agree with him on this matter.
"Unless the Void Hunter allowed him to live for some reason?" one of them suddenly muttered out loud.
"Why would it do that?"
"How would I know? It also spoke with him, and we never knew it could speak before!"

Meanwhile, Yuan unleashed his Eternal Essence to its absolute limit. After several months of relentless training, his Eternal Essence had grown tremendously, reaching an astonishing three trillion years.
Unfortunately, even that amount seemed insignificant before the Void Hunter.
The Void Hunter showed no reaction to Yuan's Eternal Essence and simply stood there in silence.

Now that Yuan could finally observe it up close, he noticed that its body was composed of the same pitch-black substance as the other Void Specters. However, unlike them, it possessed a distinctly human figure and even appeared to be wearing a cloak, its hood concealing the shape of its face.
Suddenly, the Void Hunter moved, tapping its chest with one hand while beckoning Yuan forward with the other, clearly challenging him to attack.
"Won't you look at this guy..." A cold smile tugged at Yuan's lips.
The next moment, he struck without hesitation, pouring three trillion years' worth of Eternal Essence into a single punch.
The Void Hunter remained perfectly still, making its intentions clear—that it intended to take the attack head-on.
When Yuan's fist slammed into its body, a devastating ripple erupted from the point of impact, surging beyond the horizon and causing the entire world to tremble for a full second.
The soldiers watching from afar were instantly swept away by the overwhelming force of the ripple, their bodies sent tumbling through the air like trash caught in a violent storm.
As for the Void Hunter, despite taking Yuan's punch directly, it wasn't sent flying. In fact, it didn't move even a single inch, as though its entire body were firmly rooted to the ground.
Yuan wasn't too surprised that his attack had no effect on the Void Hunter. If anything, he had expected such an outcome from the start.
Even so, seeing his attack accomplish absolutely nothing still left a bitter taste in his mouth, especially considering how much he'd trained.
'How much more do I have to train to even harm this guy?' he sighed inwardly.
The Void Hunter suddenly spoke, "You are not worthy."
Before Yuan could respond, another punch slammed into his stomach.
However, unlike before, Yuan wasn't sent flying. His feet remained firmly planted on the ground as the force of the blow pushed him back only several meters.
"Is it just me, or did you get weaker?" Yuan mocked it after spitting out a mouthful of blood.
The Void Hunter did not react to his provocation.
"You are not worthy," it repeated a moment later.
Then, its aura surged even higher.

"This bastard can still get stronger?!" Yuan gritted his teeth as the pressure bearing down on him became increasingly unbearable. At this point, the Void Hunter's presence had already surpassed the power Deemo displayed during their battle in the past—the same power that defeated Tian Chenyu.
Yuan prepared for the worst when the Void Hunter started moving again.
However, Yuan was left dumbfounded when the Void Hunter simply walked past him, completely ignoring his presence.
"Where are you going?!" Yuan called out, feeling strangely offended by the dismissal.
But the Void Hunter offered no response. Instead, it suddenly shot into the distance at the speed of light.
"That direction... Don't tell me it's going after—!"
Yuan's expression changed the moment he realized where the Void Hunter was headed, and he quickly chased after it.
Meanwhile, not too far away, the soldiers who had been blown away by the earlier shockwave had already decided to retreat.
"Let's get out of here before the Void Hunter comes after us!"
"What about that humanoid Void Specter?!" Captain Heen shouted. "I need to confirm whether it's dead!"

"If you want to stay behind and wait for the Void Hunter to kill you, then be our guest!" one of his own squad members shouted. "We've already confirmed the existence of the humanoid Void Specter. For now, we will return to the city and report everything we've learned so far!"
But before they could get far, an unfathomable presence suddenly descended upon them, pressing down on their bodies like a colossal mountain.
Unable to withstand the immense pressure, they plummeted from the sky and crashed heavily into the ground.
"T-This pressure! Don't tell me the Void Hunter already defeated that humanoid Void Specter and is coming after us now!"
"It's not coming after us! It's already here!"
Sure enough, the Void Hunter appeared before them like a ghost, its existence seemingly materializing out of thin air.
The soldiers wanted to run, but the Void Hunter's presence was so powerful that it distorted the very space around them, making Void Control impossible for them.
Then, with calm and unhurried movements, the Void Hunter approached one of the soldiers and lightly tapped him on the forehead.
The next instant, the soldier's entire body disintegrated into nothingness.
Yuan arrived just in time to witness the scene, and his eyes narrowed when he saw the soldier disintegrate, as it was eerily similar to how his own affinity had killed a soldier before.
However, Yuan had no time to dwell on it, as the Void Hunter was already moving toward its next target.
"Stop!"
He charged at the Void Hunter and attacked with all his might, desperately trying to draw its attention away from the soldiers.
Yet, the Void Hunter completely ignored him and killed a second soldier.
Then a third... a fourth...
One after another, the soldiers vanished until only one remained.
"N-No! I don't want to die!" Captain Heen cried out, tears and snot streaming down his face as terror overwhelmed him.
"Please... save me..."
Captain Heen stared desperately at Yuan as the Void Hunter's finger slowly approached his forehead, resembling death's scythe descending to claim his life.
But alas, there was nothing Yuan could do but watch as the Void Hunter claimed Captain Heen's life.
After killing every last soldier, the Void Hunter finally turned to face Yuan.
"You are not worthy."
Yuan clenched his fists in irritation. The way it kept repeating those words reminded him of the entity he had encountered on the 46th floor of Endless Assault.
"What the hell do you want from me?" Yuan asked a moment later when it seemed to have no intention of fighting him anymore.
