"I am... death."
"I am...
God!"
A voice responded.
Then, without warning, the Void Hunter's silhouette vanished into thin air.
Yuan instinctively pushed his senses to their absolute limit, but even then, he couldn't detect the Void Hunter's presence anywhere, as though it had truly disappeared from existence.
"Did it... leave?"
However, the moment those three words left Yuan's mouth, the Void Hunter suddenly reappeared directly in front of him, standing no more than a single step away.
Yuan immediately reacted, attempting to use Void Manipulation.
However, before he could even activate it, a devastating punch slammed into his stomach, sending him flying into the distance.
Yuan quickly stabilized himself, coughing up a mouthful of blood afterward.
"They're really going to fight!" Captain Heen exclaimed in a gleeful manner.
But the other soldiers were focused on something else entirely.
"D-Did he just survive a punch from the Void Hunter?!"
Of course, they weren't referring to the sheer force behind the punch.
Since the Void Hunter was classified as a Void Specter, it possessed the same terrifying ability as the rest of its kind—to kill anything it touched.
"This confirms it!
There's no way he's human if he can survive being touched by a Void Specter!" Captain Heen said.
No human has ever survived a touch from Void Specters, especially not the Void Hunter, after all.
As annoying as Captain Heen was, the others had to agree with him on this matter.
"Unless the Void Hunter allowed him to live for some reason?" one of them suddenly muttered out loud.
"Why would it do that?"
"How would I know?
It also spoke with him, and we never knew it could speak before!"
Meanwhile, Yuan unleashed his Eternal Essence to its absolute limit.
After several months of relentless training, his Eternal Essence had grown tremendously, reaching an astonishing three trillion years.
Unfortunately, even that amount seemed insignificant before the Void Hunter.
The Void Hunter showed no reaction to Yuan's Eternal Essence and simply stood there in silence.
Now that Yuan could finally observe it up close, he noticed that its body was composed of the same pitch-black substance as the other Void Specters.
However, unlike them, it possessed a distinctly human figure and even appeared to be wearing a cloak, its hood concealing the shape of its face.
Suddenly, the Void Hunter moved, tapping its chest with one hand while beckoning Yuan forward with the other, clearly challenging him to attack.
"Won't you look at this guy..." A cold smile tugged at Yuan's lips.
The next moment, he struck without hesitation, pouring three trillion years' worth of Eternal Essence into a single punch.
The Void Hunter remained perfectly still, making its intentions clear—that it intended to take the attack head-on.
When Yuan's fist slammed into its body, a devastating ripple erupted from the point of impact, surging beyond the horizon and causing the entire world to tremble for a full second.
The soldiers watching from afar were instantly swept away by the overwhelming force of the ripple, their bodies sent tumbling through the air like trash caught in a violent storm.
As for the Void Hunter, despite taking Yuan's punch directly, it wasn't sent flying.
In fact, it didn't move even a single inch, as though its entire body were firmly rooted to the ground.
Yuan wasn't too surprised that his attack had no effect on the Void Hunter.
If anything, he had expected such an outcome from the start.
Even so, seeing his attack accomplish absolutely nothing still left a bitter taste in his mouth, especially considering how much he'd trained.
'How much more do I have to train to even harm this guy?' he sighed inwardly.
The Void Hunter suddenly spoke, "You are not worthy."
Before Yuan could respond, another punch slammed into his stomach.
However, unlike before, Yuan wasn't sent flying.
His feet remained firmly planted on the ground as the force of the blow pushed him back only several meters.
"Is it just me, or did you get weaker?" Yuan mocked it after spitting out a mouthful of blood.
The Void Hunter did not react to his provocation.
"You are not worthy," it repeated a moment later.
Then, its aura surged even higher.
"This bastard can still get stronger?!" Yuan gritted his teeth as the pressure bearing down on him became increasingly unbearable.
At this point, the Void Hunter's presence had already surpassed the power Deemo displayed during their battle in the past—the same power that defeated Tian Chenyu.
Yuan prepared for the worst when the Void Hunter started moving again.
However, Yuan was left dumbfounded when the Void Hunter simply walked past him, completely ignoring his presence.
"Where are you going?!" Yuan called out, feeling strangely offended by the dismissal.
But the Void Hunter offered no response.
Instead, it suddenly shot into the distance at the speed of light.
"That direction...
Don't tell me it's going after—!"
Yuan's expression changed the moment he realized where the Void Hunter was headed, and he quickly chased after it.
Meanwhile, not too far away, the soldiers who had been blown away by the earlier shockwave had already decided to retreat.
"Let's get out of here before the Void Hunter comes after us!"
"What about that humanoid Void Specter?!" Captain Heen shouted.
"I need to confirm whether it's dead!"
"If you want to stay behind and wait for the Void Hunter to kill you, then be our guest!" one of his own squad members shouted.
"We've already confirmed the existence of the humanoid Void Specter.
For now, we will return to the city and report everything we've learned so far!"
But before they could get far, an unfathomable presence suddenly descended upon them, pressing down on their bodies like a colossal mountain.
Unable to withstand the immense pressure, they plummeted from the sky and crashed heavily into the ground.
"T-This pressure!
Don't tell me the Void Hunter already defeated that humanoid Void Specter and is coming after us now!"
"It's not coming after us!
It's already here!"
Sure enough, the Void Hunter appeared before them like a ghost, its existence seemingly materializing out of thin air.
The soldiers wanted to run, but the Void Hunter's presence was so powerful that it distorted the very space around them, making Void Control impossible for them.
Then, with calm and unhurried movements, the Void Hunter approached one of the soldiers and lightly tapped him on the forehead.
The next instant, the soldier's entire body disintegrated into nothingness.
Yuan arrived just in time to witness the scene, and his eyes narrowed when he saw the soldier disintegrate, as it was eerily similar to how his own affinity had killed a soldier before.
However, Yuan had no time to dwell on it, as the Void Hunter was already moving toward its next target.
"Stop!"
He charged at the Void Hunter and attacked with all his might, desperately trying to draw its attention away from the soldiers.
Yet, the Void Hunter completely ignored him and killed a second soldier.
Then a third... a fourth...
One after another, the soldiers vanished until only one remained.
"N-No!
I don't want to die!" Captain Heen cried out, tears and snot streaming down his face as terror overwhelmed him.
"Please... save me..."
Captain Heen stared desperately at Yuan as the Void Hunter's finger slowly approached his forehead, resembling death's scythe descending to claim his life.
But alas, there was nothing Yuan could do but watch as the Void Hunter claimed Captain Heen's life.
After killing every last soldier, the Void Hunter finally turned to face Yuan.
"You are not worthy."
Yuan clenched his fists in irritation.
The way it kept repeating those words reminded him of the entity he had encountered on the 46th floor of Endless Assault.
"What the hell do you want from me?" Yuan asked a moment later when it seemed to have no intention of fighting him anymore.

chapters.title: Chapter 2642 Fighting the Void Hunter
paragraphs: "Prove... your worth!"
The Void Hunter responded to Yuan's question before suddenly attacking again.
Yuan gritted his teeth and fought back.
"Fuck! You already claimed that I wasn't worthy! How the hell am I supposed to prove myself?!"
Yuan cursed aloud as he fought with everything he could muster, even relying on his affinity—something he had been using from the very beginning.
However, for some reason, his affinity simply didn't work on the Void Hunter.

'Whenever I attack with ordinary Eternal Essence, I can at least feel the impact. But whenever I use my affinity, it's different... It's like the attack never connects at all, as though the power simply vanishes the instant it makes contact. What the hell is going on? Is the Void Hunter immune to my affinity?' Yuan pondered inwardly as he continued his futile struggle against the Void Hunter.
The way the Void Hunter nullified his affinity felt strangely familiar to Yuan, who had achieved true immunity to several elements himself.

'Since an element can also manifest as an affinity—like Shiva's cold affinity—it would make sense for someone with a fire-based affinity to possess a natural resistance against hers,' Yuan continued to ponder.

With an unknown number of affinities existing in the world, it wasn't unreasonable for some to naturally counter or even fully nullify others, and Yuan began to suspect this was exactly what was happening.
Unfortunately, since he still didn't know the true nature of his own affinity, that only made the situation more difficult to understand.
After all, if he couldn't even identify the nature of his own affinity, what hope did he have of figuring out his opponent's?
'There's also a chance that...'
Yuan swallowed nervously after realizing another possibility.
'What if it has the same affinity as me?'
After all, the way it vaporized the soldiers earlier was similar—identical to when he used his affinity on the Ember City soldiers.
Time passed quickly, and Yuan's battle with the Void Hunter continued for several days. Although Yuan was nowhere close to defeating it, one thing had become increasingly obvious.

The Void Hunter had no intention of killing him. Instead, it seemed content to continue playing with him, like a child messing with ants because they knew there was nothing the ants could do against them.

Their battle was so intense that every Void Specter in the vicinity had been annihilated by the ripples produced whenever their Eternal Essence clashed. The tremendous energy radiating from their fight had also long since alerted every city in the world to their presence.
"T-This energy! There's no mistaking it! The Void Hunter has appeared!"
"Fucking damn it! Which fools summoned that monster?! Every time the Void Hunter appears, there's a chance it could wipe out all of humanity!"
The emergence of the Void Hunter immediately sent every city in the world into a state of panic.
Yet not a single city dared to send soldiers to investigate, fearing that doing so might draw the Void Hunter toward them.
As a result, all they could do was remain hidden within their safe zones and pray that the monster would disappear as soon as possible.
"Wait... who the hell is fighting the Void Hunter? For the hunter to be releasing this much energy, its opponent must be incredibly powerful!"
As the battle continued to drag on and the Void Hunter's energy showed no signs of diminishing, people across the cities quickly realized that whoever was fighting it was far from ordinary.
Unfortunately, none of these people had any information or record of this second energy, so they could only guess.
However, among the nine cities, there was one that had a fairly good idea of what—or rather, who—might have caused the Void Hunter to appear.
Of course, that would be Ember City, which had sent out nearly ten soldiers to investigate a newly discovered humanoid Void Specter.

Although the Void Hunter wouldn't appear unless a group exceeded ten people, they suspected that their soldiers might have encountered another squad during the investigation and inadvertently crossed that threshold.
After all, similar incidents had happened more than once before.
With that said, the higher-ups at Ember City couldn't fathom how they were lasting so long against the Void Hunter.
"What are the chances that the humanoid Void Specter is the one fighting the Void Hunter?"
"Extremely low... but if the alternative is that our soldiers are the ones fighting it, then it's practically guaranteed."
"A Void Specter fighting the Void Hunter? That doesn't make any sense at all."
"The existence of a humanoid Void Specter already makes no sense."
"If it really is the humanoid Void Specter... wouldn't it be a catastrophe to have two monsters of such level exist at once? We still don't know anything about it, either."
Nobody responded, afraid of the implications.
Time continued to pass, though for everyone except Yuan, each day seemed to crawl by painfully slowly.

As the battle dragged on, the energy radiating from Yuan's clashes with the Void Hunter continued to grow. This was because Yuan constantly absorbed the Eternal Essence left behind by the Void Specters that were inadvertently annihilated by the shockwaves of their battle.

But alas, no matter how much Yuan's Eternal Essence continued to grow, the Void Hunter only grew stronger alongside him, gradually revealing more and more of its seemingly bottomless reserves of power.
'Damn it... are we seriously going to keep this up until I'm finally "worthy"?' Yuan sighed inwardly as he coughed up another mouthful of blood.
By now, his entire body was drenched in crimson, and he had lost so much blood over the course of the battle that it could have filled a large pond.

Despite his seemingly hopeless situation, Yuan refused to give up. He was prepared to fight the Void Hunter for as long as necessary—whether that meant eventually defeating it or earning its recognition, whichever came first.
Yet, after nearly an entire month of nonstop fighting, the Void Hunter suddenly came to a halt.
"You are not worthy..."
Its voice seemed to carry a faint trace of disappointment, though Yuan couldn't tell whether that was real or merely his imagination.
Then, without explanation, the Void Hunter turned around and started walking away.
"Come back, you—"
Yuan shouted at it, but it completely ignored him and vanished without a trace like a ghost a split second later.
"Son of a bitch... When was the last time I was toyed around like this?" Yuan gritted his teeth in frustration.
He continued to linger in the area even long after the Void Hunter was gone.
"Forget it. I'll fight it again once I train some more."
He turned around and began traveling in the direction of Gaia's Heaven, deciding that it was finally time to return to the city.

Although he could have remained in the Black Zone and continued training, he felt that his progress was too slow after facing the Void Hunter. At this point, it would be more efficient to return to the city and find a way to gain access to a level two Black Zone.
Of course, Yuan would have gone there immediately if he could. Unfortunately, he had no idea where one was located.
Once the nine cities were certain that the battle had ended, each dispatched only a single soldier to investigate.
They knew the other cities would likely do the same, and sending more than one person each would risk pushing the total number of investigators past ten and summoning the Void Hunter again.
On his way back to Gaia's Heaven, Yuan suddenly sensed a familiar presence approaching from the opposite direction.
'This presence... the Ironwoman?'
Sure enough, it was indeed the Ironwoman. However, rather than stopping to speak with her, Yuan concealed his presence and quietly allowed her to pass by without noticing him.
'The direction she's heading... she must be going to investigate my battle with the Void Hunter...'
Yuan easily guessed the purpose of her mission, which was precisely why he had chosen to avoid encountering her.
By the time Yuan returned to the city, the Ironwoman had just arrived at the scene, where some soldiers from the other cities had already gathered.
"W-What the hell happened here...?" the Ironwoman muttered, a dazed expression hidden beneath her mask as she surveyed the aftermath of the battle.
Thousands of massive craters stretched as far as the eye could see, some so deep that they resembled bottomless pits leading straight into hell.
The land in this world possessed a unique regenerative property, gradually repairing any damage until the terrain returned to its original state.
However, the destruction caused by this battle was so severe that even weeks after it had ended, the landscape remained utterly devastated.
Once the Ironwoman snapped out of her daze, she was startled by the powerful energies still lingering throughout the battlefield.
Although she had never fought the Void Hunter herself, she had experienced its presence firsthand before and immediately recognized its energy.
However, what truly shocked her was the second energy lingering alongside it, as she also found it familiar.
'This energy...'
The face of a certain arrogant and handsome man suddenly appeared in her mind.
'No, it can't be him...'
She quickly dismissed the thought, finding it far too ridiculous to even entertain.
"I figured they would've sent you out here, Ironwoman."
One of the soldiers there suddenly approached her and remarked.
The Ironwoman turned to face this soldier, who wore an azure-colored uniform, and responded, "I am the most capable, after all."
"Then you must have some information about what happened here... or more specifically, who was fighting the Void Hunter." The soldier said, staring at her with slightly narrowed eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 2643 Returning to Military Base
paragraphs: "What makes you think I have such information? I literally just got here, you know?"
"I was just hoping you were capable enough to know something before coming here, that's all."
"Sorry to disappoint you, but I am not capable enough to know everything."
The soldier in the azure-colored suit shrugged, "What a pity."
The two of them grouped up with the other soldiers shortly after.
"Have you guys learned anything so far?" asked the Ironwoman.
"Not really," one of them responded, a soldier wearing a green uniform.
He then retrieved a glass vial that contained what appeared to be a chunk of dried blood and continued, "Besides the craters, this blood was left behind. And there are a lot of them."
"A little too much," said another soldier. "It's like thousands of people have been slaughtered here."

"Blood?" The Ironwoman muttered in a puzzled tone before inquiring, "How could there be blood if the Void Hunter leaves no traces of its victims behind? A single touch from that entity will turn one into dust before they could even bleed a single drop of blood."

"True, so the blood must've been the result of a fight between whoever was present when the Void Hunter was summoned. I am guessing that a large group of soldiers fought here for some reason and ended up dying to the Void Hunter."
"But that doesn't explain why the Void Hunter had fought for so long before disappearing," said another soldier.
"And we would know about it if such a large-scale battle had really occurred."
"Because the Void Hunter wasn't fighting a human," a new voice suddenly resounded.
The Ironwoman and the others turned their heads to see a soldier in crimson uniform approaching them.
"What do you know?" the Ironwoman asked him.

The soldier from Ember City sighed and said, "We were going to withhold this information until we had more, but considering the situation and implications, we have decided to share it, so listen carefully."
"Not long ago, we discovered a new kind of Void Specter—one that has the ability to perfectly disguise itself as a human, and we believe it was the Void Hunter's opponent."
"What?!"
Nearly everyone there exclaimed in shock at this revelation.
"A Void Specter that can disguise itself as a human...?" the Ironwoman mumbled.

"A few of our soldiers discovered this Void Specter during their mission. They mistook him for a human lost in the Black Zone at first and approached him to help, but it became clear that the entity was not human when it killed two of them without warning."
"That doesn't really mean anything..." said the soldier in the azure-colored uniform.
"Let me continue," said the Ember City soldier.
"After learning of its existence, we sent out a group of powerful soldiers to investigate. Nine soldiers in total."
"Almost enough to summon the Void Hunter, huh?"
"Yes, and their life signals disconnected shortly after the Void Hunter's appearance."
"Even if those nine soldiers died here, that doesn't explain the amount of blood present here."

"The blood is likely from the humanoid Void Specter. If it has the ability to disguise itself as a human, we can assume it bleeds like one, too. And since it's not a real human, it doesn't know that humans don't have an unlimited supply of blood."
"That's a whole lot of assumptions..." the Ironwoman remarked. "Nothing you've said can really be taken seriously without evidence."
The Ember City soldier turned to look at her and said, "Then you'll likely not believe me when I say that this humanoid Void Specter has taken the appearance of a soldier from your city."
"What?"
The Ironwoman frowned behind her mask.
"You heard me. The humanoid Void Specter was wearing Gaia's Heaven's uniform, and according to the survivors, he was also a corporal."
A look of bewilderment appeared on the Ironwoman's face after hearing this information.
"A corporal... from my city?" she muttered in a dazed voice as a certain face surfaced in her mind.
If the soldiers from Ember City had truly encountered a corporal wandering alone in the Black Zone, then there was only one person who fit that description—Corporal Yuan.
'Are they mistaking Corporal Yuan for a Void Specter...?' she wondered inwardly.
Even with that possibility in mind, the Ironwoman decided not to say anything until she had more information. After all, there was still a chance that the mysterious corporal wasn't Yuan at all.
"Well, that's all the information I have on the humanoid Void Specter for now, so do with it what you will," said the soldier from Ember City.
Shortly afterward, the soldiers resumed their investigation, collecting blood samples from various locations throughout the devastated area.
Meanwhile, Yuan arrived at the military gates.
When Yuan approached the gates, the soldier on duty stared at him with wide eyes, as if he were before a ghost.
"C-Corporal Yuan...?" the soldier, who recognized him, muttered in a dazed voice.
"Yeah?" Yuan casually responded, acting as if he hadn't been presumed dead for more than half a year.
The soldier rubbed his eyes and looked at Yuan again.
"I-I thought you were dead!"
"Well, as you can see, I am well and alive."
"How is that possible?! The Scorpion Squad said you entered the Black Zone and died there!"
"I was in the Black Zone, but I didn't die. I was lost, hence why it took me so long to return," Yuan said, giving a convenient excuse.
"Anyway, let me in. I have to speak with General Mei."
"R-Right away!"
The soldier immediately opened the gates.

After entering the military base, Yuan made his way toward General Mei's office, deliberately taking his time as he walked through the open areas, almost as though he wanted as many people as possible to notice his return.
"Hey... am I seeing things, or is that Corporal Yuan?"
"Huh? What are you—Holy shit! It's Corporal Yuan! He's alive?!"
"What's going on?! I thought he died a few months ago!"
The soldiers exclaimed in disbelief when they saw Yuan casually walking through the base, staring at him as though they had just seen a ghost.

The soldier from Ember City sighed and said, "We were going to withhold this information until we had more, but considering the situation and implications, we have decided to share it, so listen carefully."
"Not long ago, we discovered a new kind of Void Specter—one that has the ability to perfectly disguise itself as a human, and we believe it was the Void Hunter's opponent."
"What?!"
Nearly everyone there exclaimed in shock at this revelation.
"A Void Specter that can disguise itself as a human...?" the Ironwoman mumbled.
"A few of our soldiers discovered this Void Specter during their mission.
They mistook him for a human lost in the Black Zone at first and approached him to help, but it became clear that the entity was not human when it killed two of them without warning."
"That doesn't really mean anything..." said the soldier in the azure-colored uniform.
"Let me continue," said the Ember City soldier.
"After learning of its existence, we sent out a group of powerful soldiers to investigate.
Nine soldiers in total."
"Almost enough to summon the Void Hunter, huh?"
"Yes, and their life signals disconnected shortly after the Void Hunter's appearance."
"Even if those nine soldiers died here, that doesn't explain the amount of blood present here."
"The blood is likely from the humanoid Void Specter.
If it has the ability to disguise itself as a human, we can assume it bleeds like one, too.
And since it's not a real human, it doesn't know that humans don't have an unlimited supply of blood."
"That's a whole lot of assumptions..." the Ironwoman remarked.
"Nothing you've said can really be taken seriously without evidence."
The Ember City soldier turned to look at her and said, "Then you'll likely not believe me when I say that this humanoid Void Specter has taken the appearance of a soldier from your city."
"What?"
The Ironwoman frowned behind her mask.
"You heard me.
The humanoid Void Specter was wearing Gaia's Heaven's uniform, and according to the survivors, he was also a corporal."
A look of bewilderment appeared on the Ironwoman's face after hearing this information.
"A corporal... from my city?" she muttered in a dazed voice as a certain face surfaced in her mind.
If the soldiers from Ember City had truly encountered a corporal wandering alone in the Black Zone, then there was only one person who fit that description—Corporal Yuan.
'Are they mistaking Corporal Yuan for a Void Specter...?' she wondered inwardly.
Even with that possibility in mind, the Ironwoman decided not to say anything until she had more information.
After all, there was still a chance that the mysterious corporal wasn't Yuan at all.
"Well, that's all the information I have on the humanoid Void Specter for now, so do with it what you will," said the soldier from Ember City.
Shortly afterward, the soldiers resumed their investigation, collecting blood samples from various locations throughout the devastated area.
Meanwhile, Yuan arrived at the military gates.
When Yuan approached the gates, the soldier on duty stared at him with wide eyes, as if he were before a ghost.
"C-Corporal Yuan...?" the soldier, who recognized him, muttered in a dazed voice.
"Yeah?" Yuan casually responded, acting as if he hadn't been presumed dead for more than half a year.
The soldier rubbed his eyes and looked at Yuan again.
"I-I thought you were dead!"
"Well, as you can see, I am well and alive."
"How is that possible?!
The Scorpion Squad said you entered the Black Zone and died there!"
"I was in the Black Zone, but I didn't die.
I was lost, hence why it took me so long to return," Yuan said, giving a convenient excuse.
"Anyway, let me in.
I have to speak with General Mei."
"R-Right away!"
The soldier immediately opened the gates.

After entering the military base, Yuan made his way toward General Mei's office, deliberately taking his time as he walked through the open areas, almost as though he wanted as many people as possible to notice his return.
"Hey... am I seeing things, or is that Corporal Yuan?"
"Huh?
What are you—Holy shit!
It's Corporal Yuan!
He's alive?!"
"What's going on?!
I thought he died a few months ago!"
The soldiers exclaimed in disbelief when they saw Yuan casually walking through the base, staring at him as though they had just seen a ghost.

chapters.title: Chapter 2644 Yuan's Testimony
paragraphs: "C-Corporal Yuan?! Is that really you?!"
While most were frozen in a daze, one soldier suddenly called out to Yuan.
Yuan turned to that soldier and responded without stopping, "Yes, it's me."
"How are you still alive?! I heard you entered the Black Zone alone!"
"I don't want to explain the entire thing every time someone asks, so I'll let the higher-ups explain it later," he said.
"A-Alright..."
News of Yuan's return spread like wildfire in the military, reaching General Gu's ears even before Yuan made it to General Mei's office.
"WHAT DID YOU JUST SAY?!" General Gu stood from his chair after hearing the news and screamed at the top of his lungs.
"C-Corporal Yuan is still alive, and he'd just returned to base!"
"That's impossible! The Scorpion Squad has confirmed his death in the Black Zone!"
"The Scorpion Squad must have lied."
"Where the hell are they?! Demand answers from them!"
"Yes, General."
Meanwhile, inside General Mei's office, she also received news of Yuan's return.
"General! You won't believe this, but Corporal Yuan—the one everyone thought had died a few months ago—has returned to the city alive!"
"Really? When did he return?" Mei Feng asked in a surprised tone, though her reaction was far more subdued than the officer had expected.
"About fifteen minutes ago, and from what I heard, he seems to be approaching the direction of your—"
*Knock* *Knock*
The door was suddenly knocked on, followed by a familiar voice.
"It's me."
"Speaking of the devil..." Mei Feng muttered. "I'll speak to you later."
After disconnecting the call, Mei Feng answered Yuan, "Enter."
The door opened, and Yuan calmly stepped into the office a moment later.

Mei Feng drew a sharp breath upon seeing his face. Although she already knew he was alive, there had always been a chance that something could happen to him while he continued training alone in the Black Zone. Now that he was standing before her in person, whatever lingering unease she still harbored vanished like smoke.
"I'm back," Yuan spoke first, acting as if he'd only just gone out for a short adventure.
Mei Feng's chest rose and fell heavily, as though she were preparing to unleash a torrent of anger. However, after taking another deep breath, she let out a long sigh instead.
"Is that all you have to say?" she asked.
"Sorry for making you worried," Yuan immediately added.
Mei Feng rubbed her eyes for a moment before speaking again, "Did you really spend the entire time in the Black Zone?"
"Yes."
"Well? What do you think of the Black Zone?"
"It wasn't as dangerous as I thought," he replied without hesitation.
"What exactly are you trying to achieve?" she then questioned.
"I already told you. I am training."
Mei Feng frowned at his response and quickly replied, "If you're going to lie, at least make it believable. Your cultivation hasn't improved in the slightest since I last saw you."
"I never said I was training my cultivation," Yuan said while shaking his head. "I am training another power."
"What—"
"Don't bother asking. It's not something you can comprehend, and it's a power that only I can wield," Yuan quickly interrupted.
"A little conceited, don't you think?"
"No, not at all."
"Is it related to your physique?"
"You can say that."
"Then was it fruitful? Your training."
"It went smoothly, but it's not progressing as fast as I want. Therefore, I intend to visit level 2 Black Zone next."
"Level 2 Black Zone...? Did the Ironwoman teach you that?"
He nodded.
"What are the requirements to go there?" he then asked.
"Ask me that once you qualify for the Black Zone—officially."
"I'll do that after this."
After a moment of silence, Yuan asked, "What happened to the Scorpion Squad?

"I was wondering when you'd ask," Mei Feng replied. "Since we didn't have enough evidence to charge them with murder or conspiracy, the most we could do was hold them responsible for negligence. In other words, they essentially got away with it."
She paused briefly before continuing, "However, now that you're back, things are different. You can testify against them yourself."
"That sounds fun, but I have a feeling that General Gu might get rid of them before we can serve real justice."
"That would save us a lot of time and trouble," Mei Feng sneered.
"...Not that I am saying it should happen," she added after a brief pause.
Yuan chuckled. "So, when and where do I give my testimony?"
"We'll do it right now," Mei Feng replied. "There's a chance General Gu might try something if we wait too long, so I want to get this over with as soon as possible."
"Alright."
Mei Feng immediately contacted several officers and informed them of the situation.
Then, she brought Yuan to another location, where they waited for about half an hour before a group of officers finally arrived.
"Wow... he's really alive..."
Even though they already knew Yuan was alive, it was still surprising to see him in person.
Of course, General Gu was among these officers.
'Those useless fucks!' General Gu gritted his teeth and cursed the Scorpion Squad inwardly after confirming that Yuan was alive with his own eyes.
Although Mei Feng would have preferred to keep General Gu out of the proceedings for obvious reasons, this was an official testimony, and as a general, he had every right to be present.
In fact, the number of officers present for Yuan's testimony was more than four times the number that had attended the Scorpion Squad's interrogation a few months earlier.
"I can't wait to find out how he survived alone out there for so long."

While many were curious about what had truly happened between Yuan and the Scorpion Squad, they were even more curious about how a corporal who had only recently joined the military had managed to survive alone in the Black Zone for several months.
"Are you ready to begin?"
Some time later, the interviewer asked Yuan.
"I am."
"Then we will begin."
After starting a voice recorder, the interviewer spoke again, "Please state your identity for us."

chapters.title: Chapter 2645 Yuan's Testimony(2)
paragraphs: "Please state your identity for us."
"Yuan. Corporal Yuan."
"We'll start from the very beginning of your encounter with the Scorpion Squad. Tell us when you first encountered them and how it happened."
"I was waiting to accept a mission in the mission hall when they approached me. That was also the first time I've met them."
"What did you talk about?"
"They said they had an offer for me that I wouldn't be able to refuse and wished to speak with me in private."
"Then what happened?"

"I went with them, and that's when they said they wanted to verify the rumors of me being able to clear tunnels and defeat Void Guardians by myself, asking me if I wanted to go on a gathering mission with them."
"Did they specify which danger zone they planned on going?"
"They did say that we'd be doing the mission in the Purple Zone."
"And you agreed to it?"
"I did."
The interviewer paused for a bit before asking, "Why did you agree to going to a place you don't qualify to enter? Aren't you aware of the risks?"

A smile tugged at Yuan's lips, and he glared at the interviewer in the eyes as he responded, "I don't qualify? Says who? Just because I didn't have time to take some test doesn't mean I am not qualified."

"Also, the Scorpion Squad said I don't need any permits to enter the Purple Zone if there were at least three captains with me. I was curious about the Purple Zone, so I went. It's as simple as that."
The interviewer was stunned by Yuan's arrogance, but he quickly snapped out of his daze and asked, "Did you have any worries at that time?"
"No, I did not."
"So what happened after you agreed to go on a mission with the Scorpion Squad?
"We left the city immediately."
"How did you leave?"
"Through the front entrance."
"Did you have any interactions with the guards on duty on that day?"

"None at all. They let us leave without even speaking to us, which I found weird at the time but didn't think much of since I thought officers were treated differently. After that, we left the city and went straight to the Purple Zone."
Everything Yuan said so far wasn't new; it only confirmed what everyone already knew.
"Tell us what happened outside the city."
"Nothing eventful happened until we reached the Purple Zone, where the Scorpion Squad brought me to a tunnel they had discovered beforehand. We went inside, and I cleared the tunnel by myself."
"Y-You cleared a tunnel in the Purple Zone by yourself...?" The interviewer's eyes widened at Yuan's seemingly outrageous claim.
"Is it really that surprising? I survived alone in the Black Zone for several months, you know?" Yuan remarked.

"Anyway, nothing particularly noteworthy happened while I was clearing the tunnel. It was only at the end—when I defeated the Void Guardian—that things started to get interesting, as that was when the Scorpion Squad admitted that their true reason for bringing me outside the city was to kill me."
The interviewer narrowed his eyes and inquired, "Did they admit that to you of their own accord? Why would they expose themselves?"
"Because I revealed to them that I already know their intentions."
"That doesn't make sense. How would you know in the first place? We can assume that you followed them because you had no reason to suspect them."
"Well, it's not the first time my life has been targeted by the person behind them. And what can I say? Their killing intent was too obvious."
"Who is this person you speak of?
Yuan smiled and said, "Do I really need to spell it out for you? However, since I don't have evidence, I won't say anything more on this matter."
"Then do you have any evidence that the Scorpion Squad admitted they intended to kill you?"
"No, I don't," Yuan replied calmly.

Even before returning to the city, Yuan had already considered the possibility that his testimony might actually end up helping the Scorpion Squad rather than condemning them. After all, the opposing side could simply demand proof.
They had never possessed any evidence that the Scorpion Squad had killed him, and now that Yuan had returned alive, proving that they had intended to kill him would be even more difficult.
Meanwhile, the officers on Mei Feng's side turned to look at her with worried expressions. None of them said anything, but the implications were obvious.
If things continued this way, not just the Scorpion Squad, but even General Gu could get away scot-free from this incident.
Mei Feng didn't say anything and continued to watch in silence. As for General Gu, he had a hand over his mouth, hiding the wide smile behind it.
"You can continue with your testimony," said the interviewer.
"Is this really a testimony? It feels more like an interrogation," Yuan remarked with a cold smile.
"You—"
"Not that I care." Yuan interrupted the interviewer and continued speaking, "Anyway, after I confronted them and they revealed their intentions, I decided to run away."

"Fortunately for me, my Void Control was superior, allowing me to barely escape them. However, I knew that I wouldn't have enough energy to completely get away and return to the city safely, so I took a gamble and entered the Black Zone, hoping they wouldn't chase after me."

"And sure enough, they gave up chasing me shortly after I entered the Black Zone. But alas, I was not familiar with the Black Zone and quickly became lost after trying to avoid getting killed by the Void Specters there."

"It was quite terrifying at first, but I eventually stopped running away and fought them, and to my surprise, they were easier to deal with than I expected, so I spent the next several months trying to find my way home and defeating every Void Specter in my path."
Yuan's story left pretty much everyone present speechless.

chapters.title: Chapter 2646 Yuan's Testimony(3)
paragraphs: The room remained silent long after Yuan finished recounting his side of the story. The interrogator stared at him with wide eyes, disbelief clear across his face.
"Since this is a testimony and not an interrogation, I should be done here, right?" Yuan spoke after a moment of silence.
"O-Of course..." The interviewer nodded in a dazed manner.

Yuan left the room shortly after, but before he could go anywhere, Mei Feng came out of the spectators' room and asked him, "What are you going to do now? Don't tell me you're going to the mission hall."
Yuan smiled and said, "How did you know?"
"You can't be seriously thinking about going on another mission right after everything that has happened!" one of the officers behind Mei Feng exclaimed in disbelief.
"Hm? Who said anything about accepting a mission?" Yuan replied before elaborating, "I am going to take the exam for the Black Zone—or the Purple Zone if I have to get the permit for that first."
"Nobody would blame you for taking a rest, you know?"
"I know, but I am not the type who likes to sit around doing nothing all day."
Mei Feng sighed and said, "Do as you please."
"Thanks."
"Before you go..."
Just as Yuan started turning around, Mei Feng retrieved something from her pocket and tossed it to him.
"This is... a storage cube?" Yuan muttered after catching the item.
"The Ironwoman asked me to give it to you wh—if you ever returned," Mei Feng said, almost revealing that she already knew Yuan was alive before his return.
Yuan didn't say anything, merely offering a silent nod before leaving with the storage cube.
After leaving, Yuan made his way to the mission hall to see when the next exam was.
Unsurprisingly, his presence attracted the attention of everyone in the mission hall.
"H-Hey... am I seeing things, or is that Corporal Yuan?"
"You haven't heard yet? Apparently he managed to make it back alive."
"No, I haven't! When did he return?"
"Literally today."
"That's crazy... To survive outside the city for months alone? He's really a different breed.
"Not just outside the city. If the rumors are true, he went to the Black Zone."
It didn't take long before someone approached Yuan and asked him directly, "Can you tell us what happened out there?"
Yuan replied with a smile, "I just gave my testimony, so you will learn of it soon."
"Can't you just tell us now?"
"I was advised by General Mei not to say anything about it until then," he said, using Mei Feng as a scapegoat.
Sure enough, when the soldier heard Mei Feng's name, he immediately backed down.
And for the rest of Yuan's time in the mission hall, nobody approached him again.
Once he was inside the machine, Yuan tried to join the next Black Zone exam.
However, as he'd anticipated, he needed to first pass the exam for the Purple Zone.
After signing up for the exam, Yuan headed directly to the training area. Of course, he wanted to see how much closer he'd gotten to defeating the entity on the 46th floor.
'I have about three and a half trillion years' worth of Eternal Essence right now. Surely, I should be able to last more than a few minutes against it...'
<Your restriction on Eternal Essence has been temporarily lifted>
"Foolish mortal..."
A familiar voice resounded before the entity attacked, sending a massive wave of Eternal Essence at Yuan.
"After fighting the Void Hunter, you don't seem nearly as powerful as before," Yuan remarked with a faint smile.
He immediately unleashed his Eternal Essence—three trillion years' worth—to meet the incoming attack head-on.
A moment later, their Eternal Essences collided. However, instead of Yuan's being overwhelmed as it had been in the past, the two forces canceled each other out.
Seeing this, Yuan knew he had a good chance of defeating it.
After realizing its attack had failed, the entity immediately prepared another.
"Using the same attack after the last one failed? Who's the fool now?!"
Yuan unleashed as much Eternal Essence as he could muster, condensing it into a massive spear before launching it forward.
The spear tore straight through the incoming wave with ease and continued onward, rapidly closing in on the entity.
However, just as the spear was about to reach its target, the entity suddenly vanished from its spot like a ghost.
'Void Manipulation!'
Yuan immediately shifted his focus toward locating the entity. Unfortunately, his mastery of Void Manipulation was still inferior, making it difficult for him to track its movements through the void.
A second later, a sharp pain suddenly pierced Yuan's chest.
When he looked down, his eyes widened slightly at the sight of a massive hole torn straight through his chest.
<You have died>

"I'd like to turn this in."

The worker accepted the storage cube and placed it on a machine that counted its contents.
"T-Ten thousand Unknown Ores?!" the worker muttered in a surprised voice after seeing the result.
"By the way, is it possible to only accept merits?" Yuan suddenly asked. "I don't need the money."
"Yes, it's possible. Would you like to turn in these Unknown Ores for merits only?"
Yuan confirmed with a nod.
"I understand."

"Can't you just tell us now?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2647 Confirmation
paragraphs: "Y-Yuan?" Mei Xiaoyun muttered with a dazed look on her face as she glared at the figure standing in front of Yuan's living quarters.
She blinked a few times and even rubbed her eyes to make sure she wasn't hallucinating.
A few more moments of silence passed, and Mei Xiaoyun still had trouble believing her eyes.
It wasn't until Yuan spoke aloud that she confirmed he wasn't an illusion but real.

"Mei Xiaoyun? Oh, it's been a whole year since the recruitment, hasn't it? How was boot camp?" Yuan steadily approached her with a calm smile on his handsome face, acting like everything was normal—as if he wasn't supposed to be dead.
"What's with that look on your face? You look like you're seeing a ghost," he remarked with a chuckle.
"Am I not?" she responded with a slight frown. "You're supposed to be dead, after all."
"More like they assumed I was dead. As you can see for yourself, I am very much alive."
Mei Xiaoyun sighed. "Give me a moment."
She then spent the next two minutes repeatedly rubbing her temples and letting out several deep sighs, as though trying to convince herself that Yuan was really standing before her.
"When did you return?" Mei Xiaoyun asked once she was done.
"Today."
"What happened?"
Yuan explained the whole situation to her without hesitation.
"I see... and what are your plans now?"
"I am going to get my permit for the Black Zone and then try to get one for level 2 Black Zone."
"Unbelievable..." Mei Xiaoyun muttered with wide eyes. "I've just finished boot camp, and you're already thinking about going into level 2 Black Zone? Did we really join at the same time?"
"The exam is scheduled in two weeks. You can come watch if you'd like."
"I'll think about it."
"By the way, which division did you join?" Yuan then asked.
"The First Division."
"The same as me, huh? Good to know. Anyway, I'm going to rest now. If you need anything, don't hesitate to knock on my door."
Yuan entered his building the next moment, but Mei Xiaoyun lingered outside for some time, silently staring at his building.
'I can't believe how much his death bothered me...' she sighed inwardly, feeling a little puzzled by her own feelings.
After lingering for a few more moments, Mei Xiaoyun left.
Meanwhile, after returning home, the first thing Yuan did was train his Void Manipulation.
'There's only one method of training that I can think of in this environment...'
After taking a deep breath, Yuan activated Void Manipulation, entering the void.
However, instead of coming out, he remained inside, training directly within the void. Although it was incredibly dangerous, it was also the most effective.
'T-This feeling! It's much more painful than before!'
The pain was so much worse than when he last used this training method, forcing him to emerge from the void mere minutes later.
"What is going on? I could stay in the void for days before, but I can't last even ten minutes right now!"
After resting for a bit, Yuan returned to the void. But instead of enduring the pain, he studied it.
'No wonder it hurts so much more!' Yuan exclaimed inwardly as he quickly realized what was happening.
The pain he felt within the void pierced directly into his soul—a sensation he was all too familiar with, considering he had once shattered his own soul.
"As I thought..." Yuan muttered in a low voice after exiting the void again.
He lowered his head to look at his body.
"This body... is an avatar, composed entirely of my soul."
Yuan had already figured this was the case when his storage rings did not transport to this world with him, but he wasn't a hundred percent certain until this moment.

After all, if he were inhabiting an avatar created from his soul—similar to a player's avatar in Cultivation Online—he should have been able to summon his Soul Weapons. Yet, that wasn't the case here.
Once Yuan realized this, he sat down to ponder what to do with the information.
"Even if I am in an avatar created from my own soul, it doesn't change anything, as I still have no way out of this world."
In the end, his goal to find Gaia hadn't changed in the slightest with this new information.
Thus, he resumed training his Void Manipulation.
Although practicing Void Manipulation with nothing but his soul was far more painful, his progress was also incomparably faster than when he trained it normally.
<Your Void Manipulation mastery has reached a new level>
By the time Yuan was scheduled to take the Purple Zone examination two weeks later, his mastery of Void Manipulation had already advanced by a full level.
When Yuan exited his living quarters, his gaze shifted to look at the four soldiers who had been waiting outside for over a week.
"You know you could've knocked on the door if you wanted to speak with me," Yuan said.
"I told you he was fine," said Shi Fa.
Sergeant Bing and Sergeant Quang approached Yuan together and stopped a few steps away.
Then, without hesitation, they both lowered their heads.
"We're sorry for failing to protect you properly."

"There's no need for either of you to apologize," Yuan said, shaking his head. "Quite frankly, I never needed your protection in the first place. I only went along with it because it gave General Mei some peace of mind."
"As arrogant as ever, huh?" Wu Wang remarked with a smile.
"Where are you heading to now?"
"I'm going to take the exam for the Purple Zone."
"Do you plan on taking the one for the Black Zone?"
"Of course. Right after I pass this one."
"Then I won't bother watching this one since you'll obviously ace it," said Wu Wang.
"I'll go," said Sergeant Bing.
"Me too," said Sergeant Quang.
"I got nothing else to do, anyway," Shi Fa shrugged.
Thus, Yuan made his way to the examination site, which was being held at the same location as his previous examination.
At the same time, the Ironwoman returned to the military base to report the details of her investigation to Mei Feng.

chapters.title: Chapter 2648 Ironwoman's Report
paragraphs: "W-What did you just say?" Mei Feng muttered, staring at the Ironwoman with a dumbfounded expression after hearing the results of her investigation, looking as though she had just been told a horrifying story.

The Ironwoman cleared her throat before repeating, "Apparently, the Ember City has discovered a new Void Specter—one that rivals the Void Hunter in prowess. They also believe that Void Specter was the one fighting the Void Hunter for weeks."
"A Void Specter fighting with the Void Hunter...? That sounds ridiculous," remarked Mei Feng.
"I haven't even told you the best part. According to Ember City, this Void Specter can perfectly disguise itself as a human."
"What sort of nonsense is that?!"
"Moreover..."
"There's more?"
"This humanoid Void Specter currently has the appearance of a soldier from our city."
Mei Feng frowned upon hearing this. "A soldier from our city?"

The implications of a new Void Specter with prowess on par with the Void Hunter were already troubling enough, but the fact that it supposedly bore the appearance of a soldier from Gaia's Heaven made the situation even worse. Once word spreads, it could easily lead to unnecessary suspicion and discrimination against their soldiers.

"What do you think?" Mei Feng asked the Ironwoman a moment later. "Is this information from Ember City trustworthy, or are they using this opportunity to damage our reputation? We've been at odds with each other for generations, after all."
"Personally, I think it's a misunderstanding."
"What makes you think that?"
"Because they said this Void Specter took the appearance of a corporal."
"A corporal?" Mei Feng raised an eyebrow, looking puzzled.
"Think about it. A lone soldier with the rank of corporal in the Black Zone..."
"Corporal Yuan?!" Mei Feng exclaimed in disbelief after realizing this.
The Ironwoman nodded.
"Of course, it could just be a coincidence. We'll know for sure once we speak with him," she said.
After a brief pause, she added, "Speaking of him, any news on his return?"
Mei Feng sat back in her chair and sighed, "He returned to the city two weeks ago."
Mei Feng sat back in her chair and sighed, "He returned to the city two weeks ago."
"Oh? What happened?"
"He gave his testimony and hasn't left his living quarters since then. I'll let you hear the recording of it later.
"And the Scorpion Squad?"

"We were going to interrogate them again with the new information from Corporal Yuan's testimony, but..." Mei Feng paused to rub her temples before continuing, "We could not find them. They've completely vanished into thin air."
The Ironwoman raised an eyebrow at this news.
"That's a funny way to say General Gu got rid of them."
"Even if that's the case, we have no evidence. And quite frankly, I hope that's what happened since it saves us the trouble."
"With the Scorpion Squad gone, wouldn't it be harder to make General Gu pay for his crimes?"
"It's not like he won't have other ways to weasel his way out of trouble. Unless we catch him in the act with irrefutable evidence, there's nothing we can do to him," Mei Feng sighed.
"Well, what are we going to do now? You think he'll continue targeting Corporal Yuan?"
"I don't know, but we'll make it harder for him to target him."
"How?"

"I'm going to promote him. I checked his records last week, and he has more than enough to be promoted to Sergeant. However, he'll need to pass the examination for the Purple Zone before he fully qualifies."
"When's the next examination?"
"Today. In fact, he should be—"
Mei Feng abruptly stopped speaking when she received a call.
"What is it?"
"T-This is about Corporal Yuan!" A frantic voice responded.
"Did something happen to him?" Mei Feng frowned.
"Yes! He just finished the examination for the Purple Zone, and you won't believe the results! A perfect score! He completely aced it!"
"That's hardly surprisingly for someone like—"

"That's not all!" the voice interrupted Mei Feng before continuing, "He asked to take the examination for the Black Zone since he was already there, and the examiners agreed. In the end, he passed with perfect results, too! This is the first time anyone has aced the Black Zone exam!"
Mei Feng became speechless.
After a moment of silence, Mei Feng asked, "Are you at the examination right now?"
"Yes, I am."
"Is Corporal Yuan still there?"
"He left just a few seconds ago.
"Go catch him and tell him to come to my office immediately."
"Right away."
Time passed swiftly, and half an hour later, Yuan showed up at Mei Feng's office.
"You called?" Yuan said aloud as he walked into the room.
"Hm? You're here, too?" he looked at the Ironwoman with a raised eyebrow.
Neither Mei Feng nor the Ironwoman spoke, merely gazing at him in silence.
"What is it?" Yuan asked again.
"First and foremost, congratulations on passing your exams with perfect scores," Mei Feng said a moment later.
"Second, I have a few questions for you regarding your time in the Black Zone."
"What sort of questions?"
"Have you encountered soldiers from the Ember City?"
"Ember City? Never heard of them."
"They wear a red uniform," the Ironwoman said, giving details of their uniform to him.
"Oh, them? In that case, yes, I have," Yuan calmly admitted.
He wasn't sure how they found out, but he had no reason to hide it.
"Is that so..." Mei Feng mumbled, leaning her head back as she rubbed her temples with a weary expression.
"Is this about me killing two of their soldiers?" Yuan asked. "In that case, it was self-defense."
"This is way beyond that," said the Ironwoman, shaking her head.
"For some reason, they seem to think you're a Void Specter."
"Huh?" Yuan's eyes widened slightly at the unexpected accusation.
He had considered many possibilities regarding the situation, but being mistaken for a Void Specter was certainly not one of them.
Then he had a sudden realization.
'It was probably because of my affinity...' he sighed inwardly.
"Well? Are you actually human, or are you a Void Specter disguised as one?" the Ironwoman asked a moment later, a hint of amusement in her voice.

Yuan chuckled at her response before turning to Mei Feng and asking her, "What about you?"
"Something that doesn't belong in this world," she calmly responded.
The Ironwoman was slightly surprised by Mei Feng's response.
"Anyway, I have an idea why they think I am a Void Specter. It's just a misunderstanding," Yuan said a moment later. "Are they making a big deal out of this or something?"
"No... not yet." Mei Feng shook her head. "But it will become an issue once news spreads in the other cities—if it hasn't already."
"Can't you just tell them it was a misunderstanding?" Yuan asked.
"Of course I can. The real question is whether they'll believe us," Mei Feng replied.

After a brief pause, she continued, "That being said, the existence of a humanoid Void Specter is simply too outrageous. Without concrete evidence, I doubt most people will accept that such an entity exists. In fact, they'll probably find it much easier to believe the whole thing was a misunderstanding than to accept that a humanoid Void Specter is real."
"So what you're saying is... to just ignore it?" Yuan asked.
"For now, yes."
The room quickly fell silent afterward.
"Is that all?" Yuan asked a moment later.
"No, we're about to go into the main topic," Mei Feng responded before her expression turned dead serious.
"You... Did you fight the Void Hunter before coming back to the city?" Mei Feng asked with narrowed eyes.
"I did."
Yuan answered immediately and without the slightest hesitation, catching them off guard. They hadn't expected him to admit it so readily.
"What's with the surprised look?" Yuan remarked after seeing their faces.
"Well... I was expecting you to keep it a secret..."
"Why?" Yuan calmly replied. "It wouldn't benefit me to keep it a secret.
In his eyes, the more people who knew about his achievement, the better his reputation would be, which would allow him to progress faster in this world.
However, Mei Feng thought differently.
"Are you thinking that letting the world know you fought—and survived—the Void Hunter would help with your recognition?"
Yuan quietly nodded.
"While I will admit that you will definitely become the most famous individual in the world, it's not necessarily a good thing."
The Ironwoman then said, "Throughout history, only two people have ever fought the Void Hunter and survived. The first was Tian Yuchen, and now, you're the second."

"Tian Yuchen was already a renowned figure before his battle with the Void Hunter, but surviving that encounter propelled his reputation to the very peak of the world. And because he was affiliated with our city, the other eight cities immediately became wary of us and began working together to suppress Gaia's Heaven, fearing that we had grown too powerful."

"In order to prevent a war from breaking out, Tian Yuchen ultimately had no choice but to sever his ties with our city and become an independent figure, unaffiliated with any city, power, or individual."

"You, on the other hand, are practically unknown outside our military. If word gets out that we have someone capable of fighting the Void Hunter and surviving, the other cities will undoubtedly see us as a threat."
Yuan raised an eyebrow at such words and spoke, "Isn't this world supposed to be working together to deal with the threat prophesied by Gaia?"
"If only things were that simple..." Mei Feng sighed. "Unfortunately, not every city believes in Gaia's prophecy. Some even outright reject it, such as Ember City."
"And while we're on the topic, the next drill is scheduled to happen in two months."
"You mean the one where the civilians must go underground?"
"Yes."
"About time," Yuan said. "Anything I should know before that happens?"
"No, you'll be briefed a week before it happens."
"Alright."
"In any case, the fact that you fought and survived the Void Hunter will not leave this room, understand?" Mei Feng said a moment later.
"I do."
"What do you think? About the Void Hunter," the Ironwoman suddenly inquired.
"It's immensely powerful. So much so that I couldn't do anything to it," he admitted.
"Huh? But didn't you fight with it for weeks?"
"I did, but it was toying with me, and it left once it was satisfied. What? Did you think I was secretly as powerful as the Void Hunter? You're giving me too much credit."
The Ironwoman and Mei Feng fell silent with dumbfounded looks on their faces, but it wasn't that they realized Yuan wasn't as powerful as they expected.

"The Void Hunter... toyed with you and left you alive? I have never heard of such a thing before! When the Void Hunter appears, it always tries to kill everyone who summoned it without exception!" said the Ironwoman.
Mei Feng added, "The only time it failed was when Tian Yuchen held it back long enough for everyone to escape safely."
"What about all that blood?" the Ironwoman then asked. "There was so much of it that the place looked like the aftermath of a bloody battle between two massive armies!"
"Oh, that's my blood."
"There's no way!"
"It's a unique trait of my physique."
"And what kind of physique is that?" The Ironwoman narrowed her eyes at him.
"You don't have to answer that," Mei Feng suddenly said, dumbfounded the Ironwoman.
"Huh?"
The Ironwoman stared at Mei Feng with a suspicious gaze, falling silent.
"One more thing before I send you away," Mei Feng said, pretending the previous interaction didn't happen.
She reached into her drawer and retrieved an insignia, then handed it to Yuan.
"Congratulations on your promotion. You're now a Sergeant."
"Oh?" Yuan gladly accepted his new rank.
"Usually, there would be a ceremony for a promotion of your rank, but alas, I don't want you to draw any unnecessary attention."
"That's fine," Yuan said. "In fact, I'd rather not have one if I could choose."

chapters.title: Chapter 2650 Creating His Own Squad
paragraphs: "That's all I have for you for now," Mei Feng said to Yuan shortly after giving him his new insignia.
Once Yuan left the room, the Ironwoman turned to stare at Mei Feng in silence.
"I'm not going to tell you, so don't bother asking," Mei Feng said after a moment of silence, almost as though she could read the Ironwoman's thoughts.
"You don't need to," the Ironwoman replied. "I've already seen his status—his physique, the Inexhaustible Heavenly Refinement."

She paused briefly before continuing, "However, the fact that you don't want him answering my question suggests there's more to it than that. If I had to guess, you altered the information displayed on his status."
"..." Mei Feng remained silent, refusing to confirm or deny it.
"Do you not trust me?" the Ironwoman suddenly asked.
"This is not a trust issue," Mei Feng swiftly responded. "The fewer people know, the better. Just like how I keep my mouth shut about your background, regardless of who asks."
The Ironwoman smiled at her response before replying, "Fair enough."
She turned around and walked to the door, stopping once her hand reached the handle.
"By the way, regarding that thing we talked about before."
"What thing?"
"About having him join my squad."
"Have you decided to let him join, after all?"
"No, it's the opposite," said the Ironwoman as she shook her head.
"Huh?" Mei Feng uttered in a puzzled voice.
The Ironwoman removed her mask to show Mei Feng a stiff smile.
"He's too much for my squad. I think it'd be much better if he made one to lead himself."
"I see..." Mei Feng mumbled, understanding the Ironwoman's reasoning and finding herself in agreement.
"And since he's a Sergeant now, he can form his own squad."
"I have a feeling he'll definitely go that route once he realizes the benefits..." Mei Feng said with a nervous smile.
Meanwhile, Yuan made his way back to his living quarters after leaving Mei Feng's office.
Meanwhile, Yuan made his way back to his living quarters after leaving Mei Feng's office.
"Huh? Your rank... you've been promoted?" Sergeant Quang, who waited for him outside, remarked with a surprised face after seeing his new insignia.
"Yes, it was a sudden promotion, but I'm not complaining."
"How long has it been since you joined the military? A year?"
"Just about."
"And to think it took me fifteen years to reach this rank..." Sergeant Quang sighed aloud.

"What are the benefits of becoming a sergeant?" Yuan then asked. "Even as a corporal, I already had access to missions that were normally restricted to sergeants, so I don't really see what's changed."
"Well... as a sergeant, you can create a squad of your own."
"Hm?" Yuan stopped walking and turned to look at him with one eyebrow raised.
"My own... squad?"

Yuan immediately realized the benefit of having his own squad. With a team of trusted soldiers under his command, he would always have people ready to accompany him on missions outside the city whenever he wanted.
Of course, he'd still rather go out on his own since that was the most convenient for him, but that wasn't possible right now.
"How many members do I need to have a squad of my own?" Yuan then asked.
"Well, you can create your squad at any time, but you won't be officially recognized as one until you have at least four members, so you'll need three other people."
"For the members, is there a rank requirement?"
"No, anyone who finishes boot camp can join a squad."
"I see. Then are you already in a squad? Want to join mine?"
"Unfortunately, I am already in a squad. In fact, you were with us during your first mission," said Sergeant Quang, referring to Sergeant Bing, Wu Wang, and Shi Fa.
"Is that so? Well, if you ever feel like changing squads, you can find me. Let the others know, too."
"Alright."
Once Yuan reached his living quarters, he said to Sergeant Quang, "By the way, there's no need for you to guard me any longer. Tell Sergeant Bing this, too."
"Huh? But General Mei didn't—"
"Because this is my decision. Don't worry, she won't make things difficult for you."
"Alright...
After Yuan entered his living quarters, Sergeant Quang contacted General Mei to tell her the situation.
"Corp—Sergeant Yuan said he no longer needs us to guard him. What should we do?"
"Do as he says. In fact, I was going to relieve you of your guard duties even if he didn't ask."
"I understand."
Sergeant Quang notified Sergeant Bing of the situation afterward.
Time passed swiftly, and in the blink of an eye, another month went by.
During this time, Yuan spent all of his time inside his room training his Void Manipulation.
'I was only able to stay inside the void for a few seconds at first, but after nearly two months of training, I can stay in the void for three days at a time.'
Even though he was still a far cry from his peak, his rate of progress had improved tremendously compared to before.
With a month left before the drill, Yuan decided to challenge the entity on the 46th floor again.
On his way to the training hall, Yuan encountered Mei Xiaoyun, who appeared to be coming out of the building.
"Are you on your way to train?" Mei Xiaoyun asked him.
"Yes."
"Have fun."
Mei Xiaoyun said before continuing to walk away, but she was quickly stopped.
"Wait a second."
Once she stopped, Yuan asked, "Are you in a squad right now?"
"No, but I have had hundreds of requests," she revealed.
"Hundreds of requests...?" Yuan muttered with a somewhat dumbfounded expression.
Now that he thought about it, Yuan realized that he hadn't received a single invitation to join a squad since entering the military despite all of his achievements.
Considering his talent and reputation, it wouldn't have been strange for squads to constantly try recruiting him. Yet, for some reason, not a single one had approached him.
Despite the oddity, Yuan decided not to ponder too much about it and asked Mei Xiaoyun, "Anyway, I plan on creating my own squad and was wondering if you'd like to join it."
